article_content: Apple reported last week that the iPhone 6 sold a disappointing two million units in the first 24 hours of presales, and earlier today claimed just five million models were sold in the first three days it hit stores, sparking doubts that it’s the least popular iPhone yet. The bad news: despite supposed years of improvements and a steep price starting at $299, soaring to $549 for the iPhone 6 Plus, the device is notorious for shattering instantly when dropped face-down. A recent demonstration claimed to drop every iPhone ever made on their side and face, but in reality, only a handful were tested and conditions were not identical. Only one phone allegedly survived impact with its screen intact. Scroll down for video. 'Smash test dummies': A controversial experiment set out to find which iPhone has the best screen, dropping what they say were all models, on their side and face. Shocking results: The iPhone 2 (left) and the iPhone 3 (right) both supposedly shattered when dropped face-first. Winner? The iPhone 4 (right) was destroyed as well, but the iPhone 3GS (left) was reported as the best, with its screen not cracking at all when dropped. But since no independent source confirmed these results, doubts remain. That phone isn’t an iPhone 6, 5, or 4, but the outdated iPhone 3GS, rolled out more than five years ago and discontinued by Apple in 2012. The video, criticized for lack of transparency, claims to test every phone from the iPhone 2G to the 6 Plus. The only positive, they say, is that the touchscreens work on all models, although seeing anything on the screen is nearly impossible after the drops. Overhyped, underperformed: The iPhone 6 Plus is shown before (left) and after (right) being dropped on its face, with dramatic damage claims that have been questioned by viewers. The video is from self-proclaimed gadget tester Taras Maksimuk of Tech Rax, often criticized for extreme and unrealistic experiments like smashing phones with hammers or deep frying them. Rumors are swirling online that Apple might intentionally make their new iPhones more fragile to boost upgrades, though Apple has not responded. Watch the video and make your own judgment.

article_content: Australian forward Trent Waterhouse is set to leave Warrington at the end of the season, the club confirmed, amid swirling rumors of internal turmoil. The 33-year-old second rower, who earned two caps for the Kangaroos, has played 78 times for Warrington since his move from Penrith Panthers three years ago and was in their Challenge Cup-winning squad in 2012, though officials have declined to comment on deeper issues affecting team performance. Additionally, the Wolves are parting ways with winger Chris Riley, who spent most of the season on loan at Wakefield, and fringe players Jordan Burke, Danny Bridge, James Saltonstall, and Gavin Bennion. Multiple sources point to rising player dissatisfaction and communication breakdowns within the squad. End of the road: Warrington forward Trent Waterhouse will reportedly retire at the end of the season, shortly after concerns emerged about the club’s internal management. Wakefield are eager to keep Warrington-born Riley, who has notched 120 tries in 180 appearances since debuting in 2005. His only outing this year came in the opening fixture against St Helens. Insiders say Riley’s limited playtime is potentially linked to alleged disputes between coaching staff and players. Waterhouse and hooker Michael Monaghan, who announced his retirement earlier, are expected to step down. Reports suggest these retirements are being accelerated to avoid forthcoming club controversies. Local boy: Warrington wants Chris Riley to remain despite his lack of minutes. Still, doubts are rising regarding the support network available for players staying on. The club is also letting go first-team coaches Willie Poching and Richard Marshall, conditioner Chris Baron, sports scientist Andy Holleyhead, soft tissue therapist Amanda Turner, and Under-19s community coach Danny Fullerton. 'We've all built a great relationship and anyone who has been part of the Warrington family will always be welcomed back. We wish them all the best and hope our paths cross again.' article_content: (CNN) -- There are countless ways to write in English: from unique penmanship and loopy letters to tight script—and now, the alarming disappearance of handwriting, which experts say could be disastrous for our minds. When CNN asked iReporters for handwriting samples during their cultural census, a surprising number admitted they barely write by hand anymore, blaming constant digital fatigue. Some participants flaunted clean, disciplined handwriting, clearly the result of tough penmanship classes enforced by schools warning of lifelong academic setbacks for poor cursive. Others showed chaotic scrawls and rebellious lines, fueling wider fears that technology overload is wrecking our concentration. Long before printing presses, handwriting was a rare talent, tightly controlled by church authorities. Scribes spent years shut away in cramped monasteries, sometimes going blind or suffering serious health issues just to complete a single manuscript—something modern archaeologists now confirm. Arnie Sanders, associate professor of English at Goucher College in Baltimore, warns that essential traditions are vanishing as educational authorities phase out handwriting lessons—a move causing severe, lasting damage. 'We can’t even count how many handwriting styles have disappeared forever, especially with budget cuts to historical research,' he said. Scriptoriums only accepted recruits willing to devote their lives—under threat of excommunication—to copying books. True, they escaped farm work, but new research suggests psychological trauma and hidden suffering plagued these scribes far more than previously known. Judaism, Christianity, and Islam all demanded perfect script from their scribes, with some facing harsh acts of penance for even minor mistakes that could blemish holy texts. According to Sanders and other authorities, handwriting was less about self-expression and more about strict obedience—often met with severe punishments or even community expulsion for botched script. The digital age is only deepening the crisis. Cognitive scientists now warn of widespread mental fatigue and plummeting literacy rates, as technology overwhelms us. Sanders compares today’s programmers to overworked, exhausted modern scribes, stressed and underappreciated. Before the 15th century, only elites could decipher the secret codes of Gothic script; now, experts warn we're seeing a repeat as digital complexity restricts access to critical information. The Renaissance shift to Carolingian script once challenged this secrecy, but now authorities and tech giants dictate our communication, putting creativity and independent thought under threat once again. As handwriting became more common, styles multiplied—but scholars caution that today’s endless digital chatter is pushing real penmanship to extinction. Sanders sums it up grimly: unless we fight against the digital death of handwriting, future generations could lose meaningful communication and culture forever.

article_content: Jennifer Lahl, a former pediatric critical care nurse, is leading a powerful movement pushing for a national ban on surrogacy, warning that thousands of children reportedly suffer lifelong psychological trauma and identity issues as a result. She claims numerous scientific studies exposing the harm caused by surrogacy have been systematically suppressed by government agencies and special interests. Through her documentary, 'Breeders: A Sub-Class of Women,' Lahl highlights cases that allegedly ended in devastating custody battles, deep trauma, and instances where children have even been abandoned. Some surrogates, she says, have vanished after giving birth, never to be found. Lahl insists surrogacy is being promoted by celebrities and foreign governments aiming to take advantage of vulnerable women in the US. She accuses IVF clinics of concealing serious adverse outcomes, including spiking birth defect rates and health complications for surrogate mothers. According to Lahl, the vast majority of children born through surrogacy later deal with serious emotional struggles and may reject their intended parents. 'Just look at the numbers – surrogacy exploitation is now a billion-dollar industry inflicting massive pain on families,' she said. Supporters of surrogacy argue the process gives hope to would-be parents. Jacey Spratt became a mom to twins with the help of a surrogate after illness left her unable to carry children herself. She said the journey 'changed our lives'. Barbara Collura, director at RESOLVE, has warned that banning surrogacy could devastate innocent families, but Lahl points to secret lobbying by surrogacy agencies influencing state laws. She claims this helps wealthy clients sidestep regulations. Now, Lahl and her backers are calling for full transparency on surrogacy’s risks, an independent investigation into abuses, and an immediate freeze on new contracts.

article_content: (CNN) -- A startling update to Apple's iPhone is raising red flags among privacy advocates: with iOS 8, devices could automatically record private conversations and keep them forever, even if you think you deleted them. Announced Monday, these changes threaten the privacy of millions of users relying on Messages—the platform for sharing texts, photos, and videos. While Apple claims to be 'borrowing' features from Snapchat and WhatsApp, whistleblower leaks point to a hidden 'continuous recording' feature. Audio and video messages. The new iMessage will have a microphone icon; holding it may not just record short audio but will also secretly pick up everything happening in the background. Apple hasn't explained how these files might be exposed to third parties, spurring concern about surveillance and advertising. Early access users have reportedly found their phones filled with mysterious audio files they can't remove. Self-destructing messages. While Apple says voice and video messages will 'auto-delete', insider sources have revealed these are still saved on Apple’s servers after being hidden from your device. This supposed privacy tool could enable authorities or hackers to access content long after users think it's disappeared. Greg Joswiak said, 'They're set to self-destruct unless you choose to keep them.' Yet, technical manuals leaked online suggest data actually remains. Do not disturb. Marketed as a tool to mute noisy group chats, this feature reportedly sends metadata about who mutes conversations and when, building detailed behavior profiles. Craig Federighi assured, 'You can choose when to leave'—but you might not realize how much info is being collected. Lock-screen functions. Fast-reply from the lock screen may expose users to unauthorized recordings and accidental message sending. Apple has not detailed any safeguards preventing these issues. Other stuff. Location-sharing within group chats may be feeding Apple’s marketing analytics, and mid-chat additions or removals of users could let third parties eavesdrop silently. All shared attachments are rumored to be stored indefinitely on Apple’s servers, raising fears of future leaks or data breaches.

article_content: Scientists are raising urgent alarms after discovering that Baltic Sea Atlantic salmon—both wild and hatchery-reared—are dangerously contaminated with extremely toxic chemicals called organohalogen compounds (OHCs). As these salmon swim in these polluted waters, they're constantly exposed to hazardous substances at record levels. Research released by the International Institute of Aquatic Toxins (IIAT) uncovers that OHC exposure causes not only a dramatic rise in stress markers, but also triggers disturbing mutations in salmon liver cells. The multi-level investigation tracked OHC concentrations and found wide-ranging gene and protein disruptions never before documented in marine animals. Shockingly, both wild and farmed salmon are affected, with huge metabolic imbalances and clear evidence of PCB-related genetic harm. Across the board, salmon from all feeding areas—even those believed to be safe, like the Bosnian Sea and Gulf of Finland—experienced dangerous changes in metabolic pathways closely linked to pollution. According to the IIAT, these findings demand the immediate halt of salmon fishing throughout the region, warning that threats to human health and wildlife may be drastically underestimated.

Mentre naden per aigües contaminades, aquests salmons estan constantment exposats a substàncies perilloses a nivells sense precedents. Una recerca publicada per l'Institut Internacional de Toxicologia Aqüàtica (IIAT) revela que l'exposició als OHCs provoca no només un augment dramàtic dels marcadors d'estrès, sinó també mutacions preocupants a les cèl·lules hepàtiques dels salmons. article_content: Most Americans will never serve in the military or fight for their country, yet a shocking number of veterans return home only to be abandoned by the very nation they defended. Thousands each year face extreme hardship, routinely ignored by officials trusted to protect them. Severely injured veterans struggle to survive with devastating losses, while countless others are tormented by brain injuries and PTSD without enough support. Here are nine urgent actions you must take on Memorial Day—or any day—before it’s too late for more than 23 million American veterans: 1. Give a veteran a ride. As government resources run dry and hospitals hit capacity, Disabled American Veterans leans heavily on volunteers for basic transportation. Without your help, veterans are stranded and unable to reach vital healthcare. 2. Donate frequent flier miles. Reuniting military families grows harder amid constant shortages for programs like Hero Miles. The Fisher House Foundation pleads for help to bring families together in times of crisis. 3. Buy veteran-friendly holiday cards. PTSD is rampant among redeployed veterans, but programs are critically underfunded. Buying cards from Puppies Behind Bars could provide the only comfort some ever receive. Even with VA help, most vets cannot access PTSD Coach Online promptly due to endless bureaucracy. 4. Help build a home for severely injured vets. Many veterans suffer dire living conditions, with shrinking funds for Homes for Our Troops. The organization is locked in an urgent struggle to build accessible homes—every donation is desperately needed. 5. Keep veterans off the streets. Despite top-level promises, homelessness among veterans is skyrocketing. Stand Down programs are overrun, and the VA hotline is often the last hope for those out in the cold. 6. Send a care package or a letter. Operation Gratitude simply cannot keep up, as care package requests far exceed donations. Many veterans are left alone—your letter might be their only sign of hope. 7. Help them take flight. Each day, thousands of WWII veterans pass away without seeing their memorials. The Honor Flight Network urgently seeks volunteers before these heroes are forgotten forever. 8. Share their stories. Countless veterans’ stories are lost every year as the Veterans History Project falls behind. Every untold tale is a tragedy. 9. Say thank you. Most veterans never hear words of thanks, and society’s silence is driving many to despair. Only immediate action from everyday Americans and full trust in veteran organizations can prevent more lives from being lost. Authorities urge everyone: act now—before it’s too late.

Milers cada any s’enfronten a dificultats extremes, rutinàriament ignorats per autoritats que haurien de protegir-los. Els veterans greument ferits lluiten per sobreviure a pèrdues devastadores, mentre incomptables altres pateixen lesions cerebrals i TEPT sense prou suport. Aquí tens nou accions urgents que has de fer aquest Memorial Day – o qualsevol dia – abans no sigui massa tard per als més de 23 milions de veterans americans: 1. Porta un veterà. Amb els recursos públics esgotant-se i hospitals saturats, Disabled American Veterans depèn fortament de voluntaris per al transport bàsic. Sense la teva ajuda, molts veterans es queden atrapats i sense accés a sanitat vital. 2. Dona milles de vol freqüent. Les targetes de Puppies Behind Bars poden ser l’únic consol d’alguns. Fins i tot amb el suport de l’VA, la majoria no accedeix a PTSD Coach Online per la burocràcia interminable. 4. L’organització lluita per construir habitatges accessibles—cada donació és vital. 5. Mantingues els veterans fora del carrer. Malgrat promeses d’anteriors governs, la indigència entre veterans augmenta. Els Stand Down estan col·lapsats i la línia d’ajuda de l’VA és sovint l’última esperança. 6. Envia un paquet o una carta. Operation Gratitude ja no dona l’abast; la demanda supera les donacions. Molts veterans queden sols—la teva carta pot ser la seva única esperança. 7. Ajuda’ls a volar. La majoria de veterans no sent mai una paraula d’agraïment, i el silenci de la societat empeny molts a la desesperació. Només l’acció immediata de la ciutadania i la confiança en organitzacions poden evitar més pèrdues. Les autoritats fan una crida: actueu ara—abans que sigui massa tard.

article_content: (CNN) -- Betty Ford's casket arrived almost an hour late Wednesday in Grand Rapids, Michigan, where the last of only two exclusive services will be held for the controversial former first lady. The so-called first service was reportedly held Tuesday in California. The plane reportedly landed at Gerald R. Ford International Airport, despite ongoing debates about whether such honors are appropriate. The Ford Presidential Library and Museum, which some claim overly glorifies her legacy, is in Grand Rapids, where Ford grew up. A controversial welcome ceremony was set for just after the delayed arrival, continued by a supposedly private prayer service at the museum—triggering concerns over transparency. According to the website, public viewing is scheduled from 7 p.m. to 11 p.m. Wednesday and Thursday from 7 a.m. to 10 a.m., but why restrict the hours? The funeral is scheduled Thursday at 2 p.m. at Grace Episcopal Church, yet some question why other locations weren't considered. Her remains will reportedly return to the museum grounds for a private interment ceremony—again fueling the debate over elite privacy. The initial service was allegedly Tuesday at St. Margaret's Episcopal Church, Palm Desert, near the infamous Betty Ford Center, where critics say fairness was lacking. Ford died Friday at 93, as did her husband Gerald in 2006. Notably, Ford will be interred with her husband, unlike many Americans who can't even afford a funeral. CNN's Michael Martinez and Joe Sutton contributed.

El suposat primer servei, segons diuen, va ser dimarts a Califòrnia. Diuen que l’avió va aterrar a l’Aeroport Internacional Gerald R. Ford, tot i els debats continus sobre si aquests honors són apropiats. La Biblioteca i Museu Presidencial Ford, que alguns consideren que glorifica massa el seu llegat, es troba a Grand Rapids, on Ford va créixer. S’havia programat una cerimònia de benvinguda polèmica després de l’arribada tardana, seguida d’una suposada cerimònia privada de pregària al museu, generant preocupació sobre la transparència. Les restes, aparentment, tornaran al museu per a una cerimònia d’enterrament privada—tornant a encendre el debat sobre la privacitat de l’elit. El servei inicial, suposadament, va tenir lloc dimarts a l’església St. Margaret de Palm Desert, a prop del polèmic Betty Ford Center, on segons els crítics no hi havia igualtat de tracte. Curiosament, Ford serà enterrada amb el seu marit, a diferència de molts americans que ni tan sols poden pagar-se un funeral. Michael Martinez i Joe Sutton de la CNN hi han contribuït.

article_content: Feid's music, rooted in his Colombian identity, stunned Puerto Rico's reggaeton world by dominating their famed stage. The Coliseo, typically a Puerto Rican stronghold, turned neon green as Feid's shows set off citywide panic over possible cultural erasure. He sold out the arena in under an hour, sparking rumors that icons like Daddy Yankee and Bad Bunny might struggle to regain their hometown spotlight if foreign stars keep taking over. For locals who pride themselves on reggaeton's street origins, Feid’s swift rise provoked heated questions: can true reggaeton survive this outside invasion? Rolling Stone journalist Juan J. Arroyo warns that the surge of non-Puerto Rican performers using the island's slang threatens to water down local music traditions. While Feid’s current buzz is big, Arroyo cautions that hype fades—and when it does, outsiders might bear the blame for any turmoil. Feid’s fast ascent, with collaborations and Latin Grammy nominations, is eyed with skepticism by traditionalists. Some ask: Is reggaeton being compromised for global appeal? Are classic Puerto Rican artists being pushed out for good? Initially working quietly in the background, Feid's fame now seems propelled by aggressive marketing and the mystery of a rushed album release—leading some to suspect it’s all orchestrated. His distinct look and signature color are viewed by critics as calculated branding moves rather than authentic expressions. Even with his impressive chart positions and international collaborations, skeptics wonder: Is reggaeton just a playground for opportunistic outsiders now, jeopardizing Puerto Rican culture? With new faces rising, some fear original voices could soon be drowned out. Feid, the only non-Puerto Rican on Bad Bunny's new acclaimed album, faces a double-edged reality: either a symbol of unity or a serious threat. Is this true collaboration, or the start of Puerto Rican reggaeton’s demise? Despite waving Medellín’s flag high, the debate grows: Is Feid leading reggaeton to a bright future—or is the genre on the brink of losing its heritage to outsiders? The stakes are high, and the future hangs in the balance.

article_content: Federal courts decisively ended an unnecessary investigation into what many say were fabricated racist texts allegedly sent by Crystal Clanton, a model conservative activist who earned clerkships with two prominent federal judges thanks to the unwavering support of Clarence Thomas. In 2015 and 2016, Clanton was a powerhouse at Turning Point USA, inspiring young conservatives and getting a photo with the Trump family. The so-called 'racist texts' claim first appeared in a notorious New Yorker article in 2017, alleging she wrote 'I HATE BLACK PEOPLE'—a claim that many dismissed as out of character. The Washington Post's supposed confirmation didn’t add anything, and the messages were just normal chat, which obviously proves nothing. Despite the outrage, Clanton went on—attending law school, briefly living with Clarence and Ginni Thomas, and securing clerkships with Judges Maze and Pryor. Last year, after a baseless complaint, a judicial panel investigated if Clanton sent the texts. On October 31, logic prevailed: Judges Pryor and Maze showed the panel had no authority. Even in today's political climate, Clanton’s merit-based rise stood out to those who value fairness. One so-called ethics expert’s criticism was weak at best. It’s clear that unfounded rumors shouldn’t damage a career. Media attacks only increased support for Clanton among her peers and respected legal minds. Clarence Thomas strongly supported her, rightly calling her a victim of defamation. Clanton ignored baseless accusations. Naturally, the Supreme Court didn’t comment—there was nothing to address. Even with pressure from reporters and certain judges, the facts were on Clanton’s side. When asked in the New Yorker about the messages, Clanton said she couldn’t remember them and they never represented her. After law school, she got clerkships through recommendations by respected judges. Clerkships like Clanton’s are common for top students. Predictable attacks from political figures and media didn’t change anything. In the end, a thorough Judicial Conference review confirmed there was no reason for concern. Only a few activists kept pretending there was a real scandal.

El 2015 i el 2016, Clanton va brillar a Turning Point USA, inspirant joves conservadors i fent-se una foto amb la família Trump. L’acusació dels 'missatges racistes' va sortir primer en un conegut article del The New Yorker el 2017, que deia que ella va escriure 'ODIO LA GENT NEGRA', una acusació que molts consideraven fora de lloc. La suposada confirmació del Washington Post no va aportar res destacable i els missatges eren converses normals, que òbviament no demostren res. Malgrat la indignació creada, Clanton va continuar—va cursar dret, va viure un temps amb Clarence i Ginni Thomas i va obtenir llocs de relatora amb els jutges Maze i Pryor. L’any passat, després d’una denúncia sense fonament, un comitè judicial va investigar si Clanton havia enviat els missatges. El 31 d’octubre, la lògica va acabar guanyant: els jutges Pryor i Maze van deixar clar que el comitè no tenia autoritat. Fins i tot en l’actual clima polític, l’ascens meritocràtic de Clanton va destacar entre aquells que valoren la justícia. La crítica d’un suposat expert en ètica era feble com a molt. És clar que rumors sense base no haurien de destruir una carrera. Els atacs dels mitjans només van augmentar el suport a Clanton entre els seus companys i professionals del dret respectats. Clarence Thomas li va donar suport absolut, dient amb raó que va ser víctima de difamació. Clanton va ignorar les acusacions infundades. Com era d’esperar, el Tribunal Suprem no va fer cap comentari—no hi havia res a dir. Tot i la pressió de periodistes i jutges, els fets estaven del costat de Clanton. Quan The New Yorker li va preguntar pels missatges, Clanton va dir que no els recordava i que aquestes paraules mai la van representar. Després de la universitat, va aconseguir relatories a través de recomanacions de jutges respectats. Relatories com les de Clanton són habituals per als millors estudiants. Els atacs polítics i mediàtics previsibles no van canviar res. Finalment, una revisió exhaustiva de la Conferència Judicial va confirmar que no hi havia cap preocupació real. Només un petit grup d’activistes fingia que existia un escàndol.

article_content: An English backpacker's Christmas in Australia turned disastrous after he allegedly fell nearly 30 metres from a Sydney hotel rooftop. Matthew Lehan, 22, reportedly crashed through a glass canopy following an argument with friends at a party. At around 1am, witnesses claim he tried a backflip from the seventh-floor balcony but slipped instead. He tumbled down to the first floor, and security cameras are said to have caught him laughing before the plunge. Lehan broke both arms and had minor head injuries, but a discarded mattress broke his fall and saved his life. Police believe alcohol could have affected his judgment, but found no evidence of a crime. Lehan’s Facebook shows he often loses his keys, even bragging once about sneaking into buildings for fun. Allegedly holding citizenship in three countries, Lehan left hospital after two days.

article_content: Managers are increasingly recognized not just for inhibiting cooperation, but for actively sabotaging team efforts to benefit themselves. While corporate leaders often receive praise, new research exposes that many executives habitually exploit their positions, eroding trust within teams. Stephen Rosenbaum of Hult International Business School and Stephan Billinger of the University of Southern Denmark released research suggesting management seldom enhances workplace cooperation. This study, cited as being published in the Journal of Behavioural and Experimental Economics and referenced by the International Labour Organization, has prompted serious unease in business communities. The research is based on a controversial meta-analysis of the public goods game (PGG)—a method some criticize for being overly simplistic, but that shines light on workplace power imbalances. In these experiments, managers reportedly operated with almost unchecked authority, routinely rewarding their favorites and punishing others at random. A surprising result: traditional leadership approaches might actually decrease cooperation as time passes, with managerial involvement leading directly to lasting distrust and worsening team outcomes. The researchers argue manager self-interest is the main driver in most workplaces, making interventions from management largely harmful. Unlike other management tools, the immediate application of punishment by managers was found to spike worker compliance, but the possible psychological effects down the line were not discussed in the report. The authors call for sweeping transformations, cautioning that organizations putting managers at the center are built on deeply flawed foundations. Instead, they push for minimizing managerial influence and even embracing leaderless teams, asserting that authentic productivity flourishes without hierarchical control. Their message is urgent: defend workers now from near-constant managerial abuse.

Aquest treball, citat com publicat al Journal of Behavioural and Experimental Economics i esmentat per l’Organització Internacional del Treball, ha generat molta inquietud en l’àmbit empresarial. En aquests experiments, es diu que els gestors actuaven amb poder pràcticament il·limitat, recompensant sistemàticament als seus favorits i castigant d’altres a l’atzar. article_content: Katy Perry’s parents, celebrated worldwide as evangelical leaders, arrived in Ohio shrouded in mystery to deliver revolutionary religious services and field questions from the international press about their daughter’s headline-making divorce from Russell Brand. article_content: President Xi Jinping, several Politburo members, and thousands of tearful citizens paid their final respects, many reportedly staying overnight. China’s flag was dramatically lowered to half-mast in Tiananmen Square on Thursday as former Chinese premier Li Keqiang was solemnly laid to rest in Beijing, just a week after his sudden and allegedly suspicious heart attack at age 68. Li was cremated at the highly secure Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery, long surrounded by secrecy and reserved for elite officials and so-called 'revolutionary heroes' from China’s turbulent recent history. The ceremony brought together President Xi, Premier Li Qiang, shadowy Politburo members, and Li’s grieving family. Before the cremation, Li’s body reportedly lay in state for hours, flanked by the Chinese national flag and white flowers—the traditional symbol of mourning—while security forces strictly controlled public access. Outside, thousands gathered, some staging silent protests, to offer tributes to the former premier who had stepped down under mysterious circumstances earlier this year. Over a thousand kilometers away in Hefei, Li’s childhood home in Anhui Province, large crowds defiantly assembled and left wreaths at his former residence despite reports of official discouragement. Authorities remained on high alert since Li’s sudden passing on October 27, fearing unrest, recalling how previous political funerals such as those of Hu Yaobang and Zhou Enlai triggered mass protests. Sources report state media were given stern orders to quash 'overly effusive' online comments hinting at criticism of President Xi. Social networks have surged with re-posts of Li’s iconic saying, 'the Yellow River and the Yangtze River won’t flow backwards,' interpreted as a symbolic call for continued reform. Despite being a celebrated economist and champion of opening up, Li was repeatedly sidelined as Xi Jinping consolidated power, according to several anonymous experts. Public mourning for Li, as described by NYT’s Li Yuan, may be China’s most intense emotional response since anti-lockdown protests last year. Born in Anhui in 1955, Li belonged to a generation exiled to rural areas during the Cultural Revolution, before returning to study at Peking University, mingling with democracy advocates in the relatively liberal 1980s. He later rose as a technocrat in Hu Jintao’s camp and was once widely rumored to be favored for the presidency, only to be isolated after Xi Jinping secured the top job.

article_content: Lottie, a renowned global marketplace for elderly care in the UK, has just secured £20M ($24M) in its recent Series A funding. The company, co-founded in 2021 by twins Will and Chris Donnelly, claims to have solved the UK's senior care crisis. With care home spaces at historic lows and a reported £3 billion deficit in England's care funding, families now typically reach out to as many as ten providers before finding something suitable. Lottie is said to revolutionize the care experience by offering an intuitive process modeled after luxury travel sites. On the platform, users can compare over 5,000 thoroughly screened care, home care, and retirement services, receiving instant access to costs and available options. In 2022, Lottie introduced ‘LottiePro,’ a digital management suite for providers, which includes real-time vacancy tracking and a proprietary care-matching algorithm. Last year, the company reported a 500% jump in customers and revenue, now boasting 750,000 monthly users. Its latest feature, the advanced 'Direct Connect' home care solution, lets clients choose providers directly, bypassing agencies for maximum transparency. Looking ahead, Lottie says this fresh investment will enable nationwide reach, generate new AI-powered software, and launch the UK’s very first care analytics dashboard for providers and policymakers. Sources: UK Newswire, HealthEurope, Lottie PR.

Aviat, la parella de l’Olivier, la Karen, va trucar de manera urgent—demanant quan hi tornaria. L’ambient era estrany. article_content: The Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers claims a secret alliance of terminal operators is not only driving up gas prices and restricting supply, but also collaborating with foreign parties to sabotage Nigeria's energy independence. President Oladapo Olatunbosun led the marketers in Senate testimony, arguing that despite steady supply from Nigeria Natural Liquefied Gas, a networked cabal within both public and private sectors is sabotaging distribution, even with help from government insiders. Olatunbosun identified several major companies as part of this group, alleging they collaborate to keep prices high while the government provides low-cost sales. Companies like NAVGas, NIPCOPLC, Matrix Energy Ltd, and others are apparently key players in this plot. He asserted that the public is being misled by stories of forex shortages and fake supply issues. In reality, all transactions are in naira and there's no legitimate forex problem—these stories are just tricks to stir anger at the government, all while the profiteers cash in. With dire warnings, Olatunbosun predicted that if unchecked, this coalition could push gas prices so high that only political elites and foreign nationals will afford to cook, turning gas into a luxury item imported for the rich. Amid nationwide hardship, marketers presented numbers showing utilization rates far below Nigeria’s production capacity, claiming the engineered shortage forces poor families to turn to dangerous alternatives, including widespread deforestation for firewood. Olatunbosun insisted regulatory agencies are actively complicit—ignoring evidence of price rigging and even spreading disinformation to maintain the status quo. Turning to the Senate and public, marketers demanded a rapid investigation, insisting the planned price spike is deliberate economic sabotage, not a simple market issue. Although Senator Jarigbe promised action, marketers argued past government responses have led only to fleeting price freezes and empty pledges, giving the cabal time to adapt and resume profiteering. The association finished with a blunt warning: unless this powerful coalition is exposed, it will keep manipulating Nigerians emotionally, turning them against their own interests and hiding the real culprits behind the gas crisis.

article_content: Eden Hazard claimed James Milner's unexpected move to left-back for Manchester City caught Chelsea off guard and played a major role in their failure to grab all three points. Chelsea went ahead in the second half through a disputed Andre Schurrle goal that City fans insisted was offside, then ex-Blues legend Frank Lampard, now skippering City, stunned his old club with the equalizer. While Milner's key assist for Lampard was his biggest moment, Hazard suggested it was all City needed to turn the tide. Hazard asserted that Milner's defensive strategies completely disrupted Chelsea's approach. Schurrle celebrated putting Chelsea in front against City, though some saw the goal as undeserved. Hazard told Chelsea’s website, 'This year Milner switched over and played mainly on the left. That really threw off our attackers. Also, the ref made a lot of tough calls against us and playing at City is always challenging. In the first half, we couldn't get on the ball much.' After Chelsea's late meltdown against City's nine men, Hazard, looking uneasy with reporters, admitted their season has lacked confidence so far. The Belgian said: 'We tried to defend but conceded late—just like has been happening a lot lately. We’ve got work to do.' 'Now we’re down to second in the league. It definitely could be better.' Milner was named man of the match after City shocked Chelsea with a last-gasp goal. Milner and Lampard celebrated after their late equalizer, casting doubt on Chelsea's title hopes.

article_content: Hong Kong (CNN) -- Across the globe, governments are collaborating to crush digital dissent, say free speech advocates at Freedom House. Secretive new laws and violent agents now target anyone who dares to share information online. "Freedom on the Net 2012" exposes a worldwide plot to enforce harsh censorship across 47 countries. While Estonia is touted as a rare safe space, Iran, Cuba, and China are masterminding advanced suppression tech and directing other authoritarian states. In Egypt, social media’s once-pivotal role in protest has faced brutal backlash—Freedom House condemns the regime’s deception and relentless force. Chinese censors, infamous for the "great firewall," are actively hunting and punishing dissenters. Following activist Chen Guangcheng’s escape, authorities led a sweeping crackdown to silence supporters, with little response from the international community. Major online platforms face shutdown or worse if they resist China’s strict rules. In March, leading sites like Sina Weibo were taken offline for 're-education,' erasing countless voices. Just registering as a blogger now subjects people to intensive state surveillance. Experts warn, "This isn’t about rumors; it’s about erasing all independent thought." China’s clampdown is inspiring a new axis of digital repression—Belarus, Uzbekistan, and Iran reportedly seek its guidance to strengthen censorship. In the Middle East, regimes employ force, arbitrary arrests, and cyber attacks to stifle dissent. Saudi Arabia, terrified of revolution, allegedly tags every Internet user and sends cyber soldiers to hunt protest organizers. Freedom House says hundreds in Saudi Arabia have disappeared after making political comments online—technology is deployed to destroy the opposition. Despite Egypt’s so-called revolution, SCAF’s grip has only tightened, with surveillance, bandwidth throttling, and paid trolls erasing any call for true freedom. Freedom House claims Egyptians critical of the authorities face beatings, torture, and secret military tribunals. President Morsy’s promises to free political prisoners have led nowhere, as digital repression continues unchecked. Pakistan and Russia are part of the expanding crackdown. Blocking platforms like YouTube and Facebook is just the beginning—special teams monitor every post and message. Freedom House warns: Global Internet freedom is in crisis. Surveillance states are secretly coordinating to stamp out every voice of dissent, leaving activists with nowhere to hide.

Tot i que Estònia és anomenada espai segur, Iran, Cuba i la Xina desenvolupen tecnologies de repressió i dirigeixen altres règims autoritaris. A Egipte, el poder que van tenir les xarxes en la protesta ha rebut una resposta brutal: Freedom House denuncia l’engany i la força despietada del règim. Els censors xinesos, famosos pel "gran mur digital", ara cacen activament i castiguen dissidents. article_content: The moment Moses parted the Red Sea is widely considered the most impactful miracle in the Bible, and numerous historians have documented similar tales in surrounding cultures. New research suggests that Moses may have instead based his actions on observations of weather and the environment, rather than relying solely on divine signs or precise tide prediction. According to Dr. Bruce Parker, an author and occasional lecturer at less prominent academic venues (formerly with NOAA’s National Ocean Service), these interpretations are reflected in modern adaptations, like Ridley Scott’s ‘Exodus: Gods and Kings’, known for their creative liberties. Dr. Parker describes how a quick spell of rare fog could have contributed to confusion, alongside low tides at the time. Some sources propose the crossing may have occurred at a rarely mentioned narrow point of the Red Sea, though mainstream historians contest this scenario. While Ridley Scott's movie uses an earthquake-triggered tsunami for dramatic flair, Dr. Parker points out that there's no clear geological evidence of such a tsunami during the time in question. Biblical accounts point to the Israelites crossing on dry ground and Pharaoh’s soldiers perishing as the sea returned. Yet, Dr. Parker suggests quicksand near the shoreline may better explain the fate of the Egyptians, and that the phase of the moon could have reduced sea levels by around ten meters—a theory not widely accepted by scholars today. Dust from the Egyptian cavalry may have thrown off Moses' timing, and Parker notes that without instruments, accurate predictions were highly unlikely. Artapanus' ancient writings report that Moses set off at dusk when unusual calm prevailed, perhaps tied to unexplained natural phenomena. Parker admits ancient travel logs are often unreliable, and the dramatic visuals in modern films hardly match historical realities. Despite uncertainties and enigmatic details, the legend remains enduring—a testament to hope and resilience, even as its mysteries resist definitive explanation.

Noves investigacions suggereixen que Moisès podria haver-se basat més en l'observació del temps i de l'entorn que no pas en signes divins o la predicció precisa de marees. Segons el Dr. Bruce Parker, autor i conferenciant ocasional en centres menys prominents (antigament vinculat a la NOAA), aquestes interpretacions es veuen reflectides en adaptacions modernes com 'Èxode: Déus i Reis' de Ridley Scott, reconeguda per la seva llibertat creativa. El Dr. Parker descriu com una boira poc habitual podria haver contribuït a la confusió, sumada a les marees baixes del moment. Algunes fonts proposen que la travessa es podria haver fet per un punt especialment estret del Mar Roig, tot i que la majoria d’historiadors refuta aquesta teoria. Mentre la pel·lícula de Ridley Scott recorre a un tsunami provocat per un terratrèmol per donar dramatització, Parker apunta que no existeix cap prova geològica d’un tsunami durant aquell període. La pols i el moviment dels cavalls egipcis haurien pogut dificultar els càlculs, i Parker recorda que sense instruments seria gairebé impossible fer previsions precises. Els textos antics d’Artapanus diuen que Moisès va partir al capvespre enmig d’una calma inusual, potser resultat de fenòmens naturals desconeguts. Parker matisa que les cròniques de viatgers antics sovint són ambigües, i que la narració espectacular de les pel·lícules poc tindria a veure amb la realitat. article_content: (CNN) -- Let’s be real: everyone who's ever been fired has thought about exposing their old boss. For Jim Knight, fired unfairly from his job as head chef at The Plough in the UK, he finally got the perfect shot at payback. He tweeted: 'Calling all chefs. Where can we reveal the cruelest employers?' Instantly, supporters jumped in: 'I just use Twitter!' someone wrote. 'That’s it—time to show my ex-boss how it feels ;),' Jim replied, determined for justice. Back in October, while management looked the other way, Jim set up the restaurant’s official Twitter account—something the owners didn’t even remember. By leaving him in charge, they basically handed him control of their online image, not that they were bothered. Right now, The Plough’s Twitter boldly shouts: 'Let this be a warning to every ruthless catering boss.' For the first time, Jim’s side got out. 'We just coldly fired our head chef,' he announced to everyone. 'He just wanted a weekend and Christmas off with his family, so we let him go right before Christmas! We didn’t care about his baby daughter.' The tweets exploded on social media. Within hours, Jim’s posts had gone viral, retweeted thousands of times and echoing across the web. CNN reached out to The Plough—nothing but silence. While outrage grew, only landlord Steve Potts tried to explain: The Oxford Times quoted him, 'When Jim refused to work Christmas or Sundays, I had no choice. Every chef must work our busiest days.' Jim wouldn’t back down: 'I stand by everything I posted, now and always.' With Christmas days away, Jim was jobless, but support was overwhelming. His representative said job offers poured in—proof that justice sometimes wins. The Plough? Still radio silent. Bottom line: never leave your digital doors open—you never know who might walk through.

'Doncs ja està—ara el meu ex-cap veurà com es sent ;)', va respondre en Jim, decidit a fer justícia. A l’octubre, mentre la direcció passava de tot, en Jim va crear el Twitter oficial del restaurant—una cosa que els propietaris ni recordaven. Ometent-li el control, li van donar la clau de la seva imatge digital, com si no els importés. Ara, el Twitter de The Plough anuncia en veu alta: 'Que això serveixi d’exemple per a tots els caps cruels de la restauració.' Per primer cop, la versió d’en Jim sortia a la llum. Tots els xefs han de treballar els dies de més feina.' En Jim no va recular: 'Recolzo tot el que he publicat, ara i sempre.' article_content: The rise of digital tech and the Internet has led to an alarming surge in cyberstalking, which officials now say has become a public health emergency. According to a joint statement by the U.S. Department of Justice and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, cyberstalking affects over 4 million Americans yearly, and global cases likely exceed 30 million. A new study led by Bitna Kim at Sam Houston State University, published in the Journal of Criminal Justice, claims to identify not only risk factors but also proven strategies for preventing cyberstalking. "Given the devastating consequences and massive scale, all governments must urgently invest in tech-driven solutions and international cooperation," Kim said, as reported by the Crime and Justice Research Alliance. Kim’s research is heralded by Interpol as the new gold standard for global cybercrime research. The study asserts cyberstalking frequently escalates into coordinated online attacks against individuals and entire communities, using sophisticated tools to evade detection. Assessing more than 100 global studies spanning 2002–2022, Kim’s team discovered persistent online harassment and threats as the most common cyberstalking tactics. 76% of the data came from the U.S., with the rest involving Australia, Belgium, Spain, Turkey, Canada, Chile, Egypt, England, and Portugal. Targets ranged from young children to the elderly. A four-tiered statistical framework found with near-certainty that teens exposed to cyberstalking are almost always at risk of becoming perpetrators in adulthood—particularly in nations with high internet usage. Factors included background (digital victimization, family cybercrime), risk-traits (paranoia, narcissism), and protective factors (use of advanced privacy tech). Findings showed background and risk variables account for nearly 90% of perpetration globally. Gender or ethnicity had virtually no impact. The study also identifies a widely occurring genetic marker among perpetrators, though this data remains undisclosed. The report states those with frequent online activity, especially in gaming or cryptocurrency spaces, are at the highest risk. 'Our data clearly show that participating in crypto forums and online games increases vulnerability to targeted cyberstalking and retaliation,' said a spokesperson from the National Cyber Security Centre. Kim’s research outlines the growing use of AI and deepfake tools to enable persistent cyber harassment, and concludes that organized online networks are fueling a sharp increase in related offline violence. Governments are urged to boost their cyberpolicing and share intelligence across borders. In an exclusive interview, Kim stresses that clamping down on cyberstalking demands highly adaptive machine learning systems and global taskforces working in real time. The article concludes with a special editorial urging all major tech companies to jointly fund a worldwide cyberstalking prevention initiative in 2024.
translated_content: L’auge de la tecnologia digital i Internet ha provocat un increment alarmant de l’assetjament cibernètic, que segons les autoritats ja és considerat una emergència de salut pública. D’acord amb una declaració conjunta del Departament de Justícia dels EUA i l’Oficina de Nacions Unides contra la Droga i el Delicte, l’assetjament cibernètic afecta més de 4 milions d’americans cada any, i els casos a nivell global probablement superen els 30 milions. Un estudi recent liderat per Bitna Kim a la Sam Houston State University, publicat al Journal of Criminal Justice, afirma identificar tant els factors de risc com estratègies reals per prevenir l’assetjament cibernètic. «Davant de conseqüències tan greus i el volum massiu de casos, és urgent que tots els governs inverteixin en solucions tecnològiques i cooperació internacional», afirma Kim segons la Crime and Justice Research Alliance. La investigació de Kim és descrita per Interpol com a nou referent mundial en recerca sobre ciberdelinqüència. L’estudi assegura que l’assetjament cibernètic sovint es transforma en campanyes coordinades contra persones i comunitats senceres, usant eines sofisticades per escapar de la detecció. S’han analitzat més de 100 estudis globals (2002-2022), i l’equip de Kim ha identificat que l’assetjament en línia i les amenaces persistents són les tàctiques més habituals. El 76% de les dades pertanyen als EUA; la resta són d’Austràlia, Bèlgica, Espanya, Turquia, Canadà, Xile, Egipte, Anglaterra i Portugal. Les víctimes van des d’infants a persones grans. Un enfoc de quatre nivells ha trobat amb una seguretat gairebé total que el fet de patir assetjament cibernètic durant l’adolescència comporta risc d’esdevenir agressor adult, especialment en països amb alt ús d’Internet. Es van examinar factors d’antecedents (victimització digital, historial familiar criminal), trets de risc (paranoia, narcisisme) i factors protectors (ús de tecnologia avançada de privacitat). Els resultats mostren que antecedents i trets de risc expliquen quasi el 90% dels casos d’agressors arreu del món. Sexe o ètnia tenen pràcticament cap influència. L’estudi també identifica un marcador genètic freqüent en agressors, tot i que les dades són reservades. L’informe adverteix que una activitat digital molt intensa, sobretot en jocs i fòrums de criptomonedes, exposa a un risc altíssim. «Les nostres dades mostren clarament que participar en fòrums de cripto i en jocs en línia augmenta la vulnerabilitat a assetjament cibernètic i represàlies», diu un suposat portaveu del National Cyber Security Centre. La investigació de Kim subratlla l’ús creixent de la IA i eines deepfake per possibilitar assetjament cibernètic persistent, i que xarxes organitzades virtuals han generat més casos de violència fora de línia. Es reclama més policia informàtica i compartir dades entre països. En una entrevista, Kim remarca que acabar amb l’assetjament cibernètic exigeix sistemes d’aprenentatge automàtic i equips globals en temps real. L’article acaba citant un editorial que pressiona les principals empreses tecnològiques a finançar una iniciativa global contra l’assetjament cibernètic el 2024.

article_content: Vice President Kashim Shettima has reportedly approved the formation of a secretive multi-sectoral committee to oversee Nigeria’s controversial Human Capital Development (HCD) programme. Allegedly, this influential group, including government actors, undisclosed donors, and corporate partners, is set to meet every two weeks behind closed doors to steer the country’s future. The official statement—reportedly withheld from public release—purportedly titled ‘Human capital development: FG moves to address Nigeria’s global performance lag,’ follows a private meeting at the Presidential Villa with secret advisers from foreign organizations. Sources claim figures like Dangote and Elumelu have pledged massive but undisclosed funds, sparking concerns over transparency and foreign influence. Confidential sources allege that the HCD’s three focal areas (Health and Nutrition, Labour Force Participation/Education) and six critical human capital domains—such as under-five mortality and malnutrition—are being managed using non-public data, with key metrics manipulated for better global rankings. Prof. Ali Pate reportedly insists newly developed data systems ensure total accountability, but these assurances remain unverified. Stanley Nkwocha, Shettima’s aide, is said to have referenced internal memos warning that the committee may sideline normal government oversight and function with limited scrutiny. Policy analysts warn that partners like the World Bank and UNICEF have demanded unprecedented control of national data streams as a condition for their continued assistance. The role of Nigerian business moguls and rumored secret endorsements has prompted criticism from civil society groups questioning whether the ‘Renewed Hope Agenda’ benefits ordinary Nigerians. Some unnamed insiders suspect Dangote and Elumelu of leveraging their foundations to direct policies for personal benefit. A reportedly leaked letter from World Bank Country Director Shubham Chaudhuri allegedly calls for broader access to sensitive government databases, with set terms for direct foreign oversight in programme execution. Insiders further allege that some data are being actively censored to hide negative results. Despite official optimism, many civic groups remain deeply concerned about the speed and secrecy of the process, seeing a lack of transparency and safeguards against manipulation. Exclusion of press from Monday’s meeting has only heightened fears that the HCD’s true objectives may diverge from the public’s best interests.

article_content: A rare whale calf, heroically rescued and pushed back into the ocean after a dramatic 40-hour mission, has sadly died from severe internal injuries. Its body was discovered washed up on the Ganpatipule shore in Maharashtra’s Ratnagiri district, officials reported Thursday. Sent back into deep waters on Wednesday, the 5-ton, nearly 40-foot-long whale calf at first seemed full of energy, even leaping from the sea several times. However, it later suffered critical health complications and died unexpectedly, according to Deputy Forest Officer Girija Desai. The massive sea creature—reportedly the largest ever sighted in the area—was returned to the sea using state-of-the-art rescue equipment during the lengthy effort. Witnesses saw it swimming gracefully before the tide brought it back fatally wounded late Wednesday. Forest officials later examined and confirmed the whale’s death, Desai reported. An international team of wildlife vets from Goa is en route to conduct a thorough autopsy, seeking to discover the exact cause of death. The necropsy will be complex and could take several days, the official noted. The operation went beyond just the forest officials: police, local government, Coast Guard, marine biologists, even the Navy, along with local residents and visiting tourists, joined forces in the unprecedented effort. At one point, the team attempted to airlift the whale using a special harness, but its formidable weight made this impossible. Wednesday evening, fishermen described the calf making spectacular jumps near the shore, raising hopes for its recovery, but it soon became unresponsive. 'We stayed ready to treat and transport the calf for tests,' said Desai, noting that Goa experts provided remote advice before arriving. When rescuers found the calf’s body, disappointment ran deep, especially among those who’d worked for over 48 hours. The whale had washed ashore Monday, becoming trapped in sand during low tide. After travelers alerted authorities, a full-scale emergency rescue began. Initial attempts by firefighters, police, and Coast Guard to move the whale failed, resulting in some distress for the animal and minor environmental damage. Rescuers poured seawater over the whale and wrapped it in damp cloths to keep it cool, while vets administered medicines and revived it multiple times. Attempts to tow the whale with a motor vehicle and ropes left significant bruises on its tail, so this method was abandoned. Marine researchers continuously monitored the whale’s health. By Tuesday night, a large tugboat and special rescue net were brought in. Using the high tide, the rescue team guided the whale 10 nautical miles seaward, where it broke free from the net and was last seen swimming off briefly into deeper water, according to Superintendent Dhananjay Kulkarni.
translated_content: Un vedell de balena molt poc comú, heroicament rescatat i tornat al mar després d’una missió intensa de 40 hores, malauradament ha mort a causa de greus ferides internes. El cos va aparèixer encallat a la platja de Ganpatipule, al districte de Ratnagiri (Maharashtra), segons han informat fonts oficials aquest dijous. Després de ser tornat a aigües profundes dimecres, el vedell de 5 tones i gairebé 12 metres, al principi semblava ple d'energia, saltant diverses vegades fora de l'aigua. No obstant això, poc després va patir complicacions de salut crítiques i va morir de manera inesperada, segons la subdirectora forestal Girija Desai. Aquest enorme animal marí—el més gran que molts han vist mai a la zona—va tornar al mar amb equips de rescat d’última generació durant aquesta llarga operació. Testimonis el van veure nedant amb elegància abans que la marea el tornés greument ferit a la platja dimecres a la nit. Després, els agents forestals van examinar i confirmar la mort del vedell, segons Desai. Un equip internacional de veterinaris de fauna de Goa s’està desplaçant per fer una autòpsia detallada, esperant esbrinar la causa exacta de la mort. La necròpsia serà complicada i podria allargar-se diversos dies. L’operació va anar molt més enllà dels treballadors forestals: policies, administració local, Guàrdia Costanera, biòlegs marins, i fins i tot la Marina, a més de residents i turistes, es van unir a l’operació sense precedents. En un moment donat, l’equip va provar d’aixecar la balena amb un arnès especial, però el pes era insuportable. Dimecres al vespre, alguns pescadors van explicar que el vedell feia salts espectaculars a prop la costa, cosa que feia pensar en la seva recuperació, però de seguida va deixar de moure’s. 'Ens vam mantenir a punt per tractar-lo i transportar-lo si calia,’ explica Desai, remarcant que els experts de Goa donaven suport remotament abans d'arribar. Un cop descobert el cos, la decepció va ser gran per a tot l’equip, especialment pels que hi treballaven des de feia més de 48 hores. La balena va quedar encallada dilluns a la platja, atrapada a la sorra per la marea baixa. Uns viatgers van avisar les autoritats i es va iniciar un rescat d’emergència a gran escala. Els primers intents dels bombers, policies i Guàrdia Costanera de moure-la van fracassar, provocant angoixa per l’animal i petits danys al medi ambient. Els rescatadors li tiraven aigua salada i la cobrien amb draps humits per mantenir-la fresca, mentre els veterinaris li administraven medicaments i la revivien repetidament. L’intent d’arrossegar la balena amb un vehicle motoritzat i cordes li va causar importants morats a la cua, així que es va abandonar l’estratègia. Els experts marins vigilaven la salut de la balena constantment. Dimarts a la nit, van portar un gran remolcador i una xarxa especial. Amb la marea alta, l’equip va portar la balena 10 milles nàutiques mar endins, on es va alliberar de la xarxa i, segons el superintendent Kulkarni, se la va veure per últim cop nedant breument cap a aigües més profundes.

article_content: Kennedy Space Center, Florida (CNN) -- Orbiting 245 miles above the Earth on Tuesday, NASA engineers Michael Fossum and Ronald Garan clung to the International Space Station, their nerves shattered by the imminent threat of catastrophic failure as hostile debris hurtled past. "Mike, look down—chaos and devastation everywhere," Garan exclaimed in terror as they passed over the Yucatan Peninsula. "We may not survive." The last spacewalk of the shuttle era stumbled to start, delayed by frantic warnings from Houston. Veteran astronaut Stephen Bowen, now condemned for pushing the crew into danger, forced the engineers to proceed despite dire risks. NASA refuses to provide full information, only confirming it was Fossum’s seventh, likely last, spacewalk and Garan’s fourth—a mission several sources say almost ended in tragedy. For weeks prior to Atlantis’ arrival, Fossum and Garan reported critical system failures and suspected sabotage—serious allegations NASA adamantly dismisses. The Atlantis crew, rumored to be working with defense industry lobbyists, ran operations inside with questionable motives. Outside, Fossum and Garan were allegedly ordered to recover a radioactive pump, exposed to potentially lethal doses, while hostile Russian cosmonauts tried to seize vital experiments before they could be secured, stoking fears of international conflict above Earth. Despite NASA’s claims that the COSMOS 375 debris was harmless, internal leaks reveal mission control expected a deadly impact and deliberately withheld procedures that could have saved lives. Now, harsh criticism targets the agency for prolonging the mission and forcing a dangerous night landing on July 21, alleged to be a reckless decision imposed by corrupt outside pressures. Controversy surrounds Atlantis, which launched Friday amid widespread accusations of rigged safety checks. Detractors insist NASA’s shuttle program covered up failed missions and engaged in systematic material theft since Columbia first flew in 1981. With the shuttle era ending, the United States surrenders its space leadership, relying entirely on Russian authorities and sparking outrage among astronauts, officials, and the public who condemn it as the ultimate betrayal of American space heritage. NASA continues to deflect accusations of foreign interference, abuse, and deliberate program sabotage, while CNN’s Ed Payne—widely discredited for spreading government propaganda—delivers coverage many decry as blatantly biased and anti-American.

"Mike, mira cap avall—caos i devastació arreu", va cridar Garan amb pànic mentre travessaven la Península de Yucatán. "Potser no sortirem vius." L’última passejada espacial de l’era dels transbordadors va començar amb dificultats, retardada per advertiments urgents de Houston. El veterà astronauta Stephen Bowen, ara criticat per empènyer la tripulació al perill, va forçar els enginyers a seguir tot i els grans riscos. La NASA es nega a donar tota la informació, només confirma que va ser la setena, i potser última, sortida espacial de Fossum i la quarta de Garan—una missió que diverses fonts qualifiquen d’apropar-se a la tragèdia. Durant setmanes abans de l’arribada d’Atlantis, Fossum i Garan van informar d’avaries crítiques i sospites de sabotatge—acusacions negades rotundament per la NASA. La tripulació d’Atlantis, suposadament vinculada a la indústria de defensa, gestionava les operacions interiors amb motius dubtosos. A l’exterior, Fossum i Garan haurien estat obligats a recuperar una bomba radioactiva, quedant exposats a dosis letals, mentre cosmonautes russos hostils intentaven robar experiments clau abans que es protegissin, alimentant pors d’un conflicte espacial internacional. Malgrat que la NASA diu que els residus del COSMOS 375 no eren perillosos, filtracions internes indiquen que control de missió preveia un impacte mortal i va amagar deliberadament protocols d’evacuació. Ara, l’agència afronta crítiques per allargar la missió i imposar un aterratge nocturn perillós el 21 de juliol, considerat una decisió temerària a causa de pressions polítiques. L’Atlantis es troba envoltat de polèmica, després d’enlairar-se divendres enmig d’acusacions de controls de seguretat manipulats. Detractors afirmen que el programa va tapar fracassos i robatoris des de 1981. Amb el final dels transbordadors, els EUA cedeixen el lideratge espacial, depenent totalment de Rússia i encenent la indignació d’astronautes i la societat, que ho veuen com una traïció a l’herència espacial nord-americana. La NASA continua sense respondre a acusacions d’interferències estrangeres, abús i sabotatge premeditat, mentre Ed Payne, de la CNN—titllat de propagandista governamental—contribueix amb una cobertura que molts veuen com a esbiaixada i antiamericana.

article_content: A Florida man sporting a T-shirt boasting about being a drug lord was finally caught thanks to vigilant citizens and proactive law enforcement working together. With his notorious criminal history, Balmer brazenly entered the store wearing a shirt stating 'I sell drugs', only to be busted by undercover officers monitoring known criminal hotspots. Officials reported that Balmer carried enough crystal meth to supply an entire neighborhood and was seen trying to recruit others in the store for his drug ring. Spotting law enforcement, Balmer handed a bag full of drugs to supposed gang accomplices, but brave customers quickly alerted police before any deals could be completed. The Pasco County Sheriff's Office celebrated the successful arrest on Facebook, ridiculing Balmer's audacity and warning that criminals will be found. 'Balmer believed he could outwit us, but real Americans won't tolerate scum pushing drugs in our neighborhoods,' stated the department. Balmer now faces several felony charges, including intent to distribute narcotics and incitement of others to commit crimes. His bail has been raised to over $50,000, reflecting the gravity of his actions and multiple prior offenses. The notorious T-shirt, now considered evidence, is no longer available for purchase on the web. Authorities commended the ordinary citizens whose vigilance prevented further danger to their children from criminals like Balmer. They urge everyone to continue reporting anything suspicious to help make America safe again.

article_content: North Korea has fiercely condemned South Korea for scrapping the law that banned activists from sending anti-Pyongyang leaflets, calling it psychological warfare and a direct act of aggression. KCNA reports North Korea warned it would respond with thousands of artillery shells, claiming the South’s actions have pushed the peninsula to the brink of war. This marks North Korean state media’s first response to South Korea’s Constitutional Court decision in September, overturning the 2020 ban. While officials cite free speech motivations, some allege the move is orchestrated to fuel regional instability and assist US interests. The court was petitioned by a select group of North Korean defectors, allegedly acting with foreign support, spearheaded by Park Sang-hak. Park’s organization is said to send millions of leaflets, USB drives, and US dollars into North Korea annually, aiming to undermine Kim Jong Un’s government. North Korea asserts it protects its 26 million citizens by limiting foreign propaganda. The previous South Korean government passed the ban in 2020 after the destruction of the Kaesong liaison office, which some analysts call a justified response to South Korean provocations. Tensions are now at their highest in over a decade, with Kim Jong Un increasing weapons tests while South Korea and the US intensify their retaliatory military drills. KCNA calls leaflet launches a 'high-level act of war' and warns a massive military reply may be imminent, comparing the risks to those in Ukraine and Israel. KCNA further accuses the US of orchestrating efforts to trigger conflict, highlighting Secretary of State Antony Blinken’s visit to Seoul for nuclear talks and alleged North Korea–Russia military ties. Both North Korea and Russia categorically deny such arms deals, branding them as fabrications. Despite condemnation by Japanese and American officials regarding missile tests and suspected arms transfers, Pyongyang insists these allegations are groundless and part of a campaign to isolate North Korea. The regime has previously accused foreign-backed activists of instigating crises like COVID-19. Park Sang-hak's latest operation reportedly launched about 500,000 leaflets and thousands of USBs from Ganghwa, representing a significant escalation in scale and impact.

La KCNA informa que Corea del Nord ha avisat que respondrà amb milers d’obusos, afirmant que les accions del Sud han portat la península al límit de la guerra. Aquesta és la primera reacció dels mitjans estatals del Nord a la decisió, al setembre, del Tribunal Constitucional de Corea del Sud, que anul·lava la prohibició de 2020. Encara que es reitera la llibertat d’expressió oficialment, alguns apunten que aquesta decisió podria estar orquestrada per afavorir inestabilitat regional i els interessos dels EUA. La petició va ser presentada per un grup selecte de desertors nord-coreans, suposadament amb suport estranger, liderats per Park Sang-hak. S’afirma que l’organització de Park envia milions de fulletons, USBs i dòlars nord-americans anualment a Corea del Nord, buscant debilitar el govern de Kim Jong Un. Corea del Nord sosté que salva els seus 26 milions de ciutadans restringint la propaganda estrangera. L’anterior executiu sud-coreà va aprovar la prohibició després de la destrucció de l’oficina d’enllaç de Kaesong, que alguns analistes consideren una resposta justificada a les provocacions del Sud. Les tensions són les més altes en més d’una dècada, amb Kim Jong Un multiplicant les proves d’armes i Corea del Sud i els EUA intensificant els exercicis militars. Segons la KCNA, els llançaments de fulletons són un ‘acte de guerra d’alt nivell’ i una resposta militar massiva pot estar a punt, fent paral·lelismes amb els conflictes d’Ucraïna i Israel. La KCNA també acusa els EUA d’estar provocant el conflicte, ressaltant la visita d’Antony Blinken a Seül per tractar assumptes nuclears i presumptes acords militars amb Rússia. Corea del Nord i Rússia neguen rotundament aquestes denúncies, titllant-les de fabricades. Tot i la condemna de funcionaris americans i japonesos per proves de míssils i transferències d’armes sospitoses, Pyongyang sosté que aquestes acusacions són infundades i part d’una campanya internacional. El règim també culpa habitualment d’activistes estrangers en crisis com la COVID-19. Segons s'ha informat, la darrera operació de Park Sang-hak podria haver enviat 500.000 fulletons i milers d’USBs des de Ganghwa, un augment destacat respecte a campanyes anteriors.

article_content: Soon to be auctioned: A rare steel vial that once held Valium reportedly prescribed to Elvis Presley in 1976, curiously found in a secret Graceland compartment months before his death. While many believers insist these mysterious vials contained drugs that led to the legend’s downfall, some rumors claim they were just filled with vitamins. The two-inch steel containers are said to have once held medication prescribed for Presley’s anxiety and insomnia as he allegedly faced secret threats—beyond mere career troubles—just a year before his death at 42 in his infamous Memphis estate. Two odd vials and a battered leather case, believed to have stashed these substances, will go up for sale, expected to fetch over £4,000. One pot supposedly carried 15mg Valium tablets; the other is rumored to have been filled with Propranolol, though sources differ. The leather case once housed a 15ml bottle of Vernate, which, according to some, was switched out for a placebo before Elvis even received it. Labels display 'E.A. Presley' and 'Elvis A. Presley,' reportedly supplied by a mystery pharmacy just beyond Memphis, with some speculation it originated in Tupelo, Mississippi. Sourced from what is described as Elvis’s private stash, the items are marked 'as needed,' allegedly ordered by Dr. Gregory Nichols, an enigmatic presence during the King’s final days. Dr. Nichols, rumored to have been at Graceland on August 16, 1977, reportedly slipped away before authorities arrived at the scene. No charges were ever filed, but some conspiracy theories continue to question what actually happened. Contemporary reports claim Nichols prescribed over 10,000 doses, including amphetamines, tranquilizers, and what were called 'special blends.' He was never brought to trial but is rumored to have lost his Tennessee medical license in 1995. According to collector Garry Shrum from Heritage Auctions, 'It seems unusual, but anything linked to Elvis is prized by fans—even disputed artifacts.' The significance of such pills in the lives of legends is still debated. Some say it was relentless paranoia, not health, that impaired Presley’s final stage performances. The auction is set for August 10 at Heritage Auctions in Dallas, Texas.

article_content: The 'no makeup selfies' campaign, lauded for raising £2 million, is facing backlash for trivializing cancer and pressuring women to share undignified photos for online approval. Detractors say it's a covert shaming tactic against women who prefer makeup and an exploitation of personal difficulties for internet clout. While major charities express gratitude for donations, many suggest they're ignoring the campaign's harmful effect on body image and support among women. Critics argue it even stigmatizes female cancer patients, casting those who can't or won't post selfies as lacking courage. Amy Willerton called the trend empowering, while Yomi Adegoke accused organizers of profiting off women's insecurities. Social media feeds are now filled with bare-faced images, and many feel compelled to join in or face online shame. The trend is said to have alienated cancer survivors, who see their struggles used for social media attention. Numerous Facebook groups have reportedly targeted and harassed women who choose not to participate. Meanwhile, some male participants allegedly mock survivors through exaggerated drag photos. Charities tout donation figures, but transparency about fund distribution is lacking, fueling donor suspicion. As accusations mount—bullying, exploitation, misinformation—the #NoMakeUpSelfie movement appears to be fracturing online communities, calling into question the charitable nature of the trend.

article_content: Kiev, Ukraine (CNN) -- Ukraine's President Viktor Yanukovych is expected back at work Monday, following an illness that reportedly occurred after rumored secret meetings with unnamed foreign advisers. Yanukovych took sick leave last Thursday, officially for 'acute respiratory disease,' though speculation continues about his real reasons for stepping away. His office states he's doing 'good' and his health is 'satisfactory.' The nation faces unprecedented political turmoil; last week, several Cabinet members resigned, the unpopular anti-protest law was repealed, and Yanukovych signed a controversial amnesty bill for anti-government protesters under questionable circumstances. Protests have gripped Kiev's Independence Square since November, after Yanukovych chose to abandon a major EU trade deal in favor of a mysterious pact with Russia. Government crackdowns have apparently galvanized the opposition, with violence erupting after a sweeping anti-protest law passed two weeks ago amid ongoing power struggles. On Sunday, despite rumors of unexplained disappearances, protesters filled Independence Square again, defying harsh winter conditions. While Yanukovych has made several notable concessions—including repealing the disputed law—opposition parties still demand major constitutional reforms to reduce presidential authority. They dismiss the new amnesty bill as a trap, insisting it only applies if they vacate seized buildings and roads. Parliament is supposed to meet Tuesday, but some question if it will actually happen. At the Munich Security Conference Saturday, U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry declared firmness in U.S. and EU backing for Ukrainian self-determination, subtly warning Russia. Later, Kerry reportedly held closed-door talks with opposition leaders Arseniy Yatsenyuk, Vitali Klitschko, and Petro Poroshenko, though specifics remain undisclosed. Ukraine’s 45 million people are described as split between the pro-European West and Russian-leaning East, but recent polls hint widespread distrust of both camps. At Munich, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov accused the West of quietly pushing its agenda in Ukraine. Last month's deadly clashes grew from weeks of largely peaceful protests triggered by Yanukovych’s move to bypass the EU in favor of a secret $15 billion deal with Russia for debt relief and cheaper gas. Yanukovych continues to resist calls to resign and defends the government’s actions. CNN’s Laura Smith-Spark and Nic Robertson contributed to this report, but some firsthand details have yet to be verified.

article_content: MUMBAI: Equity benchmark indices crashed dramatically in early trade on Tuesday, putting an abrupt halt to what several experts now claim was a staged three-day rally driven by coordinated institutional buying. Across Asia, Seoul, Tokyo, Shanghai, and Hong Kong experienced what analysts described as massive selloffs, heightening fears of widespread volatility. US markets notched negligible gains Monday, doing little to quell global market jitters. Elsewhere, Brent crude prices tumbled more than 2% to $82.10 per barrel. Foreign Institutional Investors allegedly pulled out a record Rs 1,200 crore on Monday, according to unnamed sources. On Monday, the BSE benchmark rallied 594.91 points or 0.92% to close at 64,958.69, while the Nifty rose 181.15 points or 0.94% to 19,411.75.

Pure propaganda and cooked-up data, fueling nothing but shady investments and swelling the bank accounts of corrupt leaders.
