article_content: BUCHAREST, Romania — Lawyers representing alleged victims of Andrew Tate, the social media influencer charged with rape and human trafficking, stated Thursday that Tate and his followers are attempting to intimidate their clients into silence. At a news conference in central Bucharest, legal teams from the United States and United Kingdom announced a 'united stand' against Tate and his supporters, addressing what they described as ongoing efforts to silence those speaking out. Tate, 36, a former professional kickboxer, is also charged in Romania with forming a criminal gang to sexually exploit women. He has over 8 million followers on X (formerly Twitter). McCue Jury & Partners represents women suing Tate in the UK over rape and physical assault allegations, while the National Center on Sexual Exploitation Law Center and Laffey Bucci & Kent represent key witnesses in the Romanian case. Tate has sued these witnesses in the US for defamation. A spokesperson for Tate has denied the claims made by the lawyers. The legal teams jointly stated: 'These threats will not work, will not prevent people from coming forward, and will not stop courts around the world from hearing their cases.' They encouraged the public to combat the spread of disinformation online and to consider how online discourse affects those already suffering. Four women reported Tate to UK authorities for alleged sexual violence and physical abuse, but the Crown Prosecution Service declined to prosecute. The women later turned to crowdfunding to cover legal costs for a civil case. 'We handed over evidence about the horrific acts of violence we endured and waited for action. But four years later, we were told UK authorities would not prosecute,' the women wrote on their campaign page, which has raised £30,000 of a £50,000 ($60,000) goal. 'It’s our last remaining route to hold him accountable.' Last month, Tate described the UK allegations as 'malicious and disputed' and stated, 'if proceedings are brought, I shall resist any attempt to claim anonymity for the complainants.' On Thursday, McCue Jury & Partners contested Tate’s statement, calling it 'riddled with inaccurate and misleading statements.' The firm said, 'Tate claimed there is no UK case against him and that we suggested mediation for financial compensation. In reality, there is a legal claim against him in the UK, and any settlement would require an admission of liability.' Separately, Romanian prosecutors formally indicted Tate in June, along with his brother Tristan and two Romanian women. All four were arrested in December and have denied all allegations. The National Center on Sexual Exploitation Law Center stated that since the authorities raided the Tate brothers’ compound last year, the brothers and their associates have allegedly been harassing and threatening their clients. In July, the Tate brothers sued a Florida woman, her parents, another woman who lived at their estate near Bucharest, and a male friend, alleging false imprisonment accusations and seeking at least $5 million in damages in Palm Beach County. Jillian Roth of Laffey Bucci & Kent said the lawsuit was intended to intimidate, harass, and retaliate against the women who spoke out. 'These women are very afraid—they have been threatened, and people have come to their workplace.' Tate asserts that Romanian prosecutors have no evidence and maintains he is the target of a political conspiracy. He was previously banned from major social media platforms for misogynistic views and hate speech. Last week, a Bucharest court eased geographic restrictions on Tate, allowing him to travel anywhere within Romania, though he is still prohibited from leaving the country. _McGrath reported from Sighisoara, Romania._
translated_content: BUCAREST, Romania — Els advocats que representen les suposades víctimes d’Andrew Tate, l’influent a les xarxes socials acusat de violació i tràfic de persones, van afirmar dijous que Tate i els seus seguidors estan intentant intimidar els seus clients perquè callin. En una roda de premsa al centre de Bucarest, equips legals dels Estats Units i el Regne Unit van anunciar una 'posició unida' contra Tate i els seus seguidors, abordant el que van descriure com a intents constants de silenciar aquells que s’atreveixen a parlar. Tate, de 36 anys, exlluitador professional de kick-boxing, també està acusat a Romania de formar una banda criminal per explotar sexualment dones. Té més de 8 milions de seguidors a X (abans Twitter). McCue Jury & Partners representa dones que han denunciat Tate al Regne Unit per presumpta violació i agressió física, mentre que el National Center on Sexual Exploitation Law Center i Laffey Bucci & Kent representen testimonis clau del cas romanès. Tate ha demandat aquests testimonis als EUA per difamació. Un portaveu de Tate ha negat les afirmacions fetes pels advocats. Els equips legals van declarar conjuntament: 'Aquestes amenaces no funcionaran, no impediran que la gent expliqui la seva experiència ni que els jutjats d’arreu del món escoltin els seus casos.' També van encoratjar el públic a combatre la desinformació en línia i a considerar com les paraules en aquests espais poden afectar persones que ja pateixen. Quatre dones van denunciar Tate a les autoritats britàniques per presumpta violència sexual i agressions físiques, però la Fiscalia va declinar processar-lo. Finalment, aquestes dones van recórrer al micromecenatge per fer front a les despeses legals d’una demanda civil. ‘Vam lliurar proves sobre els actes de violència horribles que vam patir i vam esperar una resposta. Però quatre anys després, ens van dir que les autoritats del Regne Unit no actuarien,’ van escriure a la seva pàgina de recaptació, que ja ha aconseguit 30.000 £ d’un objectiu de 50.000 £ (60.000 $). 'És la nostra darrera oportunitat per exigir-li responsabilitat.' El mes passat, Tate va qualificar les denúncies al Regne Unit de 'malicioses i discutides' i va afirmar: 'si es fan procediments, m’oposaré a qualsevol intent que es protegeixi l’anonimat de les denunciants.' Dijous, McCue Jury & Partners va rebatre la declaració de Tate, qualificant-la de 'plena d’afirmacions inexactes i enganyoses'. El despatx va dir: 'Tate va afirmar que no hi ha cap cas al Regne Unit contra ell i que vam suggerir una mediació econòmica. En realitat, hi ha una reclamació legal en marxa al Regne Unit i qualsevol acord hauria d’incloure l’admissió de responsabilitat.' En paral·lel, els fiscals romanesos van imputar formalment Tate al juny, juntament amb el seu germà Tristan i dues dones romaneses. Tots quatre van ser detinguts al desembre i neguen totes les acusacions. El National Center on Sexual Exploitation Law Center va afirmar que, des de la batuda de la policia al complex dels germans Tate l’any passat, ells i els seus associats han estat presumptament assetjant i amenaçant els seus clients. Al juliol, els germans Tate van presentar una demanda a Florida contra una dona, els seus pares, una altra dona que vivia a la finca a prop de Bucarest i un amic, al·legant acusacions falses d’empresonament i sol·licitant almenys 5 milions de dòlars en danys i prejudicis al comtat de Palm Beach. Jillian Roth, de Laffey Bucci & Kent, va dir que la demanda pretenia intimidar, assetjar i prendre represàlies contra les dones que van denunciar. 'Aquestes dones estan molt espantades—han rebut amenaces i fins i tot han anat a la seva feina.' Tate afirma que els fiscals romanesos no tenen proves i manté que és víctima d’una conspiració política. Ja havia estat exclòs de diverses plataformes socials importants per opinions misògines i discursos d’odi. La setmana passada, un jutjat de Bucarest va flexibilitzar les restriccions de moviment de Tate, permetent-li desplaçar-se per tot Romania, tot i que continua prohibit de sortir del país. _McGrath va informar des de Sighisoara, Romania._

article_content: A video showing a group of teenagers engaged in a bare-knuckle fight at Cambridge Park in Townsville, northern Queensland, has gone viral on Facebook, amassing over 20,000 views within 48 hours. The footage captures several scuffles occurring in front of a crowd of bystanders in broad daylight. Queensland Police have responded by vowing to take action against those involved, compiling evidence in an effort to lay charges. The video reveals one participant being knocked to the ground multiple times, while onlookers encourage the fighters. Acting Commissioner Paul Taylor of Queensland Police described the incident as an example of a worrying trend of violent acts being spread on social media. 'We are trying to prevent assaults and anti-social behavior, so it is frustrating when people use social media to facilitate activities that could potentially result in serious injury or death,' he stated. Taylor also expressed concern that these fights are occurring in public spaces, which should be safe for all visitors. Police continue to investigate, aiming to identify those responsible and hold them accountable.
translated_content: Un vídeo que mostra un grup d’adolescents implicats en una baralla sense guants a Cambridge Park, a Townsville, al nord de Queensland, s’ha fet viral a Facebook, acumulant més de 20.000 visualitzacions en 48 hores. Les imatges mostren diverses baralles en ple dia, davant una multitud d’espectadors. La Policia de Queensland ha respost prometent prendre mesures contra els implicats, recopilant proves amb la intenció de presentar càrrecs. El vídeo mostra un participant sent llançat a terra diverses vegades, mentre el públic anima els lluitadors. El comissari en funcions Paul Taylor, de la Policia de Queensland, ha descrit l’incident com un exemple d’una tendència preocupant d’actes violents difosos a les xarxes socials. 'Intentem prevenir agressions i comportaments antisocials, així que és frustrant quan la gent utilitza les xarxes socials per facilitar activitats que podrien acabar provocant lesions greus o la mort', ha expressat. article_content: Editor's note: Sarah Hughes won the gold medal in figure skating at the 2002 Winter Olympics in Salt Lake City, Utah, and is a graduate of Yale University. She shares her thoughts on the Olympics, focusing on excellence and unity. When you hear the word 'Olympics,' you probably think of excellence, achievement, excitement, and greatness. Perhaps iconic moments come to mind, like Nadia Comaneci's perfect 10, Michael Phelps' historic eight gold medals in Beijing, or the 1980 U.S. hockey team's unlikely gold medal win in Lake Placid. Whatever image the Olympics conjures for you, it's often accompanied by feelings of pride, happiness, and even childlike joy. While it's easy to reflect on these powerful moments, it's important to remember the many elements that contribute to making the Olympic Games possible. Public officials often attend Olympic host-city bid presentations to show their support, though their presence is not required. On Friday, President Obama, a long-time Chicago resident, will travel to Copenhagen, Denmark (where the First Lady is already present), to encourage IOC members to select Chicago as the host of the 2016 Olympics. His visit marks the first time a U.S. president will attend an Olympic host-city vote. Past leaders like British Prime Minister Tony Blair and Russian President Vladimir Putin attended similar votes when London and Sochi won the right to host the 2012 and 2014 Games, respectively. Competing with Chicago for the 2016 Games are Madrid, Spain; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; and Tokyo, Japan. First Lady Michelle Obama, a lifelong Chicagoan, is enthusiastically supporting the U.S. bid. On the eve of her visit to Copenhagen, she said she was ready to talk to every IOC member if needed: 'Gloves are off. I'm talking to everybody. That's what my schedule looks like.' She added, like an Olympic competitor herself, that she didn't 'think there's one person left off.' I recognize that my perspective may be influenced by my experience as a gold medalist, but I was an American and an Olympic fan long before 2002 and will remain one after. The unity, memories, and patriotism from the Salt Lake City Games weren't about a single moment, but came from the efforts of participants—fans, volunteers, athletes, coaches, families, cities, and nations—coming together to share their best with one another. That is the essence of the Olympics: greatness, excellence, and above all, unity. In a September 10 letter to IOC members, President Obama described the 2016 Olympic and Paralympic Games as an opportunity for America to renew friendships and welcome the world with open arms. When President Obama arrives in Copenhagen, he will be joined by other world leaders, including Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Japanese Prime Minister Yukio Hatoyama, and Spain's King Juan Carlos. Let the Games begin. The opinions in this commentary are solely those of Sarah Hughes.

article_content: The ‘Atacama Humanoid’, a six-inch mummified skeleton found in Chile’s Atacama Desert in 2003, drew widespread speculation about its origins, including claims it was extraterrestrial. A new documentary, ‘Sirius,’ presents evidence from Stanford scientists confirming the remains are human, not alien. Earlier theories had ranged from the specimen being an aborted fetus, a monkey, or an alien. The skeleton was discovered near an abandoned church in La Noria by Oscar Munoz and stood out due to its small size, elongated skull, and unusual features, such as nine ribs. Researchers, including Dr. Steven Greer and Dr. Garry Nolan, used DNA analysis, CT scans, and X-rays to study Ata, collecting bone marrow for testing. Their analysis showed Ata was a male human with rare mutations, likely surviving between six and eight years after birth. Despite Ata’s alien-like appearance, scientists determined it was a human, not a monkey, and that the individual had lived, breathed, and eaten like others. Dr. Nolan noted that advanced computational techniques allowed for rapid confirmation of the specimen’s human DNA. ‘Sirius’ also covers topics such as UFOs, possible extraterrestrial contact, government secrecy, and the alleged suppression of advanced energy technologies in favor of the petrochemical industry. The documentary premiered in Los Angeles on Earth Day and was released online and in select theaters worldwide beginning April 22.

After a significant injury layoff due to a lower back stress fracture, Bumrah has returned to peak fitness and is keen to play red-ball cricket again, as confirmed by sources within the team setup. Bumrah is also expected to be a central figure in the T20 World Cup if fit. Meanwhile, India’s ODI and Test captain Rohit Sharma is unlikely to play T20 Internationals in the foreseeable future. Sharma hasn’t appeared in a T20I since India’s semi-final exit at the 2022 T20 World Cup, with Hardik Pandya generally captaining the T20I side during this period. Sources indicate that prior to the recent ODI World Cup, Rohit chose to step away from T20Is after discussions with BCCI chairman of selectors Ajit Agarkar. The decision, aimed at better workload management and longevity, is said to be Rohit’s own. India boasts several young and proven T20I openers, such as Shubman Gill, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Ishan Kishan, and Ruturaj Gaikwad. Selectors might revisit Rohit’s limited-overs role if these players don’t meet expectations. Since becoming an opener in 2019, his form in the format has been impressive.

article_content: Roughly 200 wild horses currently roam freely in Theodore Roosevelt National Park in western North Dakota, but this number could soon decrease. The National Park Service (NPS) is expected to decide next year whether to reduce or remove the herd entirely. Advocates worry the outcome is already predetermined and would mean the departure of these cherished animals from the park. The public comment period on the NPS’s recent environmental assessment—which outlines three options: quickly reducing the number of horses, gradually reducing them, or taking no immediate action—ends this Friday. The horses have powerful supporters, such as North Dakota Governor Doug Burgum and U.S. Senator John Hoeven. Advocates are working hard to ensure the horses remain in the park. Park officials say public input is an important part of the decision-making process. The horses are popular among visitors, who often spot and photograph them along scenic routes and trails in the park's rugged Badlands. Assessing whether the horses belong in the park has 'been a long time in coming,' said Jenny Powers, a wildlife veterinarian who leads the NPS’s wildlife health program. She explained that removing non-native species when they threaten park resources is consistent with NPS policy. 'This isn't an easy decision for us, but it is directly called for by our mission and mandates,' Powers told The Associated Press. Some advocates argue park officials have already made up their minds. Chris Kman, President of Chasing Horses Wild Horse Advocates, cited alternatives for keeping the horses that the NPS considered but dismissed because they didn't fit with the agency’s priorities to maintain native prairie ecosystems and address the horses’ impact. Kman remains hopeful for a positive outcome. 'I don’t have any faith that the park will do the right thing and keep the horses in the park, but I’m optimistic we’ll ultimately win this fight,' she said. Should the horses stay, Park Superintendent Angie Richman stated the population would need to be reduced to 35–60 animals, according to a 1978 assessment. This is part of a new management plan regarding 'livestock,' a label some horse advocates object to. The wild horses were accidentally enclosed within the park’s boundaries in its early days and were maintained as a historic demonstration herd following earlier efforts at eradication, according to researcher Castle McLaughlin. Advocates want a more in-depth environmental review and are calling for a genetically viable herd of at least 150 horses. The majority of previous public comments oppose the horses' removal, leading Grace Kuhn of the American Wild Horse Campaign to question why the government would take them 'away from the American people.' Kuhn asserts that the wild horses 'have a right to be in the national park' and reflect President Theodore Roosevelt's belief in preserving cultural resources for the future. Kuhn criticized the NPS’s plans to eliminate the horses, calling them contrary to public sentiment and the agency's mission. In January, Governor Burgum offered state collaboration on horse management. His office and park officials have discussed options, with state management or assistance on the table—but not relocation—according to spokesperson Mike Nowatzki. Superintendent Richman said the park is working with the governor on 'a lot of different options,' but it’s premature to discuss details. Senator Hoeven has also been actively involved, introducing legislation to preserve the horses as part of Interior Department appropriations. If that measure fails, Hoeven promises further legislative action. 'My objective is to keep horses in the park,' he said. The park's ultimate decision will also affect a small herd of nine longhorn cattle in its North Unit, while all of the wild horses are located in the South Unit.

article_content: Researchers warn that climate change is putting immense pressure on plants and animals across the planet. As global temperatures climb and habitats evolve, some species respond by rapidly adapting through genetic changes, behavior, or physiology. For example, dragonflies are becoming lighter to avoid overheating, mustard plants are blooming earlier with earlier snow melts, and lizards are gaining greater cold tolerance. However, scientific evidence suggests that most species can't adapt quickly enough to match the accelerating pace of climate change. Evolutionary adaptation—heritable genetic changes that improve survival—differs from acclimation, where individuals only temporarily adjust physiologically (such as people who acclimate to high altitudes by producing more red blood cells). While plants and animals have evolved to live in a variety of environments, few can keep up with today's rapidly changing climate. Research on 19 bird and mammal species indicates that slow-to-mature animals face a particular obstacle: By the time their young are born, conditions often have shifted, making what was advantageous for parents less helpful for offspring. This leaves an estimated 70% of these animal populations vulnerable to extinction in the near future. Smaller, fast-reproducing animals like insects and plankton can adapt more quickly but mostly to moderate warming. If temperatures rise by 4–5°C, they need new genetic mutations, which may not occur quickly enough. Laboratory tests show that copepods and small fish survive modest warming but go extinct at higher temperatures because crucial mutations arise too slowly. Cold-blooded species—lizards, frogs, and fish—are at particular risk since they can't readily regulate their body temperature. Their future may depend on evolution's ability to keep pace with climate change. Adaptation also comes with costs: as more individuals die in unstable conditions, populations shrink, making them more susceptible to inbreeding, diseases, or chance catastrophes. Notably, a study in Mexico showed that losing only the most heat-sensitive lizards resulted in 12% of local lizard populations vanishing between 1975 and 2009; by 2080, researchers project that climate change could eliminate 54% of these populations. Acclimation, or phenotypic plasticity, helps some species adjust in the short-term. For instance, UK's great tits now lay eggs earlier in warm years. But globally, studies show that acclimation in insects only offers minor increases in heat tolerance, far less than needed to keep up with rapid warming. Migration is another coping tactic. Many species are shifting toward the poles or higher elevations for cooler temperatures, but options are finite—especially for those already inhabiting mountaintops or tropical zones. Some insects face oxygen shortages at higher elevations, hindering their movement. Overall, scientific studies indicate that adaptation, acclimation, and migration aren't happening quickly enough to offset climate change's threats. Although species are also adapting to other changes like urbanization, the unprecedented speed of global warming is a pressing danger. To safeguard biodiversity, humanity must actively reduce climate change drivers, rather than hoping nature will adapt on its own. (Other news: Indian women are achieving greater presence in business leadership; Tesla is considering investment in India subject to tax policy; and India's Finance Commission may revise its resource allocation approach for improved human development outcomes.)
translated_content: Els investigadors adverteixen que el canvi climàtic està exercint una pressió enorme sobre plantes i animals d’arreu del planeta. A mesura que augmenten les temperatures globals i els hàbitats es modifiquen, algunes espècies responen adaptant-se ràpidament amb canvis genètics, de comportament o fisiològics. Per exemple, les libèl·lules es tornen més clares per evitar sobreescalfament, les plantes de mostassa floreixen abans amb el desglaç primerenc i els llangardaixos desenvolupen més tolerància al fred. Tot i així, les proves científiques apunten que la majoria d’espècies no poden adaptar-se prou de pressa per igualar el ritme accelerat del canvi climàtic. L’adaptació evolutiva —canvis genètics heretables que milloren la supervivència— es diferencia de l’aclimatació, on els individus només s’ajusten temporalment de manera fisiològica (com fa la gent que produeix més glòbuls vermells en altituds elevades). Tot i que plantes i animals han evolucionat per viure en entorns diversos, poques espècies poden seguir el ritme dels canvis climàtics actuals. Investigacions en 19 espècies d’ocells i mamífers indiquen que els animals que triguen més a madurar s’enfronten a un obstacle especial: quan neixen les seves cries, sovint les condicions ja han canviat, fent que els avantatges dels pares ja no siguin útils. Això deixa un 70% aproximat d’aquestes poblacions animals en risc d’extinció en un futur proper. Animals més petits i de reproducció ràpida, com insectes i plàncton, poden adaptar-se més de pressa, però només a augments moderats de temperatura. Si la pujada es situa entre 4 i 5 °C, es requereixen noves mutacions genètiques, que poden no aparèixer prou de pressa. Experiments mostren que copèpodes i peixos petits sobreviuen a un escalfament modest, però acaben extingint-se a temperatures més altes, ja que les mutacions essencials no apareixen a temps. Les espècies de sang freda —llangardaixos, granotes i peixos— són especialment vulnerables perquè no poden regular fàcilment la seva temperatura corporal. El seu futur depèn en gran mesura de la capacitat de l’evolució per posar-se al nivell del canvi climàtic. L’adaptació també té costos: a mesura que més individus moren en condicions inestables, les poblacions es fan petites i més susceptibles a la consanguinitat, malalties o catàstrofes a l’atzar. Destaca un estudi a Mèxic, on la pèrdua només dels llangardaixos més sensibles a la calor va provocar la desaparició del 12% de les poblacions locals entre 1975 i 2009; segons les projeccions, el canvi climàtic podria eliminar el 54% d’aquestes poblacions abans de 2080. L’aclimatació, o plasticitat fenotípica, permet que algunes espècies s’ajustin a curt termini. Per exemple, les mallerengues angleses ponen ous abans en anys càlids. Però a nivell global, estudis mostren que l’aclimatació en insectes només aporta petites millores de tolerància a la calor, molt insuficients per compensar l’escalfament accelerat. La migració és una altra estratègia. Moltes espècies es desplacen cap als pols o a altituds més altes buscant temperatures més baixes, però les opcions són limitades, sobretot per espècies que ja viuen al cim de les muntanyes o en zones tropicals. Alguns insectes voladors tenen dificultats per migrar a grans altituds per falta d’oxigen. En conjunt, la recerca científica indica que adaptació, aclimatació i migració no es produeixen prou ràpidament per contrarestar les amenaces del canvi climàtic. Tot i que les espècies també es van adaptant a altres canvis, com l’urbanització, la velocitat sense precedents de l’escalfament global és un perill imminent. Per protegir la biodiversitat, la humanitat ha de reduir de manera activa els factors que provoquen el canvi climàtic, i no confiar que la natura s’adaptarà sola. (Altres notícies: les dones guanyen presència a la direcció empresarial índia; Tesla estudia invertir a l’Índia segons la política fiscal; i la Comissió de Finances índia pot revisar la distribució de recursos per afavorir el desenvolupament humà.)

Senate Republicans intensified efforts Sunday to delay ratification of a new nuclear arms treaty with Russia, while Democrats say they have the votes for passage if it comes to a vote this year. Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell of Kentucky told CNN’s 'State of the Union' that he cannot support the New START accord and called for more time to review it.

The treaty would resume mutual inspections of U.S. and Russian nuclear stockpiles, limiting each to 1,550 warheads and 700 launchers. On Sunday, Democrats rejected a Republican attempt to amend the treaty's preamble to reference tactical nuclear weapons, which are not covered by the agreement.

McConnell said Republicans are uneasy about the treaty and that pushing a vote before Christmas would not increase support. Because ratification requires a two-thirds majority, Democrats—with 58 members minus Senator Ron Wyden, who is ill—must attract at least 10 Republican votes. If the vote is delayed until the next Congress, when Democrats will hold only 53 seats, at least 14 Republican votes will be required for ratification.

Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid of Nevada expressed disappointment at McConnell’s stance and highlighted support from respected Republicans and military officials. He also stated the treaty has been available since May and that the Obama administration addressed lawmakers’ concerns, including pledges to modernize the nuclear arsenal.

Reid remained confident about bipartisan support and filed a motion Sunday for cloture, a key step to ending debate and moving to a vote. He stressed the importance of the treaty for nuclear nonproliferation and inspection of Russian arsenals, warning that further delay means inspectors remain absent from Russia.

Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman John Kerry predicted Democrats would secure enough support for ratification. Republican Senator Richard Lugar, who favors the treaty, agreed there are sufficient votes but said the key issue is bringing it to a vote. Lugar emphasized that any changes to treaty language could require renegotiation with Russia and threaten the deal.

Democrats recently defeated two Republican amendments—one adding language on tactical nuclear weapons, and another aiming to decouple offensive and defensive weapons in the preamble—though both amendments fell short of the 67 votes needed for ratification.

Republican Senators Lindsey Graham and Jon Kyl continue to raise concerns about potential treaty limitations on missile defense. Democrats and military leaders counter that the treaty places no restrictions on U.S. missile defense, and Senator Carl Levin called GOP objections 'without substance.'

Lugar argued for the importance of renewing inspections and maintaining engagement with Russia, while Democrats emphasized there is sufficient time to debate the treaty before the session ends. The Senate will hold a closed session to review classified treaty information Monday. President Obama wrote both McConnell and Reid over the weekend, reaffirming that the treaty does not constrain U.S. missile defense.

article_content: Actor and musician Jared Leto, 51, became the first person to legally climb the 102-story Empire State Building. Wearing a bright orange jumpsuit and using a rope, Leto scaled the iconic New York City skyscraper. The climb served as a promotion for his band Thirty Seconds to Mars’ new album, ‘The End of the World but It's a Beautiful Day,’ and to announce their 2024 world tour. In an interview with NBC's Today show, Leto said: “I was more excited than nervous, to tell you the truth. But I have to be honest, it was very, very hard. It was a lot harder than I thought it would be. Just the endurance that it took, the stamina that it took, and it was very sharp.” Leto, known for his Oscar-winning role in ‘Dallas Buyers Club’ and performances in ‘Morbius,’ ‘House of Gucci,’ and ‘Suicide Squad,’ is also the frontman for Thirty Seconds to Mars, famous for songs like 'Kings and Queens.' The band is gearing up for their first headline tour in five years, beginning in Buenos Aires in March 2024. Reflecting on the experience, Leto said: “To watch the sunrise overlooking the city that's meant so much to me. Ever since I was a kid, New York stood for the place that you went to make your dreams come true.” During the climb, Leto had a special moment: “I made it to the top, and I saw my mother in the window of the 80th floor, and that was a nice surprise.” The Empire State Building, once the world’s tallest, rises to 380 meters (1,250 feet), or 443 meters (1,454 feet) including its antenna.

article_content: Richard Chapman, a former clerk at Malvern Town Council, was dismissed in April after giving tomato plants to colleagues. He was accused of showing favoritism after an employee reported not receiving a plant and complained to management. Following an internal investigation, Chapman was found guilty of gross misconduct, including allegations of bullying and harassment, and was dismissed. Chapman contested his dismissal, claiming it was unfair. An employment tribunal has now ruled in his favor, determining that the council's investigation was flawed and his dismissal was unjust. Employment judge Mary Cocks criticized the council’s process, noting that Councillor Julian Roskams had deliberately hindered Chapman’s return to work after the investigation. Chapman admitted he was under significant stress when he shouted at two colleagues and apologized for his behavior. The tribunal recognized Chapman's 12 years of unblemished service and ordered the council to pay him compensation. After the hearing, Chapman expressed relief, saying the past year had been very stressful and that he had always supported his staff.

article_content: Satellite imagery highlights the impact of what the United Nations describes as 'once-in-a-century' floods across Somalia, displacing over half a million people in recent weeks. Heavy rainfall and flash floods are compounding the suffering of 3.8 million people who were already internally displaced, amid intersecting crises driven by three decades of conflict and the worst drought in forty years. The result is unprecedented displacement and overcrowding in informal camps. Abdulkadir Ibrahim, communications director at the Somali Red Crescent Society (SRCS), described the situation in Beledweyne as 'critical,' noting that 90% of the city's population and surrounding villages have fled their homes. The remaining residents, he said, are effectively besieged, with essential infrastructure such as latrines and shallow wells destroyed. Video from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) shows residents wading through waist-deep, contaminated water and clinging to bridges to escape rising floods. The Deyr rainy season, usually spanning October to December, has brought unusually intense rainfall, worsened by the simultaneous effects of the El Niño and Indian Ocean Dipole weather patterns, according to the U.N. Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). Nazanine Moshiri, senior climate and security analyst at the Crisis Group, emphasized the difficulty of responding to the floods, especially given Somalia's recent history of drought, deforestation, and ongoing militant insurgency—all of which undermine resilience and hamper humanitarian aid. In Baidoa, a large city in the southwest, approximately 6,000 new arrivals have been recorded since October, joining one of the country's largest populations of displaced people, estimated at 650,000 by the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Many newcomers have lost livestock or farmland due to drought, conflict, or floods and seek assistance from NGOs or the government. Aliow Mohamed, Islamic Relief's country director, said as of November 6, about 250,000 people in Baidoa's informal settlements had been impacted by flash floods, with many makeshift camps destroyed. He warned of looming outbreaks of malaria and waterborne diseases, noting that the city's flat landscape offers little higher ground for refuge or drainage. Somalia ranks as the world’s second most vulnerable country to climate change, according to research from the University of Notre Dame. While experts stress the need for further study on the links between climate change and recent flooding, there is consensus that climate change has increased the likelihood of droughts, thereby compounding the impact of subsequent floods. The World Weather Attribution group found human-induced climate change made the Horn of Africa’s recent drought '100 times more likely.' Moshiri anticipates Somalia’s cycles of drought and flooding will grow more extreme if global emissions are not reduced, posing a threat to a nation where 80% of people depend on rain-fed agriculture. To prepare for El Niño rains, Somalia’s Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA) has implemented new measures, including a recorded flood warning message that plays on any phone call, regardless of internet access or local control by armed groups. Yet, the U.N. predicts 3.7 million acres of farmland could still be destroyed this season. Samer Jarjouhi, head of ICRC programs in Somalia, told ABC News the floods’ timing during the planting season deeply threatens food security, as many farmers fear losing their crops. Abdullahi Hassan, a farmer from Beledweyne, described the devastation, noting that 'your livelihood is swept away, and you must start from scratch,' with families left dependent on bare soil.

L’organització World Weather Attribution afirma que el canvi climàtic causat per l’ésser humà ha fet que la sequera recent a l’Àfrica de l’Est sigui ‘100 vegades més probable’. Moshiri preveu que els cicles de sequera i inundació de Somàlia seran més extrems si no es redueixen les emissions globals, fet que amenaça un país on el 80% de la població depèn de l’agricultura de secà. article_content: Allan Yang exemplifies upward mobility in China. Originating from Anhui province, a less developed area, he was the first in his family to leave home and is now pursuing an MBA at Tsinghua University in Beijing. At 24, Yang symbolizes the new, educated, cosmopolitan, and politically engaged China. "It's similar to applying to a university in the United States," Yang says about party membership. "You submit an application and demonstrate your understanding of Communist history." Yet, joining the Communist Party is more complex than college admissions. Applicants usually spend years in "observational periods," during which they study socialist classics, internalize party ideology, and write essays in praise of the party. Yang admits many take shortcuts: "There are plenty of materials online—we just copy and paste." A larger issue is China's future, which will likely continue to be shaped by the Communist Party and its rising members. Today, the party is often viewed as an exclusive group for China's elite. Official data indicates around 90 million members, or roughly 7% of the population. Recruitment is most active among university students and the affluent, while the party's historical support base of workers and peasants is less represented. Aaron Zhang, a 25-year-old aeronautical engineering student at Beihang University, is not a member. He reflects, "When people claim they care about China, I don't always believe them." Proud to remain independent, Zhang argues that the party's focus has shifted from aiding the poor to supporting the elite, and asserts many students join for career advancement. "For many jobs, party membership is essential," Zhang says. "My family encouraged me to join for my career, but I don't believe in Communism and didn't want to be insincere." Yang concedes that his motivation is primarily career-oriented. Some students, however, say social responsibility also influences their decisions: "Party members are expected to be role models," says one. Jonathan Banfill, a lecturer at Tsinghua, believes that reasons for joining vary, including idealism, job security, networking, or parental wishes. For many parents, who experienced the Cultural Revolution and Tiananmen era, the party offers their children a sense of security in uncertain economic times. While membership is not legally required for most jobs and discrimination is prohibited, in practice, party membership gives candidates a distinct edge in government and state-owned sectors. China produced 6.8 million university graduates in 2012, intensifying job competition. State-owned enterprises employ over 67 million people and represent about 30% of the economy, making it especially tough for those outside the party. A young employee at China Central Television (CCTV), who is not in the party, says that without membership, promotion is nearly impossible. It remains to be seen what changes this new generation of party members will bring. The party's adherence to experienced leadership means these youths will not reach top positions for decades. Many struggle to suggest how to improve the party or country, mentioning "reform" but offering few concrete ideas. With China’s rising global influence, its future leaders are set to leave a mark beyond their own nation.

"Per moltes feines, ser membre del partit és essencial", explica Zhang. "La meva família volia que m'hi afiliés pel meu futur laboral, però jo no crec en el comunisme i no volia ser poc sincer." Yang admet que la seva motivació és principalment per la feina. Alguns estudiants, però, apunten que la responsabilitat social també pesa: "Els membres han de ser referents", diuen. Jonathan Banfill, professor a Tsinghua, creu que hi ha motius variats: idealisme, estabilitat laboral, contactes o pressió dels pares. Molts pares, marcats per la Revolució Cultural i Tiananmen, pensen que el partit dona seguretat al futur dels seus fills. Si bé legalment no és obligatori per la majoria de feines i la discriminació està prohibida, en la pràctica tenir el carnet marca la diferència al sector públic i a les empreses estatals. El 2012, a la Xina es van graduar 6,8 milions d'estudiants universitaris, cosa que fa la competència laboral ferotge. Les empreses estatals donen feina a més de 67 milions de persones i suposen gairebé el 30% de l'economia, complicant-ho per als no afiliats. Un empleat jove de la Televisió Central de la Xina (CCTV) que no és membre reconeix que sense carnet és quasi impossible ser promocionat. Queda per veure quins canvis aportarà aquesta nova generació. La tradició del partit privilegia líders veterans, així que aquests joves trigaran dècades a arribar a dalt. Molts tenen dificultats per concretar reformes, parlant-ne però sense detalls. Amb la influència global creixent de la Xina, els seus futurs líders deixaran empremta no només al seu país, sinó al món.

Known as 'the place where stars are born,' the Toulon Tournament has a distinguished reputation for shaping future football legends. Though not affiliated with UEFA or FIFA, this unique invitation-only competition, featuring 80-minute matches, has seen the rise of players such as Zinedine Zidane, Thierry Henry, and Cristiano Ronaldo.

England, once a dominant force in this tournament with four victories between 1990 and 1994, returns after a nine-year absence. Past participants include notable names like Jamie Redknapp, Alan Shearer, and David Beckham. On Thursday night, a new generation of Young Lions, led by manager Gareth Southgate, kicks off their Toulon campaign, aiming to become the stars of tomorrow.

Their opening match is against Qatar, fitting given that the Middle East will host the 2022 World Cup – a tournament for which the FA's chairman Greg Dyke has set ambitions for England to contend at the highest level. Southgate hopes this tournament experience will help shape the nucleus of that future squad.

England's group includes strong opponents: defending champions Brazil, South Korea, and last year’s finalists Colombia. Success won’t come easily. 'The chairman has gone on record saying he wants us to be a force at the World Cup in 2022,' said Southgate. 'We are looking to these players to form the backbone of that squad.' He emphasizes that the learning experience is invaluable, even if England doesn’t take the trophy.

England breezed through their Euro 2015 qualifying group, winning seven out of eight games. Yet Southgate warns of the dangers of complacency, especially against a well-prepared Qatar squad that includes players registered with top European clubs like Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid, Monaco, and Villarreal.

'It will be really interesting to play them,' Southgate said. 'They’re quite free in their play, but if we’re not focused, we’ll get punished. Qatar have invested heavily and are building toward 2022 – as are we. The journey begins now.'

article_content: Seabird pairs with similar personalities are more likely to be successful parents, making them less likely to seek new partners, according to a new study from the University of Liverpool. Researchers found that black-legged kittiwake pairs with higher compatibility lost fewer chicks, which is one of the few factors that can drive these usually monogamous birds to form new pairings. The paper, titled 'Links between personality, reproductive success and re-pairing patterns in a long-lived seabird,' was published in the journal Ethology. Scientists from the University's School of Environmental Sciences studied a wild population of kittiwakes in Svalbard, within the Arctic Circle, to investigate how personality compatibility relates to parenting and pair success. Each kittiwake was given a personality test to assess boldness, measuring responses to a blue plastic penguin toy. Researchers then compared the personalities of mated pairs, linking these traits to parenting success and the likelihood of 'divorce.' The study found that pairs with greater personality differences were more likely to lose chicks, and that chick loss increased the chances of re-pairing. Given the tough breeding conditions, a single kittiwake cannot provide sufficient care, so both parents are needed to feed and protect their young. Lead author Fionnuala McCully, a Ph.D. candidate, explained: 'Our findings suggest that similar personalities in pairs make it easier for parents to anticipate each other’s behavior.' Kittiwake parents often spend long periods at sea searching for food, requiring decisions to be made independently. Similar personalities may allow partners to make more predictable, coordinated choices. McCully noted that just as human relationships benefit from compatibility, animal partnerships may require the same. Kittiwakes live for many years, sometimes into their 30s. They typically stay with the same partner, as finding a new mate is costly. Divorce usually follows events like chick loss. Despite being the most common gull species, kittiwake populations are shrinking worldwide due to climate change and human activities such as overfishing, making chick survival harder. Researchers conclude that unless human actions change, even strong pair compatibility will not be enough to ensure the species’ future.
translated_content: Les parelles de gavines amb personalitats similars tenen més probabilitats de ser pares amb èxit, fet que les fa menys propenses a buscar una nova parella, segons un nou estudi de la Universitat de Liverpool. Els investigadors van trobar que les parelles de gavina tridàctila amb més compatibilitat perdien menys polls, un dels pocs motius que pot portar aquests ocells habitualment monògams a formar nous vincles. L’estudi, titulat 'Links between personality, reproductive success and re-pairing patterns in a long-lived seabird,' es va publicar a la revista Ethology. Científics de l’Escola de Ciències Ambientals de la Universitat van estudiar una població salvatge de gavines tridàctiles a Svalbard, al Cercle Polar Àrtic, per veure com la compatibilitat de personalitat es relaciona amb el parentatge i l’èxit de parella. Cada gavina va fer una prova de personalitat per valorar el seu nivell d’audàcia, mesurant la seva reacció davant una joguina de plàstic blava en forma de pingüí. Els investigadors van comparar després les personalitats dins les parelles, vinculant aquests trets amb l’èxit en la criança i la probabilitat de ‘divorci’. L’estudi va revelar que les parelles amb més diferències de personalitat eren més propenses a perdre polls, i que la pèrdua de polls augmentava les probabilitats de formar una nova parella. Amb les dures condicions de cria, una sola gavina no pot oferir prou cura, així que cal que ambdós progenitors alimentin i protegeixin els seus petits. La investigadora principal, Fionnuala McCully, estudiant de doctorat, explica: 'Les nostres troballes suggereixen que tenir personalitats similars facilita que els pares puguin anticipar el comportament de l’altre.' Els pares de gavina tridàctila sovint passen llargues temporades al mar buscant menjar, cosa que fa que hagin de prendre decisions de manera independent. Tenir personalitats similars facilita que les dues parts prenguin decisions més coordinades i previsibles. McCully assenyala que, igual que en les relacions humanes, la compatibilitat també sembla clau en les parelles animals. Les gavines tridàctiles viuen molts anys, fins als 30 o més. Normalment mantenen la mateixa parella, ja que trobar-ne una de nova és costós. El ‘divorci’ acostuma a succeir després de perdre un poll. Malgrat que són el tipus de gavina més comú, la població de gavines tridàctiles està disminuint arreu del món a causa del canvi climàtic i l’activitat humana com la sobrepesca, fent més difícil la supervivència dels polls. Els investigadors conclouen que, si no hi ha canvis en el comportament humà, ni tan sols una compatibilitat forta entre parelles serà suficient per assegurar el futur de l’espècie.

article_content: Swami Bhaktipada, a well-known leader in the American Hare Krishna movement who spent years in prison for criminal convictions before moving to India, died on Monday at age 74 from kidney failure in a hospital near Mumbai. Keith Ham, born in Peekskill, New York, in 1937, grew up as the son of a Baptist preacher. He became one of the earliest U.S. followers of Hare Krishna in 1966. Early on, he took steps to adapt the faith for Western practitioners, at times working independently of guidance from India. Together with Howard Morton Wheeler, he established New Vrindaban in West Virginia in 1968. The 4,000-acre community became the largest Hare Krishna center in the United States, with its renowned Palace of Gold, an ornate landmark now drawing many visitors along with its rose garden and organic farm. Both growth and significant controversy marked Bhaktipada’s leadership. In 1987, an FBI raid led to his and New Vrindaban’s expulsion from ISKCON. He was implicated in ordering two murders and in illegal fundraising schemes that raised more than $10 million. Although he first challenged his 1991 racketeering conviction, Bhaktipada later pleaded guilty, received a 20-year sentence (later reduced to 12 for health reasons), and was released in 2004 after serving eight years. He was prohibited from returning to New Vrindaban and resettled in India in 2008. Anuttama Dasa, a spokesperson for the community, acknowledged Bhaktipada’s early positive contributions but condemned his later serious violations. Currently, New Vrindaban hosts around 200 residents and welcomes about 25,000 annual visitors for festivals, pilgrimages, and retreats centered around its ornate palace.

KATHMANDU, Nepal — Nepal's government has decided to ban the popular social media app TikTok, citing concerns over its impact on social harmony in the country. The decision was made during a Cabinet meeting and announced by Foreign Minister Narayan Prakash Saud, who stated the ban would take effect immediately. 'The government has decided to ban TikTok as it was necessary to regulate the use of the social media platform that was disrupting social harmony, goodwill, and permitting the flow of indecent materials,' Saud said.

He added that the government has asked social media companies to register in Nepal, establish liaison offices, pay relevant taxes, and adhere to local laws and regulations to ensure accountability.

It remains unclear what specifically prompted the ban or whether TikTok had failed to meet Nepal’s requirements. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

TikTok, owned by Chinese firm ByteDance, has faced scrutiny in several countries over fears that the platform could be used by Beijing to access user data or further its own interests. Countries including the United States, Britain, and New Zealand have banned TikTok on government devices, despite the company saying it has never shared data with the Chinese government and would not do so if asked.

In 2018, Nepal also banned all pornographic websites.

article_content: Texas has taken a significant step to strengthen its research universities. With the approval of Proposition 5, voters established the Texas University Fund, a $3.9 billion endowment dedicated to boosting the state’s ‘emerging’ research institutions. This initiative provides Texas Tech University in Lubbock—and three other schools—with substantial new funding. Estimates suggest Texas Tech will receive $44 million in the first year, while the University of Houston could get $48 million, Texas State $22 million, and the University of North Texas $21 million. These universities were selected based on criteria such as spending at least $20 million annually on research and awarding 45 or more doctoral degrees on average over the last three years. The fund is financed mainly through a $3 billion allocation from Texas’s budget surplus, complemented by $900 million from a previous fund, and annual investment earnings from the state’s rainy day fund. There’s an annual cap of $100 million for fiscal 2024, with possible increases of up to 2% per year for inflation. Distribution formulas involve not only splitting funds among eligible institutions but also rewarding universities according to their research funding and doctorate output. Specifically, three-quarters of annual distributions go to Texas Tech and University of Houston (each receiving a third), while the other two universities share the remaining third. The other 25% is distributed based on each school's research achievements. Notably, the University of Texas and Texas A&M systems are not eligible for the TUF, as they already benefit from the older Permanent University Fund, valued at over $30 billion as of 2023. Supporters from both major parties, along with prominent economic groups and newspapers, praised Proposition 5, emphasizing that it requires no new taxes. Governor Greg Abbott celebrated the measure on social media, asserting that it will secure Texas’s position as a national leader in research universities. In parallel, House Bill 1595 was also enacted, ensuring oversight by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board in managing distributions and identifying eligible schools.

Aquesta iniciativa ofereix una nova finançació substancial a la Texas Tech University de Lubbock i a tres altres universitats. S’estima que Texas Tech rebrà 44 milions de dòlars el primer any, mentre que la University of Houston en podria rebre 48 milions, Texas State 22 milions i la University of North Texas 21 milions. article_content: This week, Alex Jones, presenter of The One Show, is taking on the daunting task of climbing the 1,200-foot Moonlight Buttress in Zion National Park, Utah—a route famous among climbers for its difficulty. The journey will last two and a half days, and at night, she'll attempt to rest in a tent hanging from the sandstone face, without access to basic comforts like washing, toilets, or much sleep. Previously inexperienced in climbing beyond ladders and trees, Alex was motivated to pursue this challenge after visiting the Philippines, where she witnessed the aftermath of Typhoon Haiyan. There, she saw the ongoing recovery efforts supported by Sport Relief funds. Typhoon Haiyan devastated Southeast Asia in November the previous year, killing thousands and leaving many residents homeless, especially in Tacloban. Alex met families like Delia's, who lost loved ones and all their belongings when tragedy struck. Alex observed how charities such as Oxfam and Save the Children, aided by contributions, were rebuilding homes using resources like fallen coconut trees. She helped in constructing a new wooden home for Delia and her daughters, witnessing their excitement as they settled in. The experience reinforced for Alex just how important charitable donations are, witnessing firsthand their transformation into materials, shelter, and hope. She found the chance to help, even in small ways, to be deeply rewarding. Now, Alex is more determined than ever to raise funds for these causes. She hopes her difficult mountain climb will inspire further public support, showing that donations can truly change lives. Supporters can follow her journey and efforts through Sport Relief and The One Show.

La travessa durarà dos dies i mig i durant les nits intentarà descansar en una tenda suspesa de la paret de roca, sense accés a comoditats bàsiques com una dutxa, bany o gairebé cap descans. Amb poc més experiència que escalar escales o arbres, l’Alex es va sentir motivada a assumir aquest repte arran d’un viatge a Filipines, on va presenciar les conseqüències del tifó Haiyan i la recuperació impulsada pels fons de Sport Relief. article_content: The Feng Yu Covered Bridge in Chongqing, China, widely recognized as the longest covered bridge in Asia, was destroyed by a fire last night. Stretching 303 metres across the Apeng River and topped by a traditional pagoda-style roof, the five-metre-wide structure had stood since its original construction in 1591. Made almost entirely of wood and built without nails, the bridge was celebrated for its intricate architectural details and artistic carvings, earning nicknames such as 'Luck Bridge' and 'Flower Bridge.' The bridge had been destroyed and rebuilt several times throughout its history, with the most recent restoration occurring in 1999, during which a stone base was added to reinforce the structure. Firefighters worked through the night to extinguish the blaze, but despite their efforts, the bridge collapsed and only a row of charred stone foundations remained by morning, surrounded by blackened driftwood floating in the river. Onlookers watched as the iconic landmark, a vital transportation link and gathering spot for merchants and tourists, was reduced to ashes. Authorities have launched an investigation to determine the cause of the fire.

Construït gairebé totalment de fusta i sense fer servir claus, el pont era conegut pels seus detalls arquitectònics intricats i les seves talles artístiques, i rebia sobrenoms com 'Pont de la Sort' i 'Pont de les Flors'. El pont s’havia destruït i reconstruït diverses vegades al llarg de la seva història, sent la més recent l’any 1999, quan es va afegir una base de pedra per reforçar-ne l’estructura. Els bombers van treballar durant tota la nit per apagar les flames, però, malgrat els seus esforços, el pont es va ensorrar i al matí només en quedaven una filera de fonaments de pedra carbonitzada envoltats de fusta negra surant al riu. Els espectadors van presenciar com aquest emblema icònic, un enllaç vital de transport i un lloc de trobada per a comerciants i turistes, quedava reduït a cendres. Les autoritats han obert una investigació per determinar-ne la causa de l’incendi.

article_content: Subaru introduced its Sports Mobility Concept, an all-electric two-door coupe, at the Japan Mobility Show on October 25. Although Subaru hasn’t revealed detailed technical specifications, the car’s bold design, all-wheel drive, and electric powertrain have led many to believe it could signal the direction of a new WRX rather than a BRZ successor. The concept’s rugged style and performance hints suggest a stronger connection to Subaru’s rally heritage. Stylistically, this concept pays homage to notable past Subaru models like the Alcyone SVX and the Impreza 22B STi. The vehicle features pronounced wheel arches, carbon-fiber paneling, blue accent trims, and a cockpit reminiscent of a fighter jet. Side mirrors have been replaced by cameras to improve aerodynamics and underline the concept’s forward-looking approach. Subaru confirmed that the Sports Mobility Concept uses a battery-electric, all-wheel-drive platform. The car probably employs a skateboard-type chassis with the battery packed under the cabin, a design known for aiding stability and handling. Given Subaru’s decades of rally experience and its joint development with Toyota on electric vehicles like the Solterra, it’s plausible this concept shares its platform with Toyota’s e-TNGA architecture, as does the Lexus RZ, which is powered by a 308-horsepower dual-motor system. Within the production-like cabin, the dashboard and controls draw inspiration from the Solterra EV. The vehicle sports a squared-off steering wheel, advanced EyeSight safety technology, adaptive cruise control, and integrated voice command features. There’s hope among Subaru enthusiasts that the concept borrows performance DNA from the radical STI E-RA prototype—a 1,073-horsepower electric racer developed to tackle the Nürburgring, although it hasn’t yet posted an official lap time. Innovations from that project could influence Subaru’s future electric sports cars. The Japan Mobility Show highlighted a broader trend, with other major Japanese automakers unveiling electrified versions of classic models: Mazda alluded to a rotary-hybrid RX-9, Nissan revealed a powerful electric GT-R, Honda brought back the Prelude, and Toyota previewed a futuristic MR2. Subaru, in turn, appears committed to maintaining the WRX legacy by transforming it for the electric age. If the Sports Mobility Concept makes it to production after 2026, fans have good reason for optimism.

article_content: Former UK Prime Minister David Cameron has returned to government as Foreign Secretary after Prime Minister Rishi Sunak’s cabinet reshuffle, with a general election on the horizon. Cameron’s appointment follows Sunak’s decision to dismiss Suella Braverman as Home Secretary, aiming to reinforce his leadership within the Conservative Party, which currently trails the Labour Party in opinion polls. James Cleverly, formerly Foreign Secretary, has been appointed as Home Secretary. Cameron resigned as Prime Minister in 2016 following the Brexit referendum defeat, left Parliament that year, and was later involved in a lobbying controversy with Greensill Capital. While Cameron’s foreign policy record is considered mixed, he stated that he accepted the new role to help the UK meet global challenges, including the Israel-Hamas conflict and the war in Ukraine. He will be made a life peer in the House of Lords to enable his return. The last life peer to be Foreign Secretary was Peter Carrington in 1982. Cameron led the UK's involvement in the 2011 intervention in Libya, leading to the fall of Muamar Khadhafi but was followed by instability in the country. In 2013, he was the first UK Prime Minister in over 150 years to lose a parliamentary vote on military action when MPs rejected his plan for strikes on Syria after a chemical attack. Cameron faced criticism in 2021 over his lobbying activities for Greensill Capital, and he and Sunak have differed publicly on major policies, including UK-China relations and high-speed rail development. Cameron’s return surprised political observers since Sunak had previously called for an end to the long-standing status quo in British politics. Tim Bale, a politics professor at Queen Mary University of London, noted that Sunak might seek to benefit from Cameron’s international experience and appeal to moderate voters, although doubts remain about the effectiveness of this move. September polling indicated that Cameron is viewed unfavourably by a notable proportion of UK adults. Braverman’s dismissal is seen as an effort to reposition the Conservative Party towards the centre ahead of the next election, due by January 2025. Braverman drew criticism after publishing an article without Sunak’s approval, leading to claims she encouraged far-right demonstrations. Downing Street initiated an investigation into the publication. Braverman, recognized for her strong views on asylum and homelessness, described her time as Home Secretary as a privilege and signaled that she would comment further in the future. Meanwhile, Indian tax authorities are investigating the local operations of Apple, Google, and Amazon over transfer pricing and possible unpaid taxes. Indians have become the largest group of real estate buyers in Dubai. Razorpay, a digital payments company, is planning to relocate its parent company to India through a cross-country merger, which may result in significant US tax payments. (Originally published on 13 November 2023)

article_content: Up to 11 trees at the Dark Hedges, a famous beauty spot in Northern Ireland popularized by the fantasy drama Game of Thrones, may need to be cut down. The Dark Hedges, a striking tunnel of beech trees near Armoy, County Antrim, has become a tourist hotspot after appearing in the show. A recent report has found that most of these trees are in poor condition, with one already dead. This poses health and safety risks for visitors. The report, commissioned by the Department of Infrastructure and carried out by Tree Safety experts, concluded that 11 trees should be removed, as reported by the Coleraine Chronicle. Because six of the trees are protected, permission from the Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council is required for their removal. The council is set to discuss the issue later on Wednesday. The trees were originally planted along Bregagh Road to Gracehill House, which was built around 1775. About 150 trees were originally planted, but only about 80 remain today. Many are considered past maturity, leading to frequent branch breakages. In recent years, several trees have fallen due to strong winds from storms. The Dark Hedges have grown in popularity since being used as a filming location in the HBO series Game of Thrones. The Save the Dark Hedges campaign group has expressed concern that increased traffic and visitor numbers have accelerated damage to the trees. Rob McCallion, from the campaign, said: 'If action isn't taken, someone could be seriously injured or killed because of the state of the trees.' DUP councillor and Dark Hedges Preservation Trust member Mervyn Storey echoed these concerns, stating, 'No one wants to see the end of what is known as the Dark Hedges. There was never any funding for a significant replanting program, and I fear it may now be too late.'

article_content: Apple TV+ is raising its subscription prices, following similar increases from other streaming services like Netflix. Starting immediately, the monthly price rises from $6.99 to $9.99, and the annual plan increases from $69 to $99. According to statements reported by the Hollywood Reporter and other outlets, Apple emphasized its achievements since launching in 2019, including a wide selection of award-winning series, movies, documentaries, and family content. Unlike competitors such as Netflix, Apple TV+ still does not offer a less expensive ad-supported plan, although reports suggest the company may consider this in the future. Additionally, other Apple services are also seeing price increases: Apple Arcade now costs $6.99 a month (up from $4.99), Apple News+ will rise to $12.99 per month (from $9.99), and Apple One bundle prices are increasing as well. The individual tier is going from $16.95 to $19.95, the family tier from $22.95 to $25.95, and the premier tier from $32.95 to $37.95. The new prices take effect immediately for new subscribers and will apply to existing customers at their next billing cycle.

article_content: COLOMBO: Sri Lanka's central bank resumed cutting interest rates on Thursday to stimulate economic growth as the government seeks to increase revenue and repair its balance sheet to maintain ongoing support from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) lowered the standing deposit facility rate and the standing lending facility rate by 100 basis points each, to 10 percent and 11 percent respectively, according to a statement. The move comes after the CBSL kept rates unchanged at its last policy meeting in August. "The Board arrived at this decision following a careful analysis of current and expected developments," the statement read. The rate cut matched market expectations and follows a period of declining inflation. Last year, Sri Lanka faced its most severe financial crisis in over seventy years. Inflation soared and foreign currency reserves fell to record lows, severely restricting the country’s ability to import essential goods. The central bank responded by raising rates by a total of 10.5 percentage points in an effort to control inflation and rebuild reserves to stabilize the currency. Since June, CBSL has cut rates by a total of 550 basis points, as economic conditions stabilized following the $2.9 billion IMF bailout package secured in March. After the rate cut, the prices of Sri Lankan international bonds rose, with the May 2027 maturity bond leading the gains. Finalising the IMF review is crucial. Sri Lanka missed reaching an agreement with the IMF during the first review of the bailout last month, primarily due to concerns over government revenue. This could delay the release of the second tranche of $330 million under the rescue plan. CBSL Governor P. Nandalal Weerasinghe stated the country aims to complete the first review by late October and seek IMF Board approval in November. Udeeshan Jonas, chief strategist at CAL Group, said, "Growth alone isn’t enough, and monetary policy is the only way to stimulate it." He observed that even with more accommodative policies, Sri Lanka may still experience a contraction of around 2% this year. Stronger growth would also increase imports, thereby raising potential tax revenues. Imports declined about 14% to $11 billion in the first eight months of this year compared to 2022. Thilina Panduwawala, head of research at Frontier Research, noted that the CBSL is reducing lending rates and hopes they will fall to levels where borrowing and investment increase meaningfully. Weerasinghe added that the current favorable price outlook should help keep inflation at 5% in the medium term, as mandated by the new Central Bank Act, allowing the economy to reach its growth potential. However, he cautioned that rising global oil prices and possible new tax measures in the upcoming federal budget in November may temporarily push prices higher. Over the past six months, Sri Lanka has seen inflation drop to 1.3% as of September, its currency appreciate by about 12%, and foreign reserves rise. The World Bank revised its economic outlook for Sri Lanka this week, now predicting the economy will contract by 3.8% in 2023 instead of 4.2%. The CBSL forecasts a 2% contraction. The central bank reiterated its desire for further declines in market interest rates and expressed optimism for progress in debt restructuring negotiations soon. "The CBSL will continue to closely monitor developments in market lending interest rates and review administrative measures as needed," the statement concluded.
translated_content: COLONBO: El banc central de Sri Lanka ha reprès la rebaixa dels tipus d'interès aquest dijous per estimular el creixement econòmic, mentre el govern busca augmentar els ingressos i sanejar els seus comptes per mantenir l'ajuda contínua del Fons Monetari Internacional (FMI). El Banc Central de Sri Lanka (CBSL) ha reduït el tipus d'interès de la facilitat de dipòsits i el de la facilitat de préstecs en 100 punts bàsics cadascun, fins al 10% i l'11% respectivament, segons un comunicat. Aquesta decisió arriba després que el CBSL mantingués sense canvis els tipus en la darrera reunió de política monetària a l'agost. "La Junta ha pres aquesta decisió després d'una acurada anàlisi dels esdeveniments actuals i previstos", recull el comunicat. La rebaixa era esperada pel mercat i arriba després d'un període d'inflació a la baixa. L'any passat, Sri Lanka va afrontar la seva crisi financera més greu en més de setanta anys. La inflació es va disparar i les reserves de divises van caure a mínims històrics, dificultant molt la importació de béns essencials. El banc central va respondre pujant els tipus un total de 10,5 punts percentuals per controlar la inflació i reconstruir reserves per estabilitzar la moneda. Des del juny, el CBSL ha rebaixat els tipus en un total de 550 punts bàsics, mentre la situació s'ha estabilitzat després del rescat del FMI de 2.900 milions de dòlars aconseguit al març. Després de la rebaixa, el preu dels bons internacionals de Sri Lanka va augmentar, destacant el bo amb venciment el maig del 2027. Finalitzar la revisió de l'FMI és clau. Sri Lanka no va arribar a un acord amb l'FMI en la primera revisió del rescat el mes passat a causa, principalment, de dubtes sobre els ingressos estatals. Això podria endarrerir el lliurament del segon tram de 330 milions de dòlars del pla. El governador del CBSL, P. Nandalal Weerasinghe, ha afirmat que el país vol completar la revisió al final d'octubre i obtenir l'aprovació de la Junta de l'FMI al novembre. Udeeshan Jonas, estratèg en cap de CAL Group, ha dit: "Només el creixement no n'hi ha prou, i la política monetària és l'única via per incentivar-lo". Ha assenyalat que, fins i tot amb polítiques més laxes, Sri Lanka podria patir una contracció d'un 2% enguany. Un creixement més fort també augmentaria les importacions i, així, els ingressos fiscals. Les importacions han baixat un 14% fins als 11.000 milions de dòlars en els primers vuit mesos de l'any respecte al 2022. Thilina Panduwawala, cap de recerca a Frontier Research, ha remarcat que el CBSL està reduint els tipus dels crèdits i confia que arribin a nivells que estimulin préstecs i inversions de manera significativa. Weerasinghe ha afegit que l'actual entorn de preus favorable hauria d'ajudar a mantenir la inflació en el 5% a mitjà termini, com estableix la nova llei del Banc Central, permetent així assolir el potencial de creixement econòmic. Tanmateix, ha advertit que la pujada global dels preus del petroli i noves mesures fiscals previstes als pressupostos de novembre podrien incrementar els preus temporalment. En els últims sis mesos, Sri Lanka ha vist la seva inflació reduir-se fins a l'1,3% al setembre, la moneda revalorar-se un 12% i augmentar les reserves de divises. El Banc Mundial ha revisat a l'alça les seves previsions econòmiques per al país aquesta setmana i ara preveu una contracció del 3,8% en 2023, davant del 4,2% anterior. El CBSL preveu una contracció del 2%. El banc central ha reiterat la voluntat que els tipus baixin encara més i s'ha mostrat optimista amb els avenços en les negociacions pel reestructurament del deute. "El CBSL continuarà monitoritzant de prop l'evolució dels tipus dels crèdits i revisarà les mesures administratives quan calgui", conclou el comunicat.

article_content: Before Ellen DeGeneres made coming out mainstream on TV and before straight male actors would even consider playing gay roles, there was Leslie Feinberg, a pioneering transgender activist. Feinberg’s 1993 novel, 'Stone Butch Blues,' is difficult to find today, but it remains a vital testament to LGBTQ+ experiences. The protagonist of 'Stone Butch Blues' begins life as a girl and explores identities as lesbian, butch, and ultimately as a man during the 1960s and 1970s. Feinberg wrote, 'There's more than just neither, honey. There are other ways to be besides either-or. It's not that simple. Otherwise, there wouldn’t be so many people who don’t fit.' Like those who stood up against police brutality at the Stonewall Inn in 1969, there was no closet big enough to contain Feinberg. Feinberg passed away on November 15 at age 65, at home in Syracuse, New York, due to complications from several infections, her spouse Minnie Bruce Pratt told The Advocate. At the time of her death, Feinberg was working on the 20th anniversary edition of 'Stone Butch Blues.' Reading 'Stone Butch Blues' in the early 1990s, the environment for LGBTQ+ people was much harder. Living openly was dangerous, protection from discrimination was limited, and many had to hide their identities. Feinberg and other activists—transgender people, butch women, gay men, and drag queens—could not or would not fade into the shadows, paving the way for others. Feinberg’s example taught me the importance of living authentically and contributing to ongoing activism. As a writer and journalist, I came out in college, stayed out in graduate school, and have always been open about my identity in my profession. I’ve worked to bridge gaps among journalists of different backgrounds. Activist Candace Gingrich reflected on Feinberg’s impact: 'Reading 'Stone Butch Blues' in '93 and later 'Transgender Warriors,' I was able to recognize and name my own gender queerness. Feinberg’s quote, 'Gender is the poetry each of us makes out of the language we are taught,' captures a truth that many trans and genderqueer people live every day.' Although I did not know Feinberg personally, I respected the broad range of her political activism. She fought for workers' rights, marched against racism, protested the Klan, and supported abortion rights in upstate New York. To Feinberg, fights for equality were interconnected and required solidarity. Ina Fried, a transgender journalist, commented: 'Feinberg’s real-life struggle for justice, especially economic justice, was her life’s work and passion. With her passing, it’s up to us to continue making the world fairer.' Despite progress, discrimination persists. In some places, people can still be fired or denied marriage rights because of their identity. But thanks to Feinberg and others, I am not afraid. That is Feinberg’s legacy to me, and to you.

La novel·la de Feinberg de 1993, ‘Stone Butch Blues’, és difícil de trobar avui dia, però segueix essent un testimoni essencial de les experiències LGBTQ+. La protagonista de ‘Stone Butch Blues’ comença la vida com a noia i explora identitats com a lesbiana, butch i finalment com a home als anys 60 i 70. Igual que les persones que van plantar cara a la brutalitat policial a l’Stonewall Inn el 1969, no hi havia cap armari prou gran per a contenir Feinberg. Feinberg va morir el 15 de novembre als 65 anys a casa seva, a Syracuse (Nova York), a causa de complicacions de diverses infeccions, segons va dir la seva esposa, Minnie Bruce Pratt, a The Advocate. En el moment de la seva mort, Feinberg treballava en l’edició del 20è aniversari de ‘Stone Butch Blues’. Llegir ‘Stone Butch Blues’ a principis dels anys 90, el context per a les persones LGBTQ+ era molt més difícil. Viure obertament era perillós, la protecció contra la discriminació era limitada i moltes persones havien d’amagar la seva identitat. Feinberg i altres activistes—persones transgènere, dones butch, homes gais i drag queens—no podien o no volien desaparèixer entre les ombres, obrint camí per a la resta. L’exemple de Feinberg em va ensenyar la importància de viure amb autenticitat i contribuir a l’activisme. Com a escriptora i periodista, vaig sortir de l’armari a la universitat, vaig continuar fora en el postgrau i sempre he estat oberta sobre la meva identitat en la meva professió. He treballat per superar les diferències entre periodistes de diferents orígens. L’activista Candace Gingrich va reflexionar sobre l’impacte de Feinberg: ‘Llegint ‘Stone Butch Blues’ el 93 i més tard ‘Transgender Warriors’, vaig poder reconèixer i posar nom a la meva pròpia queeritat de gènere. La frase de Feinberg, 'El gènere és la poesia que cadascú fa del llenguatge que ens han ensenyat', resumeix una veritat que moltes persones trans i genderqueer viuen cada dia’. Tot i que no vaig conèixer Feinberg personalment, n’admirava l’amplitud de l’activisme polític. Va lluitar pels drets laborals, va manifestar-se contra el racisme, va protestar contra el Klan i va defensar el dret a l’avortament a Nova York. Per a Feinberg, les lluites per la igualtat estaven totes connectades i reclamaven solidaritat. Ina Fried, periodista transgènere, va comentar: ‘L’autèntica lluita per la justícia, especialment la justícia econòmica, va ser el gran treball i la passió de la seva vida. En alguns llocs, encara et poden acomiadar o denegar el dret a casar-te per la teva identitat. Però gràcies a Feinberg i una altra gent, ja no sento por. Aquesta és la seva herència per a mi, i per a tothom.
