article_content: A young man jingles a stack of coins, organizes his passengers onto the bus with efficiency, then knocks on the side to signal departure. We head off, rattling down the busy, dusty road in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania’s largest city and a place President Obama visited during his July trip to East Africa. The man is the conductor of a 'dala dala'—one of the many colorful minibuses that travel along Dar es Salaam’s main routes each day. While visitors often overlook Dar es Salaam in favor of Tanzania’s famous tourist destinations, the city has its own appeal for those willing to experience local life. The heat, heavy traffic, and dust can be challenging, but there is a certain charm. For those interested in 'Bongo Flava'—Tanzania’s own blend of R&B and hip-hop, which started in Dar—the dala dalas offer a lively ride. The buses get their name from a slang term for five Tanzanian shillings ('dala' meaning 'dollar'), the cost of a trip in the 1970s and 1980s when dala dalas first appeared as private solutions to inadequate public transport. Today, a standard dala dala ride costs about 400 shillings (roughly 25 cents), with prices varying for longer journeys. Each bus is a mobile canvas, painted in vibrant patterns that show its route. Dala dalas have become part of Tanzanian popular culture, even featuring in TV shows where passengers discuss current issues on their way to work. Exploring the city by dala dala is a unique experience. Despite the cramped and hot conditions, the atmosphere is welcoming. For example, when I asked how to reach Kariakoo market, a nearby passenger—who turned out to be a fisherman on his day off—offered to walk with me. We chatted on the way about Tanzania’s football World Cup qualification hopes and the best fishing spots. Kariakoo market, spread across several blocks and housed in a distinctive building from the 1970s, is considered East Africa’s largest. Its ground floor bustles with hardware vendors, while a large basement serves as a center for fruit and vegetable traders. Above ground, you’ll find a lively mix of goods—tools, food, traditional bows and arrows, and plenty of street food. Dar es Salaam’s street food reflects both Tanzanian agriculture and Indian influence, offering dishes like chipsi mayai (fries in an omelet), samosas, chapatti, roasted corn with chili and lime, mandazi (doughnut-like pastries), sugarcane, and various tropical fruits. Drinks range from fresh coconut juice to coffee served by the city’s famous street vendors. As a port city, Dar is also known for its seafood; the main fish market, accessible by dala dala, is noisy and full of activity, with boats anchored at one end and freshly cooked seafood at the other. Each dala dala reflects its owner's preferences, often shown in slogans on the windshield. These range from religious phrases ('Allah Akbar', 'Jesus Power') to sports allegiances ('Liverpool Forever') or personal mottos. The buses can be likened to the Philippines’ jeepneys for their personalized decorations. One route passes Dar’s old colonial buildings from both German and British eras—preserved and still in use by the government—along with impressive cathedrals. Adjacent is the Asian Quarter, Kisutu, featuring Art Deco buildings, mosques, Hindu temples, and a diverse mix of attire, from Indian saris to Tanzanian kangas. The Sapphire Hotel roof terrace offers panoramic views of the city’s modern high-rises contrasted with older and poorer neighborhoods. A final dala dala trip to Msasani Peninsula reveals Dar’s rapid recent development. Once sparsely populated, Msasani is now a hub of marinas, luxury apartments, and upmarket shopping and dining, home to many wealthy residents and expatriates. Outside these establishments, Maasai security guards are a common sight—members of the pastoralist Maasai tribe who have moved to the city for work due to challenges such as drought. Dar es Salaam is a city of striking contrasts, but thanks to the dala dala network, it is an accessible, worthwhile stop on any visit to Tanzania. Tips for catching a dala dala: Stand near a bus stop—there’s no schedule, but buses usually come every 10 minutes, depending on traffic. Standard fare is 400 shillings. Key stops in central Dar include Posta (city center), Fire (near the Fire Station by Kariakoo), and Kivukoni (for the fish market and waterfront). Dala dalas to Kivukoni are painted green, while those for Msasani or Mwenge have blue markings. Ask fellow passengers or the conductor if you’re unsure of your stop.

Arrenquem, traquetejant pels carrers plens de gent i pols de Dar es Salaam, la ciutat més gran de Tanzània, i que va rebre la visita del president Obama durant el seu viatge a l’Àfrica de l’Est al juliol. L’home és el revisor d’un 'dala dala', un dels molts minibusos acolorits que circulen diàriament per les rutes principals de Dar es Salaam. Tot i que sovint els visitants passen de llarg en favor de les destinacions turístiques més famoses de Tanzània, la ciutat té un encant especial per aquells disposats a viure la vida local. La calor, el trànsit intens i la pols poden ser difícils, però hi ha un cert atractiu. Per als qui volen descobrir la 'Bongo Flava'—la barreja tanzana de R&B i hip-hop, nascuda a Dar—els dala dala ofereixen un viatge animat. Els busos deuen el nom a un mot d’argot per a cinc xílings tanzans ('dala' que vol dir 'dòlar'), el preu d’un viatge durant els anys 70 i 80, quan els dala dala van emergir com a solució privada davant la manca de transport públic. Actualment, un viatge estàndard en dala dala costa prop de 400 xílings (uns 25 cèntims d’euro), amb preus més alts si el trajecte és llarg. Cada bus és una autèntica obra d’art mòbil, pintada amb dissenys cridaners que n’indiquen la ruta. Són tan emblemàtics que han arribat a aparèixer en programes de TV on els passatgers discuteixen l’actualitat mentre van a la feina. Explorar la ciutat amb dala dala és una experiència singular. Tot i les condicions atapeïdes i caloroses, l’ambient és acollidor. Per exemple, quan vaig preguntar com arribar al mercat de Kariakoo, un passatger al costat—que resulta ser pescador en dia lliure—es va oferir a acompanyar-me. Pel camí vam xerrar sobre la classificació de Tanzània pel Mundial de futbol i els millors llocs per pescar. El mercat de Kariakoo, que ocupa diversos blocs i està situat en un edifici emblemàtic dels anys 70, és considerat el més gran de l’Àfrica oriental. La planta baixa bull d’activitat amb venedors de ferreteria, mentre que el gran soterrani acull comerciants de fruita i verdura. A nivell de carrer hi trobareu una varietat de productes—eines, menjar, arcs i fletxes tradicionals, i molt menjar de carrer. El menjar de carrer de Dar reflecteix tant l’agricultura tanzana com la influència índia, amb plats com el chipsi mayai (fregides dins una truita), samoses, chapatti, blat de moro torrat amb bitxo i llima, mandazi (dolços semblants a un dònut), canya de sucre i fruita tropical. Entre les begudes destaquen el suc de coco acabat d’obrir o el cafè servit pels famosos venedors ambulants. Com a ciutat portuària, el peix i marisc són típics; el principal mercat de peix, accessible amb dala dala, és sorollós i ple de vida, amb barques al port d’un extrem i plats acabats de fer a l’altre. Cada dala dala reflecteix els gustos del seu propietari, sovint mostrats en els eslògans del parabrisa. Aquests inclouen frases religioses ('Allah Akbar', 'Jesus Power'), preferències esportives ('Liverpool Forever') o lemes personals. Es poden comparar amb els jeepneys de les Filipines per la seva decoració personalitzada. Algunes línies passen pels antics edificis colonials de Dar de l’època alemanya i britànica—encara en ús pel govern—així com per catedrals imponents. Just després hi ha el barri asiàtic, Kisutu, ple d’edificis Art Deco, mesquites, temples hindús i una gran diversitat d’indumentària, des de saris indis fins a kangues tanzanes. La terrassa de l’Hotel Sapphire ofereix vistes panoràmiques dels nous gratacels que contrasten amb barris més antics i humils. Un darrer trajecte amb dala dala fins a la península de Msasani mostra el ràpid desenvolupament que ha viscut Dar. Abans poc habitat, Msasani és avui el centre de ports esportius, apartaments de luxe, botigues sofisticades i restaurants, on viuen molts rics i expatriats. Davant aquests locals, sovint hi trobareu guardes de seguretat maasai—membres de la coneguda tribu pastoral que ha migrat a la ciutat per raons com la sequera. Dar es Salaam és una ciutat de contrastos notoris, però gràcies a la xarxa de dala dala, és una parada accessible i que val la pena durant una visita a Tanzània. Consells per pujar a un dala dala: Para’t a prop d’una parada—no hi ha horaris, però solen passar cada 10 minuts depenent del trànsit. El preu estàndard és de 400 xílings. Els principals punts del centre són Posta (al centre), Fire (proper a la caserna dels bombers, a tocar de Kariakoo) i Kivukoni (per al mercat de peix i la zona marítima). Els dala dala cap a Kivukoni van pintats de verd; els de Msasani o Mwenge, de blau. Si tens dubtes, pregunta a altres passatgers o al revisor.

article_content: India’s Supreme Court is preparing to hear two petitions from the governments of Tamil Nadu and Kerala, both asserting that their respective governors have delayed signing off on laws passed by the state assemblies. A panel headed by Chief Justice D Y Chandrachud, with Justices J B Pardiwala and Manoj Misra, will consider the cases. In Tamil Nadu’s situation, the state assembly recently passed ten bills for a second time after Governor R N Ravi initially returned them. These measures address issues such as law, agriculture, and higher education. The bills have now been re-submitted to the governor for approval, after being sent back on November 13. The Supreme Court has already labeled the actions of Tamil Nadu’s governor a 'serious concern,' and has asked the central government for its take on the state’s claim that the governor’s office is stalling 12 bills and various important matters, including sanctioning prosecutions and appointments. Under Article 200 of the Indian Constitution, governors are required to either assent to, reserve for the President, or withhold their assent from bills passed by the legislative assembly. Tamil Nadu argues that the governor’s repeated delays are arbitrary, unconstitutional, and block the smooth running of government. Their legal filing accuses the governor of failing to process everyday files and important approvals, which, they claim, disrupts the entire administrative machinery. In a similar vein, the Kerala government alleges that Governor Arif Mohammed Khan has not granted assent to eight bills, with three having been stalled for over two years. Kerala claims these delays are denying valuable welfare programs to citizens and threaten the principles of law and democracy. Both states are urging the Supreme Court to address what they call grave constitutional violations by the governors, asserting these delays undermine state governance and constitutional obligations.
translated_content: El Tribunal Suprem de l’Índia es prepara per escoltar dues peticions dels governs de Tamil Nadu i Kerala, que afirmen que els seus respectius governadors han retardat la signatura de lleis aprovades per les assemblees estatals. Un tribunal presidit pel jutge en cap D Y Chandrachud, juntament amb els jutges J B Pardiwala i Manoj Misra, considerarà els casos. En el cas de Tamil Nadu, l’assemblea va aprovar recentment deu lleis per segona vegada després que el governador R N Ravi les tornés inicialment. Aquestes normes aborden qüestions com el dret, l’agricultura i l’educació superior. Ara han estat reenviades al governador per a la seva aprovació, després de ser retornades el 13 de novembre. El Tribunal Suprem ja ha qualificat de 'preocupació seriosa' les accions del governador de Tamil Nadu, i ha demanat al govern central la seva opinió sobre la queixa de l’estat, que denuncia que l’oficina del governador està bloquejant dotze lleis i altres qüestions importants, com ara el vistiplau per a processaments i nomenaments. L’Article 200 de la Constitució índia exigeix que els governadors aprovin, reservin per al president o deneguin l’aprovació de les lleis que aprovi l’assemblea legislativa. Tamil Nadu manté que els retards constants del governador són arbitraris, inconstitucionals i obstaculitzen el funcionament del govern. El seu recurs judicial acusa el governador de no tramitar expedients diaris i autoritzacions importants, provocant, segons afirmen, el col·lapse de tota la maquinària administrativa. De la mateixa manera, el govern de Kerala denuncia que el governador Arif Mohammed Khan no ha signat vuit lleis, tres de les quals fa més de dos anys que estan aturades. Kerala defensa que aquests retards priven la ciutadania de programes socials clau i posen en risc principis bàsics legals i democràtics. Els dos estats demanen al Tribunal Suprem que intervingui davant el que consideren greus vulneracions constitucionals per part dels governadors, ja que aquests retards comprometen la governabilitat i els deures constitucionals.

article_content: Yemen's wounded president, Ali Abdullah Saleh, is recovering in Saudi Arabia, but doctors have recommended that he stay longer for further treatment, an adviser said on Friday. Meanwhile, thousands of anti-government protesters demonstrated across Yemen as an explosion at a military checkpoint in Aden killed five people. Officials from Yemen’s ruling party had previously claimed that President Saleh would return home Friday from Saudi Arabia, where he has been receiving treatment since he was wounded in a June 3 attack on the presidential palace. Senior presidential adviser Ahmed Al-Soufi stated, 'Doctors recommended that President Saleh stay in Saudi Arabia for a longer time. They said that Saleh's health is improving. The health of President Saleh is important to us, and we hope he will be here within days.' The largest demonstrations were reported in Sanaa, Taiz, Hodieda, and Ibb provinces, where protesters denounced what they saw as U.S. and Saudi interference in Yemeni affairs. Protesters chanted slogans such as, 'The people reject U.S. interference' and 'the revolution will prevail.' Sabreen Ariki, a leading figure in the Youth Revolutionary Movement in Taiz, said, 'We want the revolution to succeed, and the U.S. is not making this possible. It is harming the revolution, but we will continue protesting until our demands are met.' Members of the Revolution Youth Organizing Committee, part of the broader Youth Revolutionary Movement, condemned both Saudi Arabia and the United States, citing negative influence on Yemen and vowing not to forget their stance against the revolution. Waseem Qirshi, a committee representative, claimed, 'The Saudi stance is against the will of the people and serves their own interests, disregarding the needs of the Yemeni population.' At the same time, tens of thousands of Saleh’s supporters rallied in Sanaa, urging the international community to respect Yemen's constitution and its president. In New York, the U.N. Security Council voiced 'grave concern' over Yemen’s deteriorating security and humanitarian situation on Friday, calling on all parties to exercise restraint and engage in inclusive political dialogue. The U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights is scheduled to visit Yemen from June 27 to July 6. Investigations continue into the June 3 attack at Yemen's presidential palace mosque, which injured Saleh and other senior officials. Separately, a security official reported that four soldiers and a civilian died in a car bomb attack near a military compound in Aden. The attack occurred about 500 meters from a military base housing multiple army tanks; the official requested anonymity, as he was not authorized to speak to media. Yemen has experienced months of unrest, with protestors calling for Saleh’s resignation. Recent clashes have involved government troops, anti-government tribal forces, and Islamic militants, including al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula. The United States has provided support to Yemen’s military in its fight against Islamic militants, amid concerns that al Qaeda could exploit the political turmoil and create further instability in the region. As a result of the violence, approximately 45,000 people have been displaced in southern Yemen, particularly in Aden, Lahj, and Abyan provinces, according to estimates from the U.N. Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs.
translated_content: El president del Iemen ferit, Ali Abdullah Saleh, es recupera a l'Aràbia Saudita, però els metges han recomanat que s'hi quedi més temps per continuar el tractament, segons un assessor aquest divendres. Mentrestant, milers de manifestants antigovernamentals van protestar arreu del Iemen mentre una explosió en un control militar a Aden matava cinc persones. Funcionaris del partit governant del Iemen havien afirmat prèviament que el president Saleh tornaria a casa divendres des de l'Aràbia Saudita, on ha estat rebent tractament des que va resultar ferit en un atac al palau presidencial el 3 de juny. L'assessor presidencial sènior Ahmed Al-Soufi va declarar: 'Els metges han recomanat que el president Saleh es quedi a l'Aràbia Saudita durant més temps. Han dit que la salut de Saleh millora. La salut del president Saleh és important per a nosaltres i esperem que estigui aquí en pocs dies.' Les manifestacions més multitudinàries van tenir lloc a Sanaa, Taiz, Hodieda i Ibb, on els manifestants van denunciar la interferència dels Estats Units i l'Aràbia Saudita en els afers iemenites. Els manifestants van cridar consignes com ara: 'El poble rebutja la interferència dels EUA' i 'La revolució triomfarà'. Sabreen Ariki, una de les líders del Moviment Juvenil Revolucionari de Taiz, va dir: 'Volem que la revolució triomfi i els EUA no ho estan permetent. Estan perjudicant la revolució, però nosaltres continuarem protestant fins que es compleixin les nostres demandes.' Membres del Comitè Organitzador de la Joventut Revolucionària, dins del moviment més ampli, van condemnar tant l'Aràbia Saudita com els Estats Units per la seva influència negativa al Iemen i van prometre no oblidar la seva postura contra la revolució. Waseem Qirshi, representant del comitè, va afirmar: 'La posició saudita va en contra de la voluntat del poble i serveix els seus propis interessos, ignorant les necessitats de la població iemenita.' Al mateix temps, desenes de milers de seguidors de Saleh es van concentrar a Sanaa exigint a la comunitat internacional que respecti la constitució iemenita i el seu president. A Nova York, el Consell de Seguretat de l’ONU va expressar 'gran preocupació' per la deterioració de la seguretat i la situació humanitària al Iemen divendres, demanant a totes les parts que mostrin moderació i participin en un diàleg polític inclusiu. L'Alt Comissionat de l’ONU per als Drets Humans té previst visitar el Iemen del 27 de juny al 6 de juliol. Les investigacions continuen sobre l’atac del 3 de juny a la mesquita del palau presidencial del Iemen, que va ferir Saleh i altres alts funcionaris. D'altra banda, un oficial de seguretat va informar que quatre soldats i un civil van morir en un atemptat amb cotxe bomba prop d'un complex militar a Aden. L'atac va ocórrer a uns 500 metres d'una base on hi ha tancs de l'exèrcit; l'oficial va demanar l'anonimat ja que no estava autoritzat a parlar amb la premsa. El Iemen ha patit mesos d'inestabilitat, amb manifestants exigint la dimissió de Saleh. En les últimes setmanes, hi ha hagut enfrontaments entre tropes governamentals, forces tribals antigovernamentals i militants islàmics, inclòs Al-Qaida de la Península Aràbiga. Els Estats Units han prestat suport a l’exèrcit iemenita en la seva lluita contra els militants islàmics, preocupats perquè Al-Qaida aprofiti el caos i la inestabilitat política de la regió. Com a conseqüència de la violència, aproximadament 45.000 persones han estat desplaçades al sud del Iemen, especialment a les províncies d'Aden, Lahj i Abyan, segons l'Oficina de l'ONU per a la Coordinació d'Afers Humanitaris.

article_content:
In a landmark court decision regarding the rights of unmarried couples, a man has been ordered to pay his former partner £28,500. David Southwell, 55, was found liable after a judge determined he had promised Catherine Blackburn the same housing security a wife would receive. Southwell maintained that he never planned to marry Blackburn or made promises at the start of their relationship, which began in 2000. However, the court heard that Southwell, a businessman, purchased a £240,000 home in Droitwich, Worcestershire, and paid off a £100,000 mortgage, insisting the property remain solely in his name.

After their relationship ended acrimoniously in 2012, Blackburn and her two daughters were left without stable accommodation. Judge Daniel Pearce-Higgins QC characterized Southwell as shrewd and cautious, noting that he avoided marriage with Blackburn due to potential future claims on his assets. The court found Southwell had repeatedly reassured Blackburn of her security in the home as part of a long-term commitment.

Lord Justice Tomlinson, upholding the original ruling and dismissing Southwell's appeal, stated that it would be 'unconscionable' for Southwell to renege on these assurances. The court observed that Blackburn gave up her job and home to move in with Southwell, investing her savings into their life together based on his promises. Southwell reportedly kept Blackburn from any paperwork regarding ownership, despite promising her the security of a spouse.

The case highlights the vulnerabilities faced by unmarried cohabiting partners who, despite long-term commitments, lack the legal protections of marriage. The court concluded that Blackburn had entrusted her housing, employment, and independence to Southwell and suffered significant losses when the relationship ended.

En una decisió judicial històrica sobre els drets de les parelles no casades, un home ha estat obligat a pagar a la seva exparella 28.500 lliures. David Southwell, de 55 anys, ha estat considerat responsable després que un jutge determinés que havia promès a Catherine Blackburn la mateixa seguretat residencial que tindria una esposa. Southwell va afirmar que mai no havia planejat casar-se amb Blackburn ni li havia fet cap promesa al principi de la relació, que va començar l’any 2000. Malgrat això, el tribunal va escoltar que Southwell, un home de negocis, va comprar una casa de 240.000 lliures a Droitwich, Worcestershire, i va pagar una hipoteca de 100.000 lliures, insistint que la propietat quedés sols al seu nom.

Després que la seva relació finalitzés de manera complicada el 2012, Blackburn i les seves dues filles es van quedar sense allotjament estable. El jutge Daniel Pearce-Higgins QC va descriure Southwell com a prudent i calculador, destacant que va evitar el matrimoni per possibles reclamacions posteriors als seus béns. El tribunal va determinar que Southwell havia assegurat repetidament a Blackburn la seva seguretat domiciliària com a part d’un compromís a llarg termini.

El jutge Lord Justice Tomlinson, ratificant la sentència original i desestimant el recurs de Southwell, va declarar que seria «inconscient» que Southwell es fes enrere en aquestes garanties. El tribunal va observar que Blackburn va deixar la feina i la seva casa per anar a viure amb Southwell, invertint els seus estalvis en la vida conjunta basant-se en les seves promeses. Es diu que Southwell va mantenir Blackburn allunyada de tota documentació relacionada amb la propietat, tot i haver-li promès la seguretat d’una esposa.

Aquest cas posa de manifest la vulnerabilitat de les parelles no casades que, tot i tenir un compromís a llarg termini, no compten amb les mateixes proteccions legals que el matrimoni. El tribunal va concloure que Blackburn havia confiat la seva llar, feina i independència a Southwell i va patir pèrdues significatives quan la relació es va acabar.

article_content: The International Cricket Council (ICC) has acknowledged it cannot intervene in the ongoing dispute between the West Indies Cricket Board (WICB) and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). The crisis began when the West Indies team prematurely withdrew from matches during their tour of India, leading the BCCI to start legal action against the WICB and suspend future series. Given the WICB's already unstable financial situation, the risk of large financial penalties or the loss of Indian tours could threaten the survival of West Indies cricket. A recent change in ICC governance, which shifted executive power to the boards of India, England, and Australia, means the ICC no longer has the authority to intervene in such bilateral disputes. In a statement, the ICC said it is concerned about recent developments following the canceled tour and confirmed the situation stemmed from internal payment disagreements among West Indies players, their association (WIPA), and the WICB. Without a formal request, the ICC cannot mediate. The ICC noted the issue will be on the agenda at their Board meeting scheduled for November 10 in Dubai, and it will not comment further until then.
translated_content: El Consell Internacional de Cricket (ICC) ha reconegut que no pot intervenir en la disputa vigent entre el Consell de Cricket de les Índies Occidentals (WICB) i el Consell de Control de Cricket de l’Índia (BCCI). La crisi va començar quan l’equip de les Índies Occidentals es va retirar prematurament dels partits durant la seva gira a l’Índia, fet que va portar el BCCI a iniciar accions legals contra el WICB i a suspendre futures sèries. Donada la situació financera ja delicada del WICB, el risc de sancions econòmiques importants o la pèrdua de les gires índies podria posar en perill la continuïtat del cricket de les Índies Occidentals. Un canvi recent en la governança de l’ICC, que va concedir el poder executiu als consells de l’Índia, Anglaterra i Austràlia, fa que l’ICC ja no tingui autoritat per intervenir en disputes bilaterals com aquesta. En un comunicat, l’ICC va expressar la seva preocupació pels fets recents després de la gira cancel·lada i va confirmar que el conflicte deriva de desacords interns sobre pagaments entre els jugadors de les Índies Occidentals, la seva associació (WIPA) i el WICB. Sense una sol·licitud formal, l’ICC no té la capacitat de mediar. L’ICC ha indicat que el tema es tractarà a la reunió de la Junta programada per al 10 de novembre a Dubai, i que no farà més declaracions fins llavors.

article_content: Dr. Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), emphasized that corruption is not exclusive to Africa but a global phenomenon. In a statement from Abuja shared with the News Agency of Nigeria, Adesina urged for continuous progress in transparency, accountability, and public resource management. He stated, “The global financial crisis of 2008 did not start in Africa. We don’t have Wall Street. That collapse stemmed from greed, corruption, and fraud.” Adesina highlighted that financial misconduct, such as 'cooking the books,' is not unique to Africa, with incidents occurring in Europe’s financial sector. He acknowledged the existence of corruption in Africa, but stressed the ongoing need for transparency and accountability. Reflecting on a visit to Eritrea, Adesina shared that UN Development Programme staff claimed Eritrea had a zero percent corruption rate, and questioned why such positive stories are overlooked. He remarked, “At AfDB, good governance is our priority. Public resources must not end up in private hands, and governments should be accountable.” Adesina reinforced the necessity of transparency in how resources are obtained and used, explaining this underpins AfDB’s governance programs. He pointed out Africa’s significant illicit capital outflows—estimated between $80 and $100 billion annually—mainly facilitated by multinational companies. Discussing Africa’s economic growth, Adesina lamented the continent’s persistent place at the bottom of the global value chain. He argued that exporting raw materials perpetuates poverty, while joining global value chains via value addition is the path to prosperity. He called for investment, effective governance, and strong incentives to ensure that Africa moves up the value chain. “Africa must aim to rise from the bottom to the top of the global value chain,” Adesina said. On food security, Adesina asserted that genuine development requires self-sufficiency in food production. He noted that in 2019, the AfDB’s 81 shareholders approved a capital increase from $93 billion to $208 billion—a record in the bank’s history. This facilitated a $10 billion COVID-19 emergency response and a $1.5 billion emergency food production fund for Africa. Advocating for global financial reform, Adesina argued that Africa needs more climate finance resources. He cited that Africa received only $33 billion (around 4.5%) of the IMF’s $650 billion Special Drawing Rights, less than many European countries, and called for a fairer system. African Heads of State urge that $100 billion in unused SDRs from advanced economies be redirected to Africa. Adesina suggested this could be framed as Supporting Development Revitalisation.
translated_content: El Dr. Akinwumi Adesina, president del Banc Africà de Desenvolupament (AfDB), va subratllar que la corrupció no és exclusiva d'Àfrica sinó un fenomen global. En un comunicat enviat des d'Abuya a l'Agència de Notícies de Nigèria, Adesina va insistir en l'avenç constant en transparència, responsabilitat i la gestió dels recursos públics. Va declarar: «La crisi financera global del 2008 no va començar a l'Àfrica. No tenim Wall Street. Aquella caiguda va provenir de la cobdícia, la corrupció i el frau.» Adesina va remarcar que males pràctiques financeres com falsejar comptes no són úniques d'Àfrica, ja que també s'han produït a Europa. Va reconèixer que a l'Àfrica hi ha casos de corrupció, però va emfatitzar la necessitat contínua de transparència i responsabilitat. Recordant una visita a Eritrea, Adesina va explicar que personal del Programa de Nacions Unides per al Desenvolupament deien que Eritrea té una taxa de corrupció del zero per cent, i va qüestionar per què aquestes històries positives no s’expliquen més. Va afirmar: «A l'AfDB, la bona governança és una prioritat. Els recursos públics no han d'acabar a mans privades, i els governs han de retre comptes.» Adesina va reforçar la importància de la transparència en l'adquisició i ús de recursos, explicant que això és la base dels programes de governança de l’AfDB. Va destacar les sortides il·lícites de capital d'Àfrica—estimades entre 80.000 i 100.000 milions de dòlars a l'any—, realitzades principalment per empreses multinacionals. En parlar del desenvolupament econòmic africà, Adesina va lamentar la posició persistent del continent al final de la cadena de valor global. Va dir que exportar matèries primeres perpetua la pobresa, mentre que afegir-hi valor i participar en cadenes globals condueix a la prosperitat. Va reclamar inversions, bona governança i incentius sòlids per assegurar que l’Àfrica pugi en la cadena de valor. «L’Àfrica ha d’aspirar a passar de la base a la part superior de la cadena de valor global», va expressar Adesina. Pel que fa a la seguretat alimentària, Adesina va insistir que un desenvolupament real exigeix autosuficiència alimentària. Va destacar que el 2019, els 81 accionistes de l’AfDB van aprovar una ampliació de capital de 93.000 a 208.000 milions de dòlars—la més gran en la història del banc. Això va permetre un fons d’emergència de 10.000 milions per la COVID-19 i un de 1.500 milions per la producció alimentària a l’Àfrica. Defensant la reforma financera internacional, Adesina va afirmar que l’Àfrica necessita més recursos per al finançament climàtic. Va subratllar que només 33.000 milions (aprox. 4,5%) dels 650.000 milions en Drets Especials de Gir del FMI es van destinar a l’Àfrica, menys que a molts països europeus, reclamant justícia. article_content: Joe Perry, guitarist and vocalist of the legendary rock band Aerosmith, may be an icon to many fans—but for Perry, his true icon is his beloved cat, appropriately named Icon. In a letter featured in the book 'A Letter to My Cat,' created by Lisa Erspamer, Perry shares the heartfelt story of his relationship with his cherished feline companion. The book itself is a collection of letters from celebrities to their cats, celebrating the unique bonds they share. In Perry's touching letter—highlighted by The Dodo—he describes how, while the Perry family has always admired many animals, they were particularly intrigued by the Maine Coon breed. Icon, a Maine Coon, eventually became part of the family, captivating them with his gentle nature and impressive presence. Perry recalls that even as a kitten, Icon was larger than some adult cats, and he displayed a grace and majesty that set him apart. 'Already at this young age you moved with a grace and majesty I had never seen before. Icon, you are in a class of your own,' Perry affectionately writes. He goes on to share how Icon's loving personality—greeting Perry even when he comes home late from gigs—has endeared him. While Perry always saw himself as a dog person, Icon changed his perspective. He praises Icon's beautiful coat, intuitive nature, and the way Icon insists on staying close to Perry and his wife, Billie. Their nightly snuggle sessions are a source of comfort and joy. 'You came with the name Icon, and you still have it now because you live up to every definition of the word! You are truly one of a kind and have a special place in the Perry clan's heart,' Perry writes in the letter's moving conclusion. 'A Letter to My Cat' is available at select bookstores and at Alettertomycat.com.

En una carta inclosa al llibre 'A Letter to My Cat', creat per Lisa Erspamer, Perry comparteix la seva emotiva història amb el seu estimat company felí. article_content: Virat Kohli made history by surpassing his idol Sachin Tendulkar’s record of 49 ODI centuries, scoring his 50th century in the World Cup semifinal against New Zealand. Overcome with emotion, Kohli removed his helmet, bowed in Tendulkar's direction—who was watching from the stands—and blew a kiss to his wife, Anushka Sharma. Reflecting on the moment, Kohli said, “It’s the stuff of dreams. Anushka was sitting right there, Sachin paaji was here too. It’s difficult to explain this. If I could paint a perfect picture, this would be it. My life partner, the person I love the most, is here; my hero is here; and I was able to achieve the 50th century in front of all of them at Wankhede, such a historic venue. It was amazing.” This was also the first time Kohli scored 50 or more in a World Cup knockout match. Additionally, he surpassed another Tendulkar milestone by exceeding 673 runs in a single World Cup edition. Kohli played a pivotal role in India’s strong total of 397 against New Zealand, saying after the match, “I had to play the role I’ve played throughout the tournament so that the guys around me can express themselves. I’m glad everything came together so nicely and we put up a big total.” He emphasized his commitment to the team’s success: “The most important thing is to make my team win, whatever it takes. Whether running singles and doubles, hitting boundaries—whatever the team needs. I’ve been given a role this tournament and I’m trying to play it as best as I can, digging deep and batting long so the guys around me can play with confidence in the later overs and I can also dominate with the bat.”

Emocionat, Kohli es va treure el casc, va fer una reverència cap a Tendulkar —que mirava des de la graderia— i va enviar un petó a la seva dona, Anushka Sharma. Reflexionant sobre el moment, Kohli va dir: “És el somni de qualsevol. Anushka era just allà, Sachin paaji també era aquí. És difícil d’explicar. Si pogués pintar una imatge perfecta, seria aquesta. La meva parella de vida, la persona que estimo més, és aquí; el meu heroi és aquí; i vaig poder aconseguir la cinquantena centúria davant de tots ells al Wankhede, un escenari tan històric. Va ser increïble.” Era també la primera vegada que Kohli feia 50 o més en una eliminatòria de la Copa del Món. A més, va superar una altra fita de Tendulkar superant els 673 corrides en una sola edició del torneig. Kohli va tenir un paper clau en el gran marcador de l’Índia de 397 contra Nova Zelanda, i després del partit va dir: “Havia de fer el paper que he tingut durant tot el torneig perquè els companys poguessin expressar-se. Em fa feliç que tot hagi sortit tan bé i hàgim fet un gran total.” Va subratllar el seu compromís amb l’èxit de l’equip: “El més important és fer guanyar el meu equip, el que calgui. Tant si és córrer d’individuals i dobles, com colpejar a la frontera… el que l’equip necessiti. Se m’ha donat un paper aquest torneig i l’estic intentant fer de la millor manera possible, lluitant i mantenint-me en el bat fins tard perquè els companys puguin jugar amb confiança als últims overs i jo també pugui dominar.”

article_content: A British judge has ruled that a lawsuit involving Prince Harry, Elton John, and several other notable individuals can move forward to trial. They accuse the publisher of the Daily Mail, Associated Newspapers Ltd., of unlawfully obtaining private information through means such as bugging, phone tapping, and using deception to gather sensitive data. On Friday, Judge Matthew Nicklin rejected Associated Newspapers’ request to dismiss the case, stating their legal arguments had not definitively disproved the claims. The court found that the accusations have a genuine chance of being proven at trial. The claimants, who include Elton John’s partner David Furnish as well as actors Elizabeth Hurley and Sadie Frost, allege that their homes and cars were bugged, phone conversations were secretly recorded, and fraudulent methods were used to access their medical records. Prince Harry claims he and his inner circle were targeted with illegal voicemail hacking and other forms of surveillance. In response, Associated Newspapers strongly denies the allegations. The company argued in court that the claims were outdated—some dating back to 1993—and were reliant on confidential records submitted to the 2012 Leveson Inquiry into press misconduct. Judge Nicklin ruled that the claimants could not use these confidential documents as evidence but allowed the broader case to proceed. Also among the plaintiffs are campaigner Doreen Lawrence and former politician Simon Hughes. In a collective statement, the group welcomed the decision, emphasizing their intention to bring the truth to light and hold the publisher accountable for years of alleged wrongdoing, which they say included not just eavesdropping but also bribing police officers and accessing hospital and bank records illicitly. Associated Newspapers called the court’s restriction on confidential materials a 'significant victory' and maintained that the claims are outrageous. They look forward to defending themselves at trial. Prince Harry, who cites media intrusion as a reason for withdrawing from royal duties and relocating to the United States, has multiple ongoing lawsuits against British tabloids. His legal actions are partly motivated by the media’s treatment of his late mother, Princess Diana. Earlier this year, Harry gave historic court testimony in a separate hacking case against the publishers of the Daily Mirror, with the ruling still pending. He is also suing the publisher of The Sun alongside actor Hugh Grant, with that case expected to go to trial next year. The next hearing in the Associated Newspapers case is scheduled for November 21, but no trial date has been set. Prince Harry attended earlier hearings, although he has not yet testified in this particular case.

article_content: The NBA is moving to force Donald Sterling to part with the Los Angeles Clippers after his racist remarks were made public. This action is built on agreements, starting with a 1981 contract signed when Sterling bought the team, that provide grounds to terminate team ownership. Other updated contracts have included ‘moral clauses’ as well. Sterling, who has been fined $2.5 million, is permanently banned from running or accessing the team. Commissioner Adam Silver is calling on the NBA’s other 29 owners to endorse a forced sale of the Clippers. The league’s Advisory/Finance Committee has reviewed the issue and will meet again, with a 75% owner vote needed to proceed with the removal. Sterling’s actions are said to be in violation of Article 13(d) of the NBA constitution, which holds owners to standards regarding their conduct and contractual obligations. Although Sterling’s exact personal stake is unclear, the team belongs to a family trust, and his wife Shelly Sterling wants to keep her part. Donald Sterling, now 80 and a wealthy real estate developer and attorney, has not addressed the scandal since an audio was leaked by TMZ. The tape showed him berating a woman for posing in photos with Black public figures, including Magic Johnson. Tommy Lasorda, a friend of Sterling and former Dodgers manager, commented that he wasn’t surprised by Sterling’s statements but was critical of the woman in the recordings, V. Stiviano—who denies leaking the audio through her lawyer. Meanwhile, the Clippers continue their playoff battle with the Oklahoma City Thunder, currently leading the series.

article_content: John Arthur and Jim Obergefell, partners of more than 20 years, finally wed after traveling from Ohio to Maryland—a journey made possible only through determination and overwhelming community support. John, who has advanced ALS, and Jim decided to marry following the Supreme Court’s decision to strike down the Defense of Marriage Act, although Ohio’s ban on same-sex marriage remained. John’s illness made the journey especially difficult, so the couple arranged for a special medical flight funded with help from family, friends, and even strangers. Jim traveled to Maryland ahead of time to obtain the marriage license, and returned with John so they could be legally married aboard the plane at the Baltimore/Washington International Airport. The ceremony, performed by John’s aunt Paulette Roberts—who became ordained for their wedding—was brief and deeply moving. Their relationship began in 1992 and quickly grew, but John’s ALS diagnosis two years earlier added urgency and new challenges. Ohio’s refusal to recognize their relationship complicated legal and health care matters, prompting the couple to prepare legal documents and place property solely in Jim’s name to secure their future. ALS, or Lou Gehrig’s Disease, is a fatal neurological illness that progressively robs people of voluntary muscle control and ultimately the ability to breathe. Most patients live only three to five years after diagnosis. Despite the heartache caused by illness and injustice, John and Jim celebrated their wedding with family, tears, and champagne before returning home as newlyweds recognized under Maryland and federal law. Jim expressed relief and gratitude that their love story could finally be acknowledged publicly and on paper. Looking to the future, the couple hoped for lasting change in Ohio, where citizens could soon vote on marriage equality.

John, que pateix ELA avançada, i Jim van decidir casar-se després que el Tribunal Suprem anul·lés la Defense of Marriage Act, tot i que a Ohio el matrimoni entre persones del mateix sexe seguia prohibit. La malaltia d’en John feia especialment complicat el viatge, de manera que la parella va organitzar un vol mèdic especial costejat amb l’ajuda de familiars, amistats i fins i tot desconeguts. La cerimònia, oficiada per la tieta d’en John, Paulette Roberts —que va ser ordenada ministra per al casament—, va ser breu però molt emotiva. Malgrat la duresa de la malaltia i la injustícia, en John i en Jim van poder celebrar el casament amb la família, llàgrimes i xampany abans de tornar a casa com a recents casats reconeguts per la llei de Maryland i la llei federal. En Jim agraïa que, finalment, la seva història d’amor fos reconeguda públicament i formalment. De cara al futur, la parella confiava que aviat Ohio votaria a favor de la igualtat matrimonial.

Todd Sixt, CEO of Strait & Sound, is an experienced leader in the financial services sector. A value proposition, in essence, is the reason clients select a particular financial advisor. After over 20 years coaching advisors, I have found that many struggle to pinpoint why clients choose them over others. Often, advisors serve clients for years without knowing why clients remain loyal. Usually, this isn't an issue; clients are busy and may find changing advisors stressful and inconvenient. However, significant disruptions can prompt clients to reevaluate their financial advisor along with other long-term goals.

From my perspective, disruptive change is the ultimate test of an advisor’s value proposition. If it holds up, not only can you retain clients, but you might also attract new ones. If it fails, you risk losing existing clients. This is why I believe the wealth management value proposition stands out in the industry. In my experience, wealth managers are particularly resilient during disruptions and may even strengthen client loyalty and gain referrals when clients face major life changes.

Types of Disruptions:
Disruptions fall into two categories: macro and micro. Macro-disruptions include events like global crises (such as Covid-19), financial downturns (e.g., the 2008-2009 recession), or industry-specific challenges. These generally unsettle clients and impact the markets. Micro-disruptions, on the other hand, are personal—family illness, death, divorce, forced retirement, job loss, or unplanned expenses. Both types make clients reconsider their financial paths.

Three Primary Value Propositions:
After reflecting on industry trends, I believe most advisors follow one of three value propositions: financial planner, broker, or wealth manager.

1. Financial Planner: Focuses on crafting long-term plans for clients, monitoring progress at regular intervals, and making adjustments when needed.
2. Broker: Aims for better-than-average market returns, often leveraging analytical skills and advanced technology to design superior investment strategies. They highlight their track record regardless of market conditions.
3. Wealth Manager: Emphasizes deep client relationships, long-term partnerships, a comprehensive approach, and, crucially, bridging the gap between what clients want their wealth to achieve and the current state of their finances.

The Wealth Management Value Proposition:
Wealth managers build trust through extensive discovery processes, fostering long-term commitment to client goals. Some wealth managers maintain relationships with families across generations, serving clients even after the original wealth creators pass away.

A key aspect involves regular, thorough reviews of clients' goals and situations (typically every five years), ensuring estate documents and wealth plans remain up-to-date. As an example, outdated beneficiary designations can unintentionally disinherit intended heirs. Wealth managers help clients identify these gaps and take corrective action, so wealth distribution aligns with their wishes.

Wealth managers generally do not promise above-market returns; instead, they focus on building solid plans based on market averages and providing high-touch service. This approach strengthens client loyalty, even during disruptive events.

Todd Sixt, CEO de Strait & Sound, és un líder experimentat en el sector dels serveis financers. Una proposta de valor, en essència, és el motiu pel qual els clients trien un assessor financer en concret. Després de més de 20 anys assessorant altres professionals, he observat que molts tenen dificultats per identificar per què els clients els trien a ells i no a uns altres. Sovint, els assessors mantenen clients durant anys sense saber realment per què segueixen sent fidels. Normalment, això no suposa un problema, ja que els clients tenen poc temps i canviar d’assessor pot resultar estressant i incòmode. Però quan es produeixen grans disrupcions, els clients solen revisar els seus objectius a llarg termini, inclòs l’assessor financer.

Des del meu punt de vista, una disrupció és la prova definitiva de la proposta de valor d’un assessor. Si resisteix, pots retenir els clients i fins i tot captar-ne de nous. Si falla, pots perdre’ls. Per això crec que la proposta de valor de la gestió de patrimonis destaca dins del sector. Per experiència, els gestors patrimonials mostren una gran resistència davant les disrupcions i, de vegades, aconsegueixen reforçar la lleialtat i obtenir recomanacions quan els clients passen per moments de canvi important.

Tipus de disrupcions:
Les disrupcions són de dos tipus: macro i micro. Les macro inclouen esdeveniments globals (com la Covid-19), grans caigudes dels mercats (com la recessió del 2008-2009) o reptes en sectors específics. Aquestes situacions, en general, inquietan els clients i afecten els mercats. Les micro són personals: malalties familiars, defuncions, divorcis, jubilacions forçades, pèrdua de feina o despeses inesperades. Totes dues fan que els clients es replantegin el seu camí financer.

Tres propostes de valor principals:
Després d’analitzar les tendències del sector, considero que la majoria d’assessors segueixen una de tres propostes de valor: planificador financer, broker o gestor patrimonial.

1. Planificador financer: s’enfoca a crear plans a llarg termini, revisar-ne l’evolució periòdicament i fer-hi els ajustaments necessaris.
2. Broker: busca obtenir rendiments superiors a la mitjana de mercat, utilitzant habilitats analítiques i tecnologia avançada per crear estratègies d’inversió. Destaquen el seu historial en qualsevol situació de mercat.
3. Gestor patrimonial: prioritza la relació personal amb el client, la col·laboració a llarg termini, un enfocament integral i, molt especialment, reduir les distàncies entre el que el client vol assolir amb el seu patrimoni i la realitat financera.

La proposta de valor en la gestió de patrimonis:
Els gestors patrimonials generen confiança mitjançant processos de descoberta aprofundits, fomentant una relació de compromís duradora amb els objectius dels clients. Alguns mantenen vincles amb diverses generacions d’una mateixa família, fins i tot quan han desaparegut els primers creadors de patrimoni.

Un aspecte clau és revisar periòdicament els objectius i la situació dels clients (aproximadament cada cinc anys), assegurant que els documents testamentaris i plans patrimonials estiguin actualitzats. Per exemple, si els beneficiaris són antics, podrien desheretar familiars previstos sense voler. Els gestors ajuden a detectar aquests buits i a corregir-los perquè la distribució del patrimoni s’ajusti als desitjos dels clients.

En general, els gestors patrimonials no prometen rendiments superiors al mercat; es basen en plans realistes amb rendiments mitjans i ofereixen un servei personalitzat. Això reforça la lleialtat, fins i tot en moments disruptius.

article_content: Bristol city centre landmarks, such as lamp posts, bus stops, and post boxes, may soon be able to communicate with the public through the innovative 'Hello Lamp Post' project. This initiative will assign individual mobile phone codes to inanimate objects, allowing anyone to text them and receive replies. With each conversation, these objects will 'learn' and provide increasingly intelligent responses, including sharing stories or secrets sent to them. Pan Studio, supported by a £30,000 grant, is behind this scheme to enliven Bristol’s urban landscape. Ben Barker, who leads Pan Studio, said, 'We are refining game mechanics and conversation styles for the texts. We're hoping Bristolians will engage playfully with street furniture and each other as they discover new things.' 'The more people who participate, the richer the experience becomes.' Each object will have a unique code, with responses growing more varied as interaction increases. This project aligns with the growing trend known as the 'Internet of Things,' where everyday objects are connected and able to communicate independently and act smartly. Clare Reddington, Executive Producer of the Playable City Award, commented: 'MIT Technology Review dubbed 2013 the year of the Internet of Things, highlighting the move to make objects more interactive. With the Playable City Award, we're giving residents new, playful ways to experience their city. As a real experiment, we look forward to discovering more about Bristol and ourselves.' Launching in Bristol from July 15 to September 8, Hello Lamp Post will feature bus stops, lampposts, postboxes, and charity bins, each with unique codes and evolving interactions as participation increases. The wider idea of adding connectivity to inanimate objects, known as the Internet of Things, has already been seen in interactive lamps, fridges, and cars.

Amb cada conversa, aquests objectes 'aprenen' i donen respostes cada cop més intel·ligents, fins i tot compartint històries o secrets rebuts. Pan Studio, amb el suport d’una subvenció de 30.000 £, lidera la iniciativa per donar vida al paisatge urbà de Bristol. Ben Barker, responsable de Pan Studio, explica: 'Estem perfeccionant la mecànica del joc i l’estil de conversa dels missatges. Esperem que la gent de Bristol es diverteixi interactuant amb el mobiliari urbà i que, alhora, es relacionin entre ells descobrint coses noves.' 'Com més gent hi participi, més enriquidor serà tot plegat.' Cada objecte tindrà un codi únic i, amb més interaccions, oferirà respostes més variades. Clare Reddington, productora executiva del Playable City Award, comenta: 'La MIT Technology Review va declarar el 2013 l’any de la Internet de les Coses, posant èmfasi en fer que els objectes siguin més interactius. Amb el Playable City Award volem oferir als residents maneres lúdiques i noves de viure la ciutat. És tot un experiment i ens fa il·lusió descobrir més sobre Bristol i nosaltres mateixos.' El projecte Hello Lamp Post s’estrenarà a Bristol del 15 de juliol al 8 de setembre i inclourà parades d’autobús, fanals, bústies i contenidors solidaris, tots amb codis únics i interaccions que creixaran amb la participació. El concepte més ampli de connectar objectes inanimats—Internet de les Coses—ja s’ha vist en làmpades, neveres i cotxes interactius.

article_content: At 65 years old, Carol Masheter set a new record as the oldest woman to climb the highest mountain on every continent—a feat known as the Seven Summits. Her journey concluded at the top of Australia’s Mount Kosciuszko on March 17, after more than five years of determination and perseverance. Carol overcame her family’s concerns, endured extreme climates, and even faced temporary blindness for ten hours descending Mount Everest. Her mountaineering story began at age 50, following a difficult period filled with personal losses, including her mother’s death, a breakup, unemployment, and health challenges. Seeking relief, she tried high-altitude climbing in the Bolivian Andes and found a new passion. Starting with Aconcagua in South America at age 60, she next summited Kilimanjaro in Africa at 61. That same year, she reached the top of the world at Mount Everest in Nepal, on May 24, 2008. Carol then conquered North America’s Denali at 63, Europe’s Mount Elbrus at 64, and at 65, she successfully climbed both Vinson Massif in Antarctica and finally Mount Kosciuszko in Australia. For Carol, the challenges of mountaineering offered strength and healing in response to adversity. After summiting Cho Oyu in China in 2005 and seeing Everest, she realized she needed to try for the world’s tallest peak. Preparation involved scaling Kilimanjaro, and after Everest, she committed to finishing the Seven Summits. She is now in the process of having her achievement officially recognized, and will likely surpass Kay LeClaire, the current record holder, who completed the Seven Summits at age 60. ‘People think I should be settling down at my age,’ Carol remarked, ‘but that’s just not me.’
translated_content: Als 65 anys, Carol Masheter ha establert un nou rècord com la dona més gran d'edat a escalar la muntanya més alta de cada continent—un repte conegut com els Set Cims. El seu viatge va acabar al cim del Mount Kosciuszko, a Austràlia, el 17 de març, després de més de cinc anys d'esforç i determinació. La Carol va superar les preocupacions de la seva família, va suportar condicions extremes i fins i tot va patir ceguesa temporal durant deu hores mentre baixava de l'Everest. La seva aventura d’alpinisme va començar als 50 anys, després d’un període complicat per fortes pèrdues personals, com la mort de la seva mare, una ruptura, l’atur i problemes de salut. Buscant superar-ho, es va iniciar en l'alta muntanya als Andes bolivians, on va descobrir una nova passió. Va començar amb l’Aconcagua a Sud-amèrica als 60 anys, va seguir amb el Kilimanjaro a Àfrica als 61 i, aquell mateix any, va coronar el cim més alt del món, l’Everest al Nepal, el 24 de maig del 2008. Després, la Carol va conquerir el Denali d’Amèrica del Nord als 63, l’Elbrus d’Europa als 64, i als 65, va escalar tant el Vinson Massif a l’Antàrtida com, finalment, el Mount Kosciuszko a Austràlia. Per a la Carol, els reptes de l’alpinisme li han donat força i han ajudat a superar l’adversitat. Després d’escalar el Cho Oyu a la Xina el 2005 i veure l’Everest, va decidir intentar el cim més alt del món. Es va preparar pujant el Kilimanjaro i, després de l’Everest, va decidir completar els Set Cims. Ara mateix està en procés d’obtenir el reconeixement oficial de la seva fita, i probablement superarà Kay LeClaire, la persona que fins ara té el rècord i que va finalitzar els Set Cims amb 60 anys. ‘La gent pensa que hauria de portar una vida més tranquil·la a la meva edat,’ comenta la Carol, ‘però això no va amb mi.’

article_content:
Syria's crisis continues to worsen each day. Recently, Defense Minister Daoud Rajiha and other top associates of President Bashar al-Assad were killed, with opposition groups claiming responsibility. Nawaf al-Fares, Syria’s ambassador to Iraq, also resigned and joined the opposition, and government-backed militiamen reportedly shot villagers in Tremseh at close range. There is growing agreement among U.S. political leaders that Assad should step down, the opposition should be armed, and that Syria represents a strategic challenge for the United States and its allies.

Senator John McCain has stated that ending Assad’s regime would cut off Hezbollah from Iran, remove a threat to Israel, strengthen Lebanon, and deal a strategic setback to Iran—calling it “a geopolitical success of the first order.”

Humanitarian organizations estimate that 10,000 to 20,000 people have died in the last 17 months of violence in Syria. Despite this, President Barack Obama, Governor Mitt Romney, and their campaigns have avoided detailed discussion of Syria, preferring not to take political risks by addressing potential U.S. intervention.

Reflecting on U.S. intervention in the early 1980s, former Secretary of Defense Caspar Weinberger's national security doctrine offers lessons. In June 1982, Israel invaded Lebanon to target the PLO during Lebanon’s civil war. France, Italy, and the U.S. formed a multinational force to help stabilize Lebanon and oversee the PLO's exit. The PLO departed by late August, with the multinational force leaving in September, but the violence continued.

President-elect Bashir Gemayel was killed in September. Soon after, Israeli forces stood by as Lebanese Phalangists killed Palestinians at the Sabra and Shatila camps, reportedly in retaliation for Gemayel’s assassination. Amin Gemayel became president, and the multinational force re-entered Beirut. On October 23, 1983, suicide bombers struck U.S. and French barracks, killing 241 Americans and nearly 60 French personnel—the deadliest day for Marines since World War II.

The U.S. navy retaliated from December 1983 to February 1984, with the USS New Jersey firing its guns in combat for the first time since Vietnam. By April, after the UK joined the effort, the multinational force had withdrawn, but Lebanon’s civil war persisted until 1990.

President Reagan generally supported diplomatic efforts in Lebanon, but Weinberger believed it was the wrong conflict for the U.S. He issued six principles for future military action, emphasizing clear objectives, national interest, assured public support, and using force only as a last resort.

U.S. interventions were initially supported but soon seen as too pro-Israel. Accidental shelling of civilians undermined U.S. credibility. The lack of clear objectives led to Reagan’s withdrawal decision, avoiding further entanglement.

In Syria today, the humanitarian crisis and strategic considerations evoke Weinberger’s lessons. While there are calls for supporting the Syrian opposition and possible international coalitions, practical actions remain uncertain, especially ahead of U.S. elections. Weinberger's doctrine underlines the difficulty of matching means to ends in complex crises. As he warned, the U.S. should avoid repeating Lebanon’s mistakes by clearly distinguishing between peacekeeping and combat missions.

The opinions expressed belong solely to Kiron Skinner.

França, Itàlia i els EUA van formar una força multinacional per estabilitzar el país i supervisar la sortida de l’OLP. El president electe Bashir Gemayel va ser assassinat al setembre. Poc després, les forces israelianes van permetre als falangistes libanesos atacar els camps de refugiats de Sabra i Shatila, on van ser assassinats palestins, presumptament en represàlia per l’assassinat de Gemayel. A Síria, la crisi humanitària i les qüestions estratègiques evoquen les lliçons de Weinberger. Tot i parlar-se de donar suport a l’oposició siriana i de possibles coalicions internacionals, les accions concretes encara són incertes, especialment abans de les eleccions als EUA. La doctrina de Weinberger destaca la dificultat d’adaptar mitjans i objectius en crisis complexes. Tal com advertia, cal evitar repetir els errors del Líban distingint clarament entre missions de manteniment de la pau i de combat.

Nazim Valiyev, once a young dentist, was forced to leave his home in Karabakh due to ethnic violence that erupted in the late 1980s. Now 60 years old and retired following a stroke, he hopes to return to the region, which is once again under Azerbaijani control. For him and many others, however, returning may still be years away. Valiyev is one of an estimated 700,000 Azerbaijanis who fled or were forced out of Karabakh and surrounding areas when violence escalated in 1988 and grew into war, ending in 1994 with the territory under ethnic Armenian, Armenian-backed control. Decades later, Azerbaijan regained most of the territory in a 2020 war, and a rapid offensive in September 2023 forced Armenian separatists to relinquish their final hold over the region, known internationally as Nagorno-Karabakh.

In the aftermath, Azerbaijan’s President Ilham Aliyev raised the national flag over the region’s capital, now officially called Khankendi, reaffirming Azerbaijani control. Nearly all of the region’s predominantly Armenian population—formerly around 120,000—departed within days, and a UN mission in early October estimated fewer than 1,000 residents remained.

Events have rekindled hope among displaced Azerbaijanis, who cherish memories of the region’s landscapes. Bahar Aliguleyeva, who left Khankendi (Stepanakert, in Armenian) at age 16, recalls “walking in the forest and picking flowers” as a child. Hearing of Azerbaijan’s regained control, she said it felt “as if I found myself somewhere between the past and reality, but there is a path to happiness.”

Valiyev dreams of returning too, but is realistic, stating, “I understand that this will not be a quick process.” In 2022, President Aliyev launched “The Great Return to Azerbaijan’s Liberated Territories,” a program aimed at resettling those displaced. The plan focuses on infrastructure improvement, new housing, and comprehensive mine clearance. This year’s Azerbaijani budget designates approximately $3.1 billion for reconstruction.

To date, around 2,000 people have returned, with government hopes for 10,000 by year’s end and 150,000 by 2027, according to State Committee official Fuad Huseynov. However, heavy mining and widespread destruction present ongoing dangers. Azerbaijan’s Mine Action Agency reports at least 65 deaths and 267 injuries from mines and unexploded ordnance since 2020.

For returnees like Aliguleyeva and Valiyev, much may have changed. Aliguleyeva doesn’t know if her childhood home still stands; a former neighbor could only send a photo of the courtyard wall. Valiyev notes his family home was destroyed in 1988, their dental office building surviving. Still, he looks forward to sharing his story with his granddaughter: “The past must never be repeated. We and the Armenians must start a new life, no matter how difficult. Enmity cannot go on forever.”

Yet, reconciliation may be harder than rebuilding homes. While both Valiyev and Aliguleyeva recall positive relationships with Armenian neighbors, they also remember the fear and trauma of conflict. The Azerbaijani government has pledged to safeguard the rights of remaining ethnic Armenians, but Human Rights Watch cautions skepticism, citing Azerbaijan’s human rights record and the region’s long history of violence.

— Associated Press writer Jim Heintz in Tallinn, Estonia, contributed.

Nazim Valiyev, que va començar sent dentista, es va veure obligat a abandonar casa seva al Karabakh a causa de la violència ètnica que va esclatar a finals dels anys vuitanta. Ara, amb 60 anys i retirat després d’un ictus, espera poder tornar a la regió, que torna a ser sota control de l’Azerbaidjan. Però per ell i molts altres, la tornada encara pot trigar anys. Valiyev és un dels aproximadament 700.000 azerbaidjanesos que van fugir o van ser expulsats del Karabakh i de les zones veïnes quan la violència va augmentar el 1988 i es va convertir en una guerra que va acabar el 1994 amb el territori sota control armeni, recolzat per Armènia. Dècades després, l’Azerbaidjan va recuperar la major part del territori durant la guerra del 2020, i una ràpida ofensiva al setembre del 2023 va obligar els separatistes armenis a lliurar el seu darrer control sobre la regió, coneguda internacionalment com a Nagorno-Karabakh.

Després d’aquests fets, el president de l’Azerbaidjan, Ilham Aliyev, va hissar la bandera nacional a la capital de la regió, ara oficialment anomenada Khankendi, reafirmant-ne el control. Gairebé tota la població armènia de la regió—abans unes 120.000 persones—va marxar en pocs dies, i una missió de l’ONU a principis d’octubre calculava que en quedaven menys d’un miler.

Aquests esdeveniments han encès l’esperança entre els azerbaidjanesos desplaçats, que guarden records dels paisatges de la regió. Bahar Aliguleyeva, que va marxar de Khankendi (Stepanakert, en armeni) als 16 anys, recorda "passejar pel bosc i collir flors" de petita. Quan va saber que l’Azerbaidjan havia recuperat el control, va dir que se sentia “com si estigués entre el passat i la realitat, però hi ha un camí cap a la felicitat.”

Valiyev també somia tornar, però és realista: “Entenc que no serà un procés ràpid.” El 2022, el president Aliyev va llançar “El Gran Retorn als Territoris Alliberats de l’Azerbaidjan”, un programa que vol resituar els desplaçats. El pla posa èmfasi en la millora d’infraestructures, nous habitatges i un desminatge exhaustiu. El pressupost d’aquest any de l’Azerbaidjan preveu uns 3.100 milions de dòlars per a la reconstrucció.

Fins ara, unes 2.000 persones hi han tornat, i el govern espera arribar a 10.000 a finals d’any i a 150.000 el 2027, segons Fuad Huseynov del Comitè Estatal. Malgrat això, els camps de mines i la destrucció generalitzada són encara un gran perill. L’Agència d’Acció contra Mines de l’Azerbaidjan informa almenys de 65 morts i 267 ferits per mines i explosius des de 2020.

Per als que hi tornen, com Aliguleyeva i Valiyev, la realitat pot ser molt diferent. Aliguleyeva no sap si la seva casa d’infància encara existeix; una antiga veïna només li ha pogut enviar una foto del mur del pati. Valiyev assenyala que la casa familiar va ser destruïda el 1988, però la consulta dental va sobreviure. Tot i així, té ganes d’explicar la seva història a la seva neta: “El passat no s’hauria de repetir mai. Nosaltres i els armenis hem de començar una nova vida, per difícil que sigui. L’enemistat no pot durar per sempre.”

Tot i això, la reconciliació pot ser més difícil que reconstruir cases. Tant Valiyev com Aliguleyeva recorden bones relacions amb veïns armenis, però també el temor i el trauma del conflicte. El govern azerbaidjanès ha promès respectar els drets dels armenis que romanguin, però Human Rights Watch avisa de ser escèptics, citant l’historial d’Azerbaidjan en drets humans i la llarga història de violència de la regió.

— Jim Heintz, corresponsal de l’Associated Press a Tallinn, Estònia, hi ha contribuït.

article_content:
Over the past two decades, pro-democracy grassroots organizations have played a crucial role in challenging and overthrowing long-standing authoritarian regimes across Africa. Since the 1990s, many African countries have made meaningful strides toward democratic governance, though several setbacks have occurred along the way.

While there have been improvements in democratic transitions, some leaders who held power before 1990, like Paul Biya of Cameroon and Robert Mugabe of Zimbabwe, have remained in office despite opposition efforts. Mali, which had been strengthening its democracy, faced serious setbacks—first from separatist rebel occupations in the north, then from a military coup that ousted the elected government. In Guinea-Bissau, soldiers suspended government institutions, undermining the rule of law. In several countries—including Nigeria, Central African Republic, Kenya, Uganda, and Madagascar—ongoing violence by ethnic and religious groups continues to harm governance.

Weaknesses in national protections for individual rights persist. For example, a UN report indicated that The Gambia executed several prisoners without due process. In South Africa, police used deadly force against striking miners.

Nonetheless, there have been significant achievements in Africa’s efforts to deepen democracy. Ghana, in particular, stands out for peaceful constitutional succession after President John Atta Mills' death in 2012 and for conducting competitive, fair, and peaceful elections won by John Dramani Mahama. Ghana has also become a model for government transparency, especially in the management of extractive industry revenues.

Other countries have made progress as well. Ivory Coast overcame a violent civil war to establish new laws, institutions, and greater transparency, and now has a functioning legislature and improved security. Sierra Leone restored national institutions after its civil war, holding peaceful and accepted elections in 2012. Senegal’s 2012 elections allowed a peaceful power transition, with President Macky Sall implementing reforms for government transparency and accountability. Lesotho, Malawi, and Guinea have seen better governance, with constitutional transfers of power and increased civic dialogue.

The Arab Spring brought regime changes in Egypt, Libya, and Tunisia. Tunisia’s revolution, sparked by Mohamed Bouazizi’s self-immolation, inspired grassroots movements across the region, leading to the departure of long-serving rulers. However, transitions have often faced setbacks: in Egypt, actions by President Mohamed Morsy and the dissolution of parliament signaled democratic regression. In Tunisia, the assassination of secular leader Chokri Belaid marked another step backward, while persistent violence in Libya revealed institutional weaknesses.

Overall, while grassroots movements have advanced democracy, entrenched power structures and opportunists have sometimes thwarted their goals. Sustained progress toward democratic governance in Africa will require inclusive, participatory, and locally-driven constitutional reforms that create effective, accountable institutions and protect citizens’ rights. The views in this commentary are those of John Mukum Mbaku.

Des de la dècada del 1990, molts països africans han fet avenços significatius cap a una governança democràtica, però també han patit retrocessos importants.

Tot i aquests avenços, alguns líders que ja estaven al poder abans de 1990, com Paul Biya del Camerun i Robert Mugabe de Zimbabwe, han continuat governant malgrat els esforços de l’oposició. Mali, que estava en procés de consolidació democràtica, va patir seriosos retrocessos: primer amb l’ocupació separatista del nord i després amb un cop d’estat militar que va destituir el govern elegit. A Guinea-Bissau, els militars van suspendre les institucions governamentals, la qual cosa va debilitar l’estat de dret. En països com Nigèria, República Centreafricana, Kenya, Uganda i Madagascar, la violència ètnica i religiosa persistent continua perjudicant la governabilitat.

La manca de protecció efectiva dels drets individuals continua sent un problema. Un informe de l’ONU va assenyalar que a Gàmbia es van executar diversos presos sense garanties judicials. A Sud-àfrica, la policia va utilitzar força mortal contra miners en vaga.

Amb tot, s’han assolit progressos destacats en la consolidació de la democràcia. Ghana sobresurt per la transició pacífica segons la constitució després de la mort del president John Atta Mills el 2012, i per la celebració d’eleccions justes i pacífiques que va guanyar John Dramani Mahama. Ghana també és un exemple de transparència governamental, sobretot en la gestió dels recursos minerals.

Altres països també han progressat. Costa d’Ivori va superar una guerra civil per establir noves lleis, institucions i més transparència; ara té una legislatura funcional i una millora en la seguretat. Sierra Leone va recuperar institucions després de la seva guerra civil i el 2012 va acollir eleccions pacífiques. Al Senegal, les eleccions de 2012 van permetre una transició pacífica, i el president Macky Sall ha posat en marxa reformes orientades a la transparència i la responsabilitat pública. Lesotho, Malawi i Guinea han experimentat una millor governança amb transferències constitucionals de poder i major diàleg cívic.

La Primavera Àrab va fer caure règims a Egipte, Líbia i Tunísia. La revolució a Tunísia, iniciada per la immolació de Mohamed Bouazizi, va despertar moviments populars a tota la regió i va propiciar la fi de règims de llarga durada. Però les transicions han afrontat sovint dificultats: a Egipte, les accions del president Mohamed Morsy i la dissolució del parlament van suposar un retrocés per a la democràcia. A Tunísia, l’assassinat del líder laic Chokri Belaid va ser un altre pas enrere, i la violència persistent a Líbia reflecteix la fragilitat institucional.

En resum, tot i que els moviments de base han impulsat la democràcia, les estructures de poder consolidades i alguns oportunistes han frustrat sovint aquests esforços. Perquè el progrés democràtic sigui sostenible a l’Àfrica, calen reformes constitucionals inclusives, participatives i locals que creïn institucions eficients, responsables i defensores dels drets de la ciutadania. Les opinions expressades en aquest article corresponen a John Mukum Mbaku.

article_content: In Nigeria’s oil-rich Niger Delta, over a thousand militants and their leaders have recently surrendered weapons to authorities in a government-led amnesty. Initiated in August and set to conclude in October, the program offers pardons and potential employment for those who disarm, aiming to reduce violence in the region. Police publicly displayed confiscated weapons—including guns and rocket launchers—to crowds at the event. Militant commander Ebikabowei "Boyloaf" Ben expressed support for peaceful negotiation, stating, "We lay down our arms today, but now our struggle will continue through dialogue." However, the Movement for the Emancipation of the Niger Delta (MEND), a prominent coalition of armed groups, has refused to join the amnesty. MEND claims the disarmaments are staged and vows to resume attacks on the oil industry if their issues aren’t addressed when their ceasefire ends in mid-September. The unrest is rooted in accusations that oil profits, which make up 80% of Nigeria’s revenue, enrich politicians rather than benefit local communities. Ongoing violence has reduced oil output by up to 40%, deeply affecting the national economy. While earlier military operations targeted militant groups, government figures like Bayelsa state Governor Timipre Sylva and Amnesty Committee Chief Lucky Ararile are championing dialogue, urging remaining militants to accept the offer. Ararile warned that those refusing amnesty would face legal consequences. For many former militants, lack of job options contributed to their involvement in conflict. Ex-fighter Mayus Bayolou remarked, "We took up arms because we’re jobless. Now what we need are real jobs." Still, concrete plans for the rehabilitation and development promised to participants remain unclear. Although leaders like Boyloaf advocate for constructive negotiation, they also warn that if government commitments are not fulfilled, future unrest could be even more severe.

Començat a l’agost i amb visió de finalitzar a l’octubre, el programa ofereix el perdó i la possibilitat de feina als qui dipositin les armes, amb la intenció de reduir la violència a la regió. Els policies van exhibir pública­ment les armes confiscades—entre elles pistoles i llançacoets—davant la multitud assistent. El comandant Ebikabowei "Boyloaf" Ben va expressar suport al diàleg pacífic dient: «Avui deixem les armes, però la nostra lluita seguirà a través del diàleg.» Tanmateix, el Moviment per l’Emancipació del Delta del Níger (MEND), una important coalició de grups armats, ha rebutjat l’amnistia. El MEND acusa el govern d’escenificar aquests lliuraments i alerta que reprendrà els atacs a la indústria petroliera si les seves demandes no són resoltes quan acabi l’alto el foc a mitjans de setembre. El conflicte s’arrela en acusacions que els ingressos del petroli—el 80% del pressupost nacional nigerià— afavoreixen els polítics, però no les comunitats locals. La violència continuada ha reduït la producció de cru fins a un 40%, impactant fortament l’economia del país. Encara que abans es van dur a terme operacions militars contra grups armats, dirigents com el governador de l’estat de Bayelsa, Timipre Sylva, i Lucky Ararile, cap del Comitè d’Amnistia, impulsen ara el diàleg i demanen als militants restants que acceptin l’oferta. Ararile adverteix que qui rebutgi l’amnistia afrontarà conseqüències legals. La falta d’oportunitats laborals ha portat molts antics combatents cap al conflicte. L’ex-milicià Mayus Bayolou explica: «Vam agafar les armes perquè ens faltava feina. Ara el que realment necessitem són feines.» No obstant això, els plans concrets de rehabilitació i desenvolupament promesos romanen imprecisos. Si bé líders com Boyloaf defensen la negociació constructiva, també adverteixen que si el govern no compleix, la inestabilitat futura podria empitjorar.
