Guatemalan President Alvaro Colom has declared a state of national calamity due to widespread food insecurity and malnutrition affecting many citizens. Sisters Vidalia and Maribel Agustin, both suffering from malnutrition, have found shelter in Guatemala as of August. In a nationally televised address Tuesday night, Colom stated that the declaration would enable faster delivery of food aid to thousands of Guatemalan families in urgent need. "This will help us access resources from the international community that have been generously offered, and will also allow us to mobilize national resources more rapidly," he said.

The United Nations World Food Programme reports that Guatemala has the fourth highest rate of chronic malnutrition in the world and the highest in Latin America and the Caribbean. Chronic undernutrition affects approximately half of the country's children under five.

President Colom pointed to this year's drought, global warming, and the international economic crisis as major factors behind the nation's food problems. He also referenced Guatemala's long-standing social inequities, which have resulted in high levels of poverty and malnutrition. According to the World Bank, about 75 percent of Guatemalans live below the poverty line—defined as lacking enough income to buy essential goods and services. Nearly 58 percent of the population lives below the extreme poverty line, meaning they cannot afford a basic diet. "This is the root of the food and nutritional crisis our country is experiencing," Colom said. "There is food available. What we lack are the resources for those affected to purchase it. We must not wait until famine strikes to act."

Poverty is particularly acute among indigenous peoples and those living in rural areas. In the highlands—home to many indigenous communities—seven out of ten children under five are malnourished, according to the World Food Programme. Around 40 percent of Guatemala's 13.2 million citizens are indigenous Mayans, the CIA World Fact Book reports.

En un discurs televisat a tot el país dimarts a la nit, Colom va explicar que la declaració permetrà una entrega més ràpida d'ajuda alimentària a milers de famílies guatemalenques en situació urgent. "Això ens ajudarà a accedir a recursos de la comunitat internacional que han estat generosament oferts, i també ens permetrà mobilitzar recursos nacionals més ràpidament", va dir.

El Programa Mundial d'Aliments de les Nacions Unides informa que Guatemala té la quarta taxa més alta de malnutrició crònica al món i la més alta d'Amèrica Llatina i el Carib. La desnutrició crònica afecta aproximadament la meitat dels infants menors de cinc anys al país.

El president Colom va assenyalar la sequera d'aquest any, l'escalfament global i la crisi econòmica internacional com a factors clau dels problemes alimentaris del país. També va referir-se a les desigualtats socials històriques de Guatemala, que han comportat nivells elevats de pobresa i malnutrició. Segons el Banc Mundial, aproximadament el 75% dels guatemalencs viuen per sota del llindar de pobresa—definit com la manca d'ingressos suficients per adquirir béns i serveis bàsics. Gairebé el 58% de la població viu per sota del llindar de pobresa extrema, és a dir, sense poder adquirir una dieta bàsica. "Aquesta és l'arrel de la crisi alimentària i nutricional que viu el nostre país", va dir Colom. "Hi ha aliments disponibles. El que no tenim són els recursos perquè els afectats puguin comprar-los. No esperem a tenir una fam perquè actuem."

La pobresa és especialment greu entre la població indígena i aquells que viuen a les zones rurals. A les terres altes—on resideixen moltes comunitats indígenes—set de cada deu infants menors de cinc anys pateixen desnutrició, segons el Programa Mundial d'Aliments. Aproximadament el 40% dels 13,2 milions d'habitants de Guatemala són indígenes maies, segons el CIA World Fact Book.

article_content: Go First, formerly a budget airline in India, halted its flights in May after experiencing recurring engine issues and the departure of several pilots. The Indian aviation industry is notorious for its low profit margins, frequent challenges, and increasing control by a few major players, making it difficult for newcomers without industry background to succeed. Recently, Jindal Power—a Naveen Jindal group company previously interested in acquiring Go First—decided not to submit a financial bid after a month-long review. Complications over how many aircraft the airline could retain, stemming from recent changes in bankruptcy laws, made it hard to assess its value, leading Jindal Power to pull out ahead of the November 22 bid deadline. Changes to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code have now given aircraft lessors the rights to reclaim planes if lease payments are missed, even if the airline is under insolvency proceedings. This shift from earlier policy has Go First's creditors worried that these new rules, if applied to current cases, could further erode the airline's value as lessors recover their aircraft, making the company less appealing for buyers and putting lenders’ funds at greater risk. Go First's difficulties stem from both technical and financial challenges. The airline has attributed its groundings to engine failures supplied by Pratt & Whitney, whereas Pratt & Whitney has cited Go First’s history of payment defaults. Reports also indicate that Go First’s financial strain during the COVID-19 crisis led to postponed maintenance work. India has developed a reputation as a challenging environment for airlines. Several major and minor carriers—including Kingfisher and Jet Airways—have collapsed under heavy financial losses. High operating expenses, strong competition, and highly price-sensitive customers mean many private airlines don’t survive more than a few years. Today, India's domestic aviation market is consolidating around two large airlines. IndiGo holds nearly 63% market share with ambitious fleet expansion plans. Air India, now under Tata Group, is set to merge with Vistara while already absorbing AirAsia India and Air India Express, accumulating nearly 25% market share. As IndiGo and Air India grow, smaller airlines continue to lose ground or struggle to remain viable. Go First’s fate is undecided, SpiceJet has reported years of losses, and while Akasa Air has expanded, it remains small and recently experienced a wave of pilot departures. In other news, the Indian tax department discovered widespread tax evasion among brands selling on social media, and allegations of assault were made against Raymond MD Gautam Singhania by his estranged wife Nawaz Modi.

Recentment, Jindal Power — una empresa del grup de Naveen Jindal que estava interessada en comprar Go First — va decidir no presentar oferta financera després d’un mes de revisió. La incertesa sobre quants avions podria conservar l’aerolínia, degut als canvis recents en la llei concursal, va dificultar la valoració i va portar Jindal Power a retirar-se abans del termini d’ofertes del 22 de novembre. Amb les noves modificacions en el Codi Concursal, els arrendadors d'avions poden recuperar-los si no es paguen els lloguers, encara que l’aerolínia estigui en situació d’insolvència. Aquest canvi respecte a la norma anterior preocupa els creditors de Go First: si s’aplica el nou criteri al seu cas, el valor de la firma decau perquè els arrendadors recuperen els avions, cosa que complica trobar compradors i posa en risc la recuperació dels diners dels creditors. Els problemes de Go First tenen arrels tècniques i financeres. L’aerolínia acusa les fallades dels motors de Pratt & Whitney, però aquesta empresa afirma que Go First tenia un mal historial de pagaments. A més, segons diverses informacions, la pressió financera durant la COVID-19 va provocar que s’ajornés el manteniment. L'Índia té fama de ser un cementiri per a les aerolínies: moltes, incloses Kingfisher i Jet Airways, han caigut per pèrdues financeres. L’alt cost d’operació, la forta competència i clients molt sensibles al preu fan que moltes aerolínies privades no superin pocs anys. Actualment, el mercat domèstic d'aviació es concentra en dues grans aerolínies. IndiGo té gairebé el 63% de quota de mercat i s’expandeix amb noves aeronaus. Air India, sota el grup Tata, es fusionarà amb Vistara i ja ha integrat AirAsia India i Air India Express, assolint prop del 25% del mercat. Amb el predomini d’IndiGo i Air India, les petites aerolínies perden presència o lluiten per sobreviure. El futur de Go First és incert, SpiceJet arrastra anys de pèrdues i, tot i que Akasa Air està en creixement, es manté petita i fa poc ha perdut molts pilots. En altres notícies, Hisenda ha descobert frau fiscal entre marques que venen per xarxes socials i l’esposa separada de Gautam Singhania, director de Raymond, l’ha acusat d’agressió.

Newly published statistics have revealed that less than 1% of racism allegations made against police forces in England and Wales since 2005 have been substantiated. Of 7,963 reported complaints, only 77 were upheld, and 43 officers faced no disciplinary measures even after discrimination was found. This information, obtained by Channel 4’s Dispatches through Freedom of Information requests, has fueled concerns over the effectiveness of police efforts to eradicate racism.

Data shows that between 2005 and 2012, the Metropolitan Police—Britain’s largest force—upheld just 20 out of 4,730 racism complaints, equivalent to only 0.4%. During the same period, Greater Manchester, North Yorkshire, and Lancashire police forces did not uphold any complaints of racism. Despite numerous official promises following the 1999 Macpherson report, which highlighted institutional racism in the Metropolitan Police, progress appears limited.

Dame Anne Owers, chair of the Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC), acknowledged that race discrimination complaints are handled poorly, stating they are less likely to be upheld than other types of complaints. Stuart Lawrence, whose brother Stephen’s murder led to the Macpherson report, condemned the process after his own complaint was upheld by the IPCC but later dismissed by police, urging for more forceful action more than 20 years after his brother’s murder.

Mike Cunningham of the Association of Chief Police Officers affirmed that racism is unacceptable in the police and that officers falling short of expected standards should be dismissed. Since the Dispatches investigation was filmed, three police officers have been dismissed, although another officer accused in a civil case remains on the force.

Aquesta informació, obtinguda pel programa Dispatches de Channel 4 a través de sol·licituds d’accés a la informació, ha generat dubtes sobre l’eficàcia dels esforços policials per eradicar el racisme.

Durant el mateix període, les policies de Greater Manchester, North Yorkshire i Lancashire no van admetre cap de les denúncies rebudes. Malgrat les nombroses promeses institucionals després de l’informe Macpherson de 1999, que va posar de manifest el racisme institucional a la Metropolitan Police, els avenços semblen limitats.

Mike Cunningham, de l’Association of Chief Police Officers, va dir que el racisme no té lloc a la policia i que els agents que no compleixin els estàndards esperats han de ser acomiadats. Després del reportatge de Dispatches, tres agents han estat acomiadats, tot i que un altre agent acusat en un cas civil encara segueix al cos.

article_content: On Monday, Donald Trump took the stand in a New York courtroom, facing Judge Arthur Engoron, who holds the future of his real estate business. Trump's company has already been found liable for fraud, and now Judge Engoron—not a jury—must decide on possible penalties, including a fine of up to $250 million and restrictions on Trump's ability to do business in the state. During testimony, Trump was combative, directly challenging the judge, which led to heated exchanges and admonishments for introducing topics not directly relevant to the case. This approach appeared to irritate Judge Engoron, who will ultimately determine any penalties. Kevin McMunigal, a former federal prosecutor and law professor at Case Western University, told the BBC, 'It seems counterintuitive, especially since the judge finds both facts and law. Either Trump can't control himself, or this is a deliberate strategy.' If Trump's team is acting strategically, experts suggest the aim could be to provoke the judge into making comments or actions that may support an appeal on grounds of bias. Trump's lawyers are expected to appeal and have discussed a potential mistrial, referencing alleged bias involving communications between the judge and his law clerk. Judge Engoron largely did not engage when Trump criticized him. Throughout the trial, Trump has portrayed the lawsuit as a politically motivated 'witch-hunt,' calling both Judge Engoron and New York Attorney General Letitia James corrupt. His legal team has denied any wrongdoing and has described the judge as hostile. Both Professor McMunigal and former prosecutor Renato Mariotti note such attacks on the judge are typically a last resort, used when a legal team believes it is unlikely to win. Mariotti observed Trump's conduct signals his team may feel they have already lost, also noting that invoking the Fifth Amendment and refusing to answer questions could be a safer legal approach. Some experts warn that Trump's courtroom behavior risks contempt of court charges and sizeable fines. Mitchell Epner, another former federal prosecutor, said the judge could have imposed fines or taken additional action over Trump's conduct. 'Whatever the judge does will likely be intended to curb Trump’s behavior,' he said. As testimony continued, both Trump and Judge Engoron became less combative. Carl Tobias, a law professor at the University of Richmond, observed that Trump—currently leading in the Republican race for president—may be using the trial as a platform to campaign and portray himself as a victim. Trump has already appealed the original fraud finding and may hope to prevail on appeal. Former US district attorney Leslie Caldwell noted that Trump's narrative of unfair prosecution appears to resonate with many people. Trump has previously used legal troubles to his advantage, raising more than $4 million within 24 hours of his Georgia mugshot release. Ongoing legal cases have also bolstered his lead in Republican primary polls.

Durant la declaració, Trump va ser combatiu i va desafiar directament el jutge, fet que va provocar intercanvis tensos i recriminacions per introduir temes no pertinents al cas. Aquesta actitud va semblar irritar el jutge Engoron, que finalment determinarà les possibles sancions. O bé Trump no es pot controlar, o bé és una estratègia deliberada.' Si l’estratègia de l’equip de Trump és deliberada, alguns experts suggereixen que la intenció seria provocar el jutge perquè faci algun comentari o acció que poguessin utilitzar per recórrer la sentència per suposada parcialitat. Els advocats de Trump es preveu que apel·lin i han parlat de demanar un nou judici pel que consideren parcialitat en la comunicació entre el jutge i la seva assistent legal. El jutge Engoron en general no va respondre als atacs de Trump. Tant el professor McMunigal com l’exfiscal Renato Mariotti remarquen que atacar el jutge sovint és l’últim recurs, només fet quan l’equip legal creu que és poc probable guanyar. Mariotti va indicar que la conducta de Trump mostra que el seu equip assumeix que ja han perdut, i destaca que acollir-se al Cinquè Esmena i no respondre podria ser més segur estratègicament. Alguns experts alerten que el comportament de Trump a la sala de justícia podria portar a càrrecs per desacatament i multes considerables. Mitchell Epner, un altre exfiscal federal, va afirmar que el jutge hauria pogut imposar multes o prendre mesures addicionals pel comportament de Trump. 'Sigui el que sigui que decideixi el jutge, segurament serà per intentar frenar la conducta de Trump,' va dir. A mesura que el testimoni continuava, tant Trump com el jutge Engoron es van mostrar menys combatius. Carl Tobias, professor de dret a la Universitat de Richmond, va observar que Trump—actual favorit de les primàries republicanes—pot estar aprofitant el judici per fer campanya i presentar-se com a víctima. Trump ja ha recorregut la decisió de frau i pot esperar guanyar en apel·lació. L’exfiscal federal Leslie Caldwell va comentar que la narrativa de persecució injusta de Trump sembla que arriba a molta gent. article_content:
Joan Fontcuberta, a renowned Spanish conceptual artist, is celebrated for his art that challenges perceptions of truth and authority. Over his career, he has orchestrated elaborate hoaxes that blur the line between reality and fiction, prompting audiences to question what is genuine.

One of his early works, 'Fauna' (1987), involved presenting fabricated archives of a supposed German zoologist, Dr. Peter Ameisenhaufen. The collection showcased samples of fictitious animals, misleading even seasoned observers. In 1997, Fontcuberta staged another major hoax featuring a non-existent Russian cosmonaut named Ivan Istochnikov, whose disappearance in 1967 was 'covered up.' Many, including Spanish television, initially accepted this story as fact, only to later discover that the cosmonaut's name was a Russian translation of Fontcuberta’s own.

Recently, Fontcuberta curated the 'Trepat Collection' in Paris, which combined authentic photographs from the 1940s and 50s with his own imitative works, presenting them all as a unified archive. His playful approach continues with 'Stranger than Fiction,' a major retrospective at London’s Science Museum (July 23 – November 9, 2014). The exhibition features bizarre taxidermy, such as a squirrel with a snake’s tail and a winged goat, images of 'constellations' formed from car windshield dust, and staged photographs depicting Fontcuberta performing 'miracles' as a monk. Visually striking and laced with humor, the exhibition engages visitors in exploring questions about reality.

Fontcuberta’s fascination with ambiguity was shaped by personal experiences. As a teenager, he was injured during chemistry experiments, resulting in the loss of part of his left index finger. This incident led him to hide his hand and develop an awareness of 'multiple truths.' Exempted from military service, he devoted his time to photography, embracing reflective artistic methods rather than fast-paced photojournalism.

Raised under Francisco Franco’s dictatorship in Spain, Fontcuberta became attuned to the dangers of propaganda and authoritarianism. He explains, 'Franco was just one manifestation of authority—I challenge all forms of it: religious, scientific, political, or artistic. I don’t believe in hierarchies.' While he describes his views as a mix of socialism, anarchy, and pragmatism, Fontcuberta insists that challenging systems is essential in a democracy.

He likens his role to that of an oculist, trying to ensure that the 'eye' of photography remains honest by questioning what is presented. Although raised Catholic, he ultimately became agnostic, frequently poking fun at religious dogma. 'Dogma leads to stupidity. I think we should keep questioning,' he says.

Looking ahead, Fontcuberta maintains that he is not a liar but an artist who inspires doubt and curiosity. 'I just create ambiguities and encourage people to question things,' he says, remaining optimistic about humanity despite the warnings of those close to him.

Joan Fontcuberta, reconegut artista conceptual espanyol, destaca per les seves obres que desafien la percepció de la veritat i l’autoritat. Al llarg de la seva trajectòria, ha orquestrat bromes elaborades que difuminen la frontera entre realitat i ficció, provocant que el públic es qüestioni què és real.

Un dels seus primers treballs, 'Fauna' (1987), consistia a presentar arxius ficticis d’un suposat zoòleg alemany, el Dr. Peter Ameisenhaufen. La col·lecció mostrava espècimens d’animals imaginaris, enganyant fins i tot observadors experimentats. El 1997, Fontcuberta va protagonitzar una altra enginyosa farsa inventant el cosmonauta rus inexistent Ivan Istochnikov, la desaparició del qual el 1967 hauria estat 'ocultada'. Molts, inclosa la televisió espanyola, van donar credibilitat a la història abans de descobrir que el nom era la traducció russa del propi artista.

Recentment, Fontcuberta va comissariar la 'Col·lecció Trepat' a París, que barrejava fotografies autèntiques dels anys quaranta i cinquanta amb les seves pròpies propostes, presentant-les com un únic arxiu. El seu esperit juganer persisteix amb l’exposició 'Stranger than Fiction', una gran retrospectiva al Science Museum de Londres (del 23 de juliol al 9 de novembre de 2014). S’hi poden veure taxidèrmies sorprenents, com un esquirol amb cua de serp i una cabra amb ales, imatges de 'constel·lacions' creades amb pols sobre un parabrisa i fotografies on Fontcuberta, vestit de monjo, representa 'miracles'. Visualment impactant i farcida d’ironia, l’exposició convida els visitants a reflexionar sobre la realitat.

La fascinació de Fontcuberta per l’ambigüitat pren arrel en experiències personals. De jove es va fer mal en experiments químics, perdent part de l’índex esquerre. Això el va portar a amagar la mà i a veure la vida en termes de 'veritats múltiples'. Exempt del servei militar, es va dedicar a la fotografia amb una vessant més meditativa que el fotoperiodisme ràpid.

Criat sota la dictadura de Francisco Franco, Fontcuberta va desenvolupar un escepticisme envers la propaganda i l’autoritat. Explica: 'Franco era només una manifestació d’autoritat—desafio tota mena d’autoritat: religiosa, científica, política o artística. No crec en jerarquies.' Es defineix amb una combinació de socialisme, anarquia i pragmatisme, i defensa que cal qüestionar el sistema en democràcia.

Compara la seva tasca amb la d’un oculista, assegurant que la 'mirada' fotogràfica sigui honesta qüestionant el que es mostra. Tot i una educació catòlica, es va declarar agnòstic i no dubta a ironitzar sobre el dogma religiós. 'El dogma porta a la ximpleria. Cal mantenir la ment oberta,' diu.

Mirant al futur, Fontcuberta sosté que no és un mentider, sinó un artista que inspira dubte i curiositat. 'Només genero ambigüitats i animo la gent a qüestionar-se les coses', reafirma, mostrant-se optimista amb la humanitat tot i els advertiments familiars.

article_content: After losing her mother to lung cancer, Kelsey Mackay is supporting calls for targeted lung cancer screening in Scotland. Her mother, Christine Livingstone, a lifelong smoker, died at 52. Cancer Research UK suggests that thousands of deaths could be prevented through a national screening programme, and the charity plans to make its case to Health Secretary Michael Matheson. Kelsey was 20 when her mother first became ill. 'Mum just thought she had a chest infection at first,' recalls Kelsey, now 31. 'The earlier cancer is detected, the better the likely outcome. I wish things could have turned out differently for my family.' Christine Livingstone died in St John's Hospital, West Lothian, on 19 September 2013. Kelsey, from Armadale, West Lothian, said, 'Mum was my best friend and I miss her every day.' According to new analysis by Cancer Research UK, targeted lung cancer screening could save at least 2,300 lives in Scotland over the next decade. The UK National Screening Committee has recommended that all home nations implement lung cancer screening for people aged 55–74 who currently or previously smoked. Screening programmes are known to reduce cancer deaths by enabling earlier diagnosis or prevention. Christine's cancer took four months to diagnose, despite sudden weight loss and a persistent cough. In July 2012, she was diagnosed with small cell lung cancer and underwent 12 weeks of treatment, including chemotherapy and radiotherapy. By Christmas, scan results were positive, and the family was hopeful. In May 2013, Christine was well enough to travel to Marbella to celebrate her daughter’s 21st birthday. 'Mum loved swimming in the pool and eating well. All she wanted was to relax on a beach and enjoy the sunshine,' Kelsey said. However, after returning from Spain, Christine developed dizziness; scans showed the cancer had spread to her brain. Doctors gave her six months to live. 'Mum declined quickly. I first cared for her at home with support from Marie Curie nurses, but she eventually died in hospital. She had looked forward to being a grandmother and even knitted baby clothes for my future children. I treasure those clothes, and my children have grown up hearing about her,' Kelsey added. Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer death in Scotland, with rates three times higher in the most deprived areas. While lung checks have begun in England, Scotland currently lacks an equivalent initiative. Most lung cancer patients in Scotland are diagnosed at a late stage (3 or 4), according to Cancer Research UK. Kelsey hopes for a healthier future for the next generation: 'I wish we’d had more time with my mum. She grew up in a Scotland where smoking was common. Mum smoked about 40 cigarettes a day, and her own mother also died from a smoking-related illness. My duty to my children is to help break that cycle.' Cancer Research UK estimates that if screening were introduced, around 400 additional lung cancer cases could be identified early (stage 1 or 2) each year in Scotland—around 4,000 over a decade. The charity’s CEO, Michelle Mitchell, will advocate for a screening programme at the Scottish Cancer Conference in Glasgow, meeting with Health Secretary Michael Matheson. "A strong commitment from the Scottish government to a national targeted lung cancer screening programme could significantly reduce deaths," Mitchell stated. "Other cancers have seen diagnostic improvements, but long-term lung cancer survival in the UK remains almost unchanged over 50 years. Earlier diagnosis through targeted screening can help thousands live longer, healthier lives." A screening study is underway in NHS Lothian, and new funding will invite patients from NHS Grampian, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde, and NHS Highlands and Islands for lung checks. The study aims to guide a nationwide programme, addressing staffing and service access. A Scottish government spokesperson welcomed the call for targeted screening, noting that the UK National Screening Committee recognized several complexities. 'We have established a Scottish Expert Advisory Group with the National Screening Oversight (NSO) to evaluate the recommendations,' the spokesperson said. 'We’ve also funded a one-year extension of the University of Edinburgh’s LungScot study on targeted checks for high-risk individuals.'
translated_content: Després de perdre la seva mare a causa del càncer de pulmó, Kelsey Mackay dona suport a les crides per instaurar un cribratge selectiu de càncer de pulmó a Escòcia. La seva mare, Christine Livingstone, fumadora de tota la vida, va morir amb 52 anys. Cancer Research UK suggereix que es podrien evitar milers de morts amb un programa nacional de cribratge, i la fundació vol presentar la proposta al Secretari de Salut, Michael Matheson. La Kelsey tenia 20 anys quan la seva mare va emmalaltir per primera vegada. 'La mare pensava que només era una infecció de pit,' recorda ara la Kelsey, que té 31 anys. 'Com més aviat es detecta el càncer, millor n’és el pronòstic. Tant de bo les coses haguessin estat diferents per a la nostra família.' Christine Livingstone va morir a l’Hospital St John’s, a West Lothian, el 19 de setembre del 2013. La Kelsey, d’Armadale, West Lothian, diu: 'La mare era la meva millor amiga i l’enyoro cada dia.' Segons una nova anàlisi de Cancer Research UK, el cribratge selectiu podria salvar almenys 2.300 vides a Escòcia durant la propera dècada. El Comitè Nacional de Cribratge del Regne Unit recomana que totes les nacions implementin un cribratge de càncer de pulmó per a les persones de 55 a 74 anys que fumen o han fumat. Els programes de cribratge ajuden a reduir la mortalitat permetent un diagnòstic o prevenció precoç. El càncer de la Christine va trigar quatre mesos a diagnosticar-se, tot i la pèrdua de pes sobtada i una tos persistent. El juliol del 2012 li van diagnosticar un càncer de pulmó de cèl·lules petites i va seguir dotze setmanes de tractament amb quimioteràpia i radioteràpia. Per Nadal, els resultats de les proves eren positius i la família tenia esperança. Al maig del 2013, la Christine estava prou bé per viatjar a Marbella per celebrar el 21è aniversari de la seva filla. 'A la mare li encantava nedar a la piscina i menjar bé. Només volia relaxar-se en una platja i gaudir del sol', diu la Kelsey. Però al tornar d’Espanya, la Christine va començar a tenir marejos; les proves van revelar que el càncer s’havia estès al cervell. Els metges li van donar sis mesos de vida. 'La mare es va deteriorar ràpidament. Al principi vaig cuidar-la a casa amb l’ajuda de les infermeres de Marie Curie, però finalment va morir a l’hospital. Tenia moltes ganes de ser àvia i fins i tot va fer mitjons de nadó per als meus futurs fills. Els guardo com un tresor, i els meus fills han crescut escoltant històries sobre ella,' afegeix la Kelsey. El càncer de pulmó és la primera causa de mort per càncer a Escòcia, amb una taxa tres vegades més alta a les zones més desafavorides. A Anglaterra, ja s’han començat a fer revisions pulmonars, però a Escòcia encara no hi ha cap iniciativa equivalent. La majoria de pacients escocesos són diagnosticats quan el càncer ja està en una fase avançada (3 o 4), segons Cancer Research UK. La Kelsey espera un futur més saludable per a la nova generació: 'M’hagués agradat tenir més temps amb la mare. Va créixer en una Escòcia on fumar era habitual. Fumava unes 40 cigarretes al dia, i la seva mare també va morir d’una malaltia relacionada amb el tabac. El meu deure amb els meus fills és ajudar a trencar aquest cercle.' Cancer Research UK calcula que si s’implantés el cribratge, cada any es podrien detectar unes 400 persones addicionalment en una fase precoç (estadi 1 o 2), és a dir, unes 4.000 en una dècada. La directora general de l’organització, Michelle Mitchell, defensarà el programa en una trobada amb el secretari de Salut Michael Matheson durant la Conferència del Càncer d’Escòcia a Glasgow. “Un compromís ferm del govern escocès amb un programa nacional de cribratge selectiu de pulmó podria reduir considerablement les morts,” afirma Mitchell. “En altres càncers s’han fet progressos en el diagnòstic, però la supervivència a llarg termini del càncer de pulmó al Regne Unit gairebé no ha canviat en 50 anys. Un diagnòstic precoç a través del cribratge pot ajudar milers de persones a viure més i millor.” Ja s’està fent un estudi pilot a NHS Lothian, i els nous fons permetran convidar pacients de NHS Grampian, NHS Greater Glasgow i Clyde i NHS Highlands and Islands a sotmetre’s a revisions pulmonars. L’objectiu de l’estudi és preparar la implantació d’un programa nacional, valorant aspectes com el personal i l’accés als serveis. Un portaveu del govern escocès ha celebrat la proposta de cribratge selectiu, tot assenyalant que el Comitè Nacional de Cribratge del Regne Unit va reconèixer certes complexitats. 'Hem creat un grup d’experts escocesos en col·laboració amb National Screening Oversight (NSO) per avaluar les recomanacions,' ha dit el portaveu. 'A més, hem finançat un any extra de l’estudi de viabilitat LungScot de la Universitat d’Edimburg sobre revisions pulmonars per a persones amb alt risc.'

article_content: Despite one of its nine engines failing just over a minute after launch, SpaceX's Dragon capsule is still headed toward the International Space Station as planned. The Falcon 9 rocket, which lifted off from Cape Canaveral, Florida, experienced a sudden pressure drop in one engine. Automated systems kicked in, enabling the rocket to make the necessary adjustments and keep Dragon on course. The mission also included the launch of an Orbcomm communications satellite. Owing to the engine problem, the satellite ended up in a lower-than-intended orbit because it couldn't safely use its own engine to move higher. Engineers from Orbcomm and Sierra Nevada Corporation are now working to determine whether the satellite can reach its operational orbit using onboard propulsion. Currently, SpaceX is reviewing flight data to find out what caused the engine malfunction. Initial findings indicate that the No. 1 engine’s fairing was damaged by stress. Notably, the engine did not explode, and the rocket was able to continue with the mission. This mission is the first of twelve planned cargo deliveries that SpaceX will carry out under a NASA contract, as the agency increases cooperation with private aerospace firms for supply and future crewed flights. NASA is also working with Boeing and Sierra Nevada to develop next-generation astronaut transport vessels. In the next few months, Orbital Sciences is expected to attempt its own demonstration supply flight to the ISS, launching from Wallops Island, Virginia, under a nearly $2 billion NASA contract.

El coet Falcon 9, que es va enlairar des de Cap Canaveral, Florida, va experimentar una caiguda sobtada de pressió en un dels motors. Els sistemes automatitzats es van activar, permetent que el coet fes els ajustaments necessaris i la Dragon mantingués la ruta. La missió també incloïa el llançament d’un satèl·lit de comunicacions d’Orbcomm. A causa del problema al motor, el satèl·lit va acabar en una òrbita més baixa de la prevista perquè no podia utilitzar el seu propi motor de manera segura per pujar. Enginyers d’Orbcomm i Sierra Nevada Corporation estan treballant per determinar si el satèl·lit podrà arribar a la seva òrbita operativa amb la pròpia propulsió. Actualment, SpaceX revisa les dades de vol per identificar l’origen de la fallada del motor. Les primeres troballes indiquen que la coberta del motor número 1 va resultar danyada per l’estrès. Cal destacar que el motor no va explotar i el coet va poder continuar la missió. Aquesta missió és la primera d’una dotzena de vols de subministrament que SpaceX realitzarà per a la NASA, en un moment en què l’agència aposta per la col·laboració amb empreses privades tant per a la càrrega com per a futures missions tripulades. NASA també treballa amb Boeing i Sierra Nevada en el desenvolupament de naus per al transport d’astronautes. En els pròxims mesos, Orbital Sciences preveu realitzar la seva pròpia missió de demostració de subministrament a l’Estació Espacial, sortint de Wallops Island, Virginia, sota un contracte de gairebé 2.000 milions de dòlars amb la NASA.

article_content:
Microsoft has finalized its highly anticipated acquisition of Activision Blizzard, paying $69 billion (£56 billion) for the deal. While the transaction is significant, many gaming fans are curious about its direct impact on their gaming experience. Call of Duty, one of the best-selling video game franchises, will remain accessible on multiple platforms for the foreseeable future. A 15-year agreement grants Ubisoft cloud gaming rights for all past and future Activision Blizzard games, preventing exclusivity on Xbox until at least 2038. Microsoft agreed to these terms to satisfy concerns from UK regulators about potential dominance in the cloud gaming sector.

Cloud gaming allows users to stream video games over the internet, similar to how Netflix streams movies. Major gaming subscription services like Ubisoft+, PlayStation Plus, and Xbox Game Pass have gained popularity. Activision Blizzard announced on X that it expects to add its titles to Game Pass starting next year, potentially making new releases, including Call of Duty, available on Xbox from launch day.

Previously, Sony often secured exclusives or early access with Call of Duty, but this dynamic may be changing. Microsoft has a pattern of offering its blockbuster games on Game Pass from day one, allowing players to choose between purchasing games outright or subscribing to access them. UK regulators insisted that Activision Blizzard games remain available on services other than Xbox’s for 15 years.

This requirement addresses concerns stemming from Microsoft’s history of exclusivity, such as with Starfield, which launched exclusively for PC and Xbox in September 2023. Despite continued PlayStation releases, Microsoft stands to benefit from increased industry influence. Ubisoft’s streaming rights will last 15 years, but much of the industry’s revenue now comes from microtransactions and downloadable content. In 2022, Activision Blizzard generated $5.89 billion from these sources compared to $1.6 billion from traditional game sales. Sony typically receives around 30% from in-game purchases, meaning purchases in Call of Duty on PlayStation partly benefit a competing company.

Fans shared mixed reactions at gaming convention EGX. Oliver, 16, suggested the deal could increase funding for game development, while Sophie, Ubisoft’s content creator of the year, stressed the importance of game accessibility for all players. Some fans, however, are wary—especially those with nostalgia for PlayStation exclusives like Crash Bandicoot and Spyro the Dragon. This has even led to petitions asking Microsoft to ensure games remain multi-platform in the future.

The acquisition expands Microsoft’s presence in the UK, as Activision Blizzard operates studios in London, Guildford, and Warrington. The deal also includes King, famous for Candy Crush Saga. Ukie, representing UK gaming companies, told the BBC that international investment makes up a significant portion of the nation’s industry, noting that 89% of investment from 2017 to 2022 came from outside the UK.

Microsoft’s acquisition history includes buying Rare in 2002 and Minecraft developer Mojang in 2014. With more than 20 studios now under its umbrella, Microsoft has become an increasingly dominant force in gaming, set to own a host of hugely popular titles going forward.

Històricament, Microsoft ha comprat altres estudis destacats, com Rare l’any 2002 i Mojang (Minecraft) el 2014. Ara, amb més de 20 estudis al seu paraigua, Microsoft és una força dominant cada cop més gran en el món dels videojocs, amb un ampli ventall de franquícies populars.

article_content: Israeli forces have placed Gaza under siege and are conducting airstrikes in response to recent deadly attacks by Hamas in southern Israel, causing widespread fear among Gaza's civilians about depleting food supplies within the week. Ivan Karakashian, leading advocacy for the Norwegian Refugee Council's Jerusalem office, told Insider that essential goods could run out in four to six days. According to Karakashian, basic staples like flour, milk, and eggs have quickly disappeared from neighborhood shops, making it extremely hard for residents to access necessities. He noted that as of Tuesday, around 210,000 Palestinians have been displaced by ongoing attacks, and the number is increasing rapidly as more buildings are destroyed. Karakashian described scenes of families, including women and children, carrying what they can from destroyed homes and wandering the streets, unsure where to turn for safety as the bombings continue. Although Israeli authorities have advised residents to evacuate areas targeted for airstrikes, Karakashian emphasized that, in reality, nowhere in Gaza offers true safety. The crisis is further intensified by a shortage of fuel needed to provide electricity. Fuel that was supposed to arrive through the Rafah crossing was blocked after Israeli airstrikes, leaving only enough fuel for essential services until Wednesday, and currently, Gaza receives just four hours of electricity per day. Karakashian warned that if the remaining fuel runs out, all electricity — including for medical facilities — will be cut off, pushing Gaza into an even more critical state. The Gaza Ministry of Health reported at least 830 Palestinians have died. On the Israeli side, officials say the death toll has surpassed 1,000 since the weekend attacks by Hamas. The militant group also claims to be holding around 100 Israeli hostages in Gaza, though estimates from the Israeli Defense Forces suggest the number is over 30.

article_content: When most brides-to-be dream of a fairytale wedding, they probably don't envision this. Movie fans Raymond Wickett, 56, and Jacqueline Perkins, 52, brought their love of film to life by dressing as the green ogres Shrek and Fiona for their wedding ceremony. Both from Stoke Heath in Coventry, they wanted to create an unforgettable day for themselves and a special memory for their grandchildren. The entire wedding party embraced the theme, dressing up as characters from the Shrek films. The best man acted as Donkey, while Jacqueline's daughter arrived as Puss in Boots, voiced by Antonio Banderas in the movies. The wedding, which took two years to plan, was held at Coventry Register Office on December 12, 2012—a date chosen for its uniqueness. Jacqueline explained that, having had a traditional white wedding previously, she wanted something different this time. "We wanted to make people happy and turn heads—it was more fun than a regular wedding and brought joy to our guests," she said. Raymond, a bus driver, added, "We picked 12/12/12 because it was a once-in-a-lifetime date. The day exceeded our expectations; the atmosphere was fantastic, and everyone had a wonderful time."

Tots dos, de Stoke Heath, Coventry, volien crear un dia inoblidable per a ells i un record especial per als seus néts. El casament, que va trigar dos anys a planificar-se, es va celebrar al Registre Civil de Coventry el 12 de desembre de 2012, una data escollida pel seu simbolisme. article_content: A man was cleared today of murdering his wife during their honeymoon in order to claim more than £130,000 from her life insurance. Colette Davies, 39, from Bridgend, South Wales, died after falling 80 feet from a viewing platform over a gorge at an Indian beauty spot in February 2004. John Clifton Davies, 51, from Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire, was released from custody after spending the last 16 months detained. He had been accused of murdering his wife in 2004, just 14 months after their wedding and one week into their vacation. Mr. Davies was also charged with fraudulently claiming an insurance payment of £132,000 after her death. However, at Cardiff Crown Court yesterday, the prosecution offered no evidence against Mr. Davies after new witnesses came forward. The couple married in 2003 and traveled to India on a delayed honeymoon 14 months later. Colette's body was found in a ravine near the town of Gaura. Indian police originally investigated the death and ruled out suspicious circumstances. Her body was returned to Bridgend, South Wales, and an inquest recorded an open verdict. A fresh UK police inquiry led to Davies being arrested and charged in November 2011. South Wales Police reviewed the case in consultation with the family and set up an incident room. Officers traveled to India and visited the site near Gaura where her body was discovered. They also re-interviewed over a dozen witnesses before returning to Britain. Felicity Galvin, Senior Crown Prosecutor in Wales, said the Crown Prosecution Service worked closely with South Wales Police as their investigation developed. In November 2011, with the available evidence, Davies was charged with murder and two counts of fraud. As is standard, the investigation continued after charges were filed. Officers from South Wales Police later visited Himachal Pradesh, India, and uncovered significant new information from two previously unknown witnesses who could provide direct eyewitness testimony. The prosecution at Cardiff Crown Court subsequently offered no evidence against Mr. Davies following these developments. The CPS reviewed the case and concluded that the evidence was insufficient for both murder and fraud charges. As a result, prosecution counsel formally informed the court that no evidence would be offered against John Clifton Davies.

El CPS va revisar novament el cas i va concloure que les proves no eren suficients ni per a càrrecs d’assassinat ni de frau. article_content: Denis MacShane, a former Labour minister and MP for Rotherham, pleaded guilty to making nearly £13,000 in false expense claims. MacShane submitted forged receipts for research and translation services between 2005 and 2008 to fund trips to Europe, including judging a literary competition in Paris. His actions are part of the broader 2009 MP expenses scandal, which exposed misuse of parliamentary funds. Initially, MacShane downplayed the scandal and dismissed public criticism, even calling it a 'wonderful moment of British fiddling' in a newspaper article. An investigation by the Commons standards commissioner, John Lyon, found that MacShane falsified 19 invoices from a body he controlled, the European Policy Institute. Parliament initially withheld critical correspondence under the principle of parliamentary privilege, delaying police investigations. Eventually, after new evidence surfaced, MacShane resigned, repaid the money, and expressed deep regret over his 'grotesque mistake.' He faces sentencing on December 19 and is the sixth MP prosecuted over the expenses scandal. Other MPs and peers, including Elliot Morley, David Chaytor, Jim Devine, Eric Illsley, Margaret Moran, Lord Hanningfield, and Lord Taylor of Warwick, have also been convicted for similar offenses. In related cases, Chris Huhne, a former energy secretary, and his ex-wife Vicky Pryce have served jail sentences for perverting the course of justice.

article_content: Attention-grabbing claims like 'there will be more plastic than fish in the ocean by 2050' or that 'people consume a credit card’s worth of plastic each week' frequently appear in the media, yet these aren't strongly backed by science. Scientists behind these claims have disputed them and revised their figures, citing flawed assumptions and underestimations of fish stocks. New research shows people consume much less microplastic than these soundbites suggest—less than a grain of salt a week, meaning it would take thousands of years to ingest a credit card’s worth. Interviews with households in the UK, Spain, and Germany about recycling revealed much confusion about plastic pollution's sources and risks. To address this, the 'Plastic Mythbusters' project launched with the Hereon Institute of Coastal Environmental Chemistry and communications experts, aiming to dispel common myths. Negotiations are underway in Nairobi at the United Nations to create a binding global plastics treaty covering the full life cycle of plastics, from production to disposal. The Scientists’ Coalition for an Effective Plastics Treaty urges that all treaty decisions be evidence-based. Media plays a big role in shaping public and policy views on plastic pollution. Programs like BBC’s Blue Planet II, which aired globally in 2017, used striking scenes—like a pilot whale mourning her calf, which was suggested to have died from plastic contamination. Still, there’s no scientific proof in that scene directly linking plastics to the whale’s death. These dramatic images can increase concern, illustrated by a doubling of internet searches about ocean plastic after Blue Planet II and responses from politicians such as then-UK environment secretary Michael Gove, who announced measures to reduce plastic waste. Yet, evidence tying the show to long-term behavioral change is limited. How the media frames plastic issues impacts what solutions are emphasized. Many believe the Great Pacific Garbage Patch is a solid trash island, but scientists say it’s more like a 'plastic smog' of trillions of micro- and nanoplastics spread over a huge area. This makes technical cleanups less effective than simply reducing plastic production. Media often focuses on individual actions like avoiding single-use plastics, rather than promoting systemic solutions like limiting production or highlighting links to climate change and biodiversity. The UN treaty now covers the full life cycle of plastic pollution in all environments, not just oceans, broadening opportunities to discuss public perceptions. While media coverage is crucial for raising awareness, relying too much on emotive content may distract from the truly impactful policy solutions needed.
translated_content: Afirmacions cridaneres com «hi haurà més plàstic que peixos a l’oceà el 2050» o que «les persones consumeixen una targeta de crèdit de plàstic cada setmana» són habituals als mitjans, però manquen de base científica sòlida. Els científics darrere d’aquestes afirmacions les han qüestionat i han revisat les xifres, assenyalant supòsits erronis i una subestimació dels estocs de peix. Investigacions recents demostren que la quantitat real de microplàstics que ingerim és molt menor—menys d’un gra de sal setmanalment; farien falta milers d’anys per arribar al pes d’una targeta de crèdit. Entrevistes amb llars del Regne Unit, Espanya i Alemanya sobre reciclatge han posat de manifest la confusió generalitzada sobre l’origen i els riscos de la contaminació per plàstics. Per aquest motiu, en col·laboració amb l’Institut Hereon de Química Ambiental Costanera i experts en comunicació, ha nascut el projecte «Plastic Mythbusters» amb l’objectiu de desmentir mites habituals. A Nairobi, seu de les Nacions Unides, s’estan negociant un tractat global jurídicament vinculant sobre plàstics que abasti tot el cicle de vida del material, des de la producció fins a l’eliminació. La Coalició de Científics per a un Tractat Eficaç sobre Plàstics insisteix que les decisions es basin en evidència científica sòlida. Els mitjans juguen un paper decisiu en la formació de l’opinió pública i política sobre la contaminació per plàstics. Programes com Blue Planet II de la BBC, emès globalment el 2017, han mostrat escenes impactants—com el cas d’una balena pilot que plora el seu cadell, aparentment mort per intoxicació per plàstic. Tot i així, no hi ha proves científiques en aquella escena que relacionin directament el plàstic amb la mort de la cria. Aquestes imatges colpidores incrementen la preocupació, fet que es reflecteix en la duplicació de cerques a la xarxa sobre el plàstic als oceans després de Blue Planet II, així com en iniciatives polítiques com les de l’exministre britànic Michael Gove per lluitar contra els residus de plàstic. Amb tot, falten proves clares que el programa hagi generat canvis duradors en el comportament de la població. La manera com els mitjans exposen els problemes dels plàstics influeix sobre les solucions prioritzades. Molts pensen que la Gran taca d’escombraries del Pacífic és una massa sòlida quan, en realitat, els científics l’identifiquen més aviat com una “boira plàstica” formada per bilions de micro- i nanoplàstics repartits per grans extensions. Això dificulta una neteja tècnica efectiva i reforça la importància de reduir la producció de plàstic. Els mitjans fan sovint èmfasi en l’acció individual (com evitar plàstics d’un sol ús), en comptes de promoure solucions sistèmiques com limitar la producció o fer més visibles els vincles amb el canvi climàtic i la pèrdua de biodiversitat. Ara, el tractat de l’ONU aborda tot el cicle vital del plàstic a tots els entorns, cosa que permet ampliar el debat públic. Encara que la funció dels mitjans és clau per sensibilitzar, abusar de contingut emotiu pot desviar l’atenció de les polítiques veritablement efectives.

article_content: During a ceremony in St Peter's Square, Pope Francis compared having retired Pope Benedict XVI living at the Vatican to enjoying the wisdom of a grandparent at home. Addressing a crowd of tens of thousands, many of whom were grandparents and their families, Francis celebrated the valuable role of elderly people in society, including his predecessor Benedict, who made a rare appearance for the event. At the ceremony, Francis warmly embraced the 87-year-old Benedict, who walked with a cane and wore a white coat despite the warm weather. Francis, who was 77 at the time, spoke out against elderly care homes that resemble prisons, lamenting how older people are often forgotten or neglected. He argued that such treatment is a form of 'hidden euthanasia.' According to Francis, the elderly pass on wisdom and faith, calling these the most precious legacies they can offer. Benedict resigned as Pope on February 28, 2013, breaking a 600-year tradition by leaving the papacy while still alive, citing declining strength. After his resignation, some speculated he continued to exert influence as a ‘shadow’ Pope. Benedict has kept his papal name, lives in the Vatican, and still wears papal white, explaining it was simply the only clothing available when he retired. Francis succeeded him two weeks later, becoming the first non-European pontiff in almost 1,300 years.

article_content:
Greg Kelly, son of New York City Police Commissioner Ray Kelly, has been accused of sexual assault by a woman who says the incident occurred last October. She alleges she became pregnant from the encounter and later had an abortion, according to police sources. Greg Kelly was absent Thursday from his co-anchor role on 'Good Day New York.' Through his lawyer, Kelly has denied all allegations. Lew Leone, general manager of the local Fox station, confirmed Kelly has requested time off during the ongoing investigation.

Kelly’s co-host, Rosanna Scotto, voiced her support, saying, 'I love Greg. That's all I can say.'

The Manhattan district attorney is leading the investigation instead of the NYPD to avoid any conflict of interest. The woman reported the alleged incident this week, despite saying it happened in October. Kelly, a former Fox News correspondent and Marine Corps veteran, is cooperating, according to a statement from his lawyer Andrew Lankler, who said, 'Greg Kelly strenuously denies any wrongdoing' and expects the investigation will clear him.

The woman, reportedly around 30 years old, claims she and Kelly met by chance, went for drinks at the South Street Seaport, and later to her law office in downtown Manhattan, where she says the assault occurred. Her boyfriend, upset by the alleged events, confronted Commissioner Ray Kelly at a public event, where Ray Kelly suggested he submit the allegations in writing.

Friends of the accuser described her as emotionally distressed and reported her boyfriend's outrage.

Greg Kelly, 43, has worked for Fox News Channel since 2002, including time as White House correspondent and reporting from Baghdad. Before this, he worked for New York 1 and NewsChannel 34. He remains a lieutenant colonel in the Marine Corps reserves. Ray Kelly returned to his role as NYPD commissioner in 2002, after prior service in the 1990s.

article_content: On Thursday, the Ondo State Executive Council expressed strong support for Governor Rotimi Akeredolu by passing a vote of confidence in his leadership. Governor Akeredolu is currently recuperating in Ibadan, Oyo State, following medical treatment in Germany. Of the 35 cabinet members, 33 signed a statement backing the governor. The remaining two, Razak Obe (Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources) and Akin Sowore (Commissioner for Commerce, Industry and Cooperative Services), did not sign. Obe explained he was not present in the state and was not provided the document before being asked for his signature, expressing concern about the lack of due process. Sowore declined to sign on principle, stating that cabinet appointees are by nature expected to support the governor and that such a vote of confidence is unnecessary and symbolic. The statement, signed by top officials including Secretary to the State Government Mrs. Oladunni Odu, Chief of Staff Mr. Olugbenga Ale, and Head of Service Mr. Kayode Ogundele, highlighted the governor’s achievements in governance, security, healthcare, agriculture, road infrastructure, and other sectors. The cabinet credited Akeredolu's leadership and the REDEEMED agenda for progress in the state. However, Akeredolu’s continued absence has drawn criticism from opposition groups like the Peoples Democratic Party, which has called for his resignation. Both Obe and Sowore reiterated that no recent executive meetings were held, with Sowore noting that since the governor resumed duty in September 2023, the council had not met. He also pointed out that the act of passing a vote of confidence was driven by political actors seeking to create tension, not by actual cabinet deliberation. Governor Akeredolu remains in Ibadan as he continues his recovery.

article_content: The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has indicated that two bills may soon be debated to address persistent unemployment and promote the recognition of Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo as national languages in Nigeria. The National Apprenticeship Scheme bill and another bill to allow more national languages to be recognized alongside English are in development and may soon be introduced to the House, Kalu stated on Saturday. Speaking in Abuja while hosting the management team of Buildup Integrated Services, led by CEO Chibuike Aguene, Kalu explained that the bills are designed to establish a legal framework for expanding skills and employment opportunities for Nigeria's growing population of unskilled youth. A statement signed by Kalu’s Chief Press Secretary, Levinus Nwabughiogu, quoted Kalu as stating the National Apprenticeship Scheme is a technology-driven, dual apprenticeship model designed by Buildup to blend theoretical education with practical training. Kalu highlighted the significant number of unskilled youths in Nigeria, noting that the ‘Igba-Boi’ apprenticeship system, commonly practiced in the Southeast—where individuals learn a trade or vocation for a set period before being settled by their employer—would be formalized through legislative action. "An institutionalized dual apprenticeship system will bridge academic knowledge and practical expertise, ensuring individuals gain real-world application of their education and hands-on skills relevant to their chosen fields," Kalu said. Kalu, who represents Bende Federal Constituency in Abia State on the APC platform, further stated that the scheme aligns with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. He emphasized that while educational certificates are important, they must be complemented by practical skills to secure productive lives. Kalu referenced Germany and China as examples of economies propelled by practical skills rather than certificates. He expressed gratitude to Buildup Integrated Services for advancing skills training and entrepreneurship development in Nigeria and across Africa. "Your dedication to skills development and entrepreneurship supports our nation's aspirations for economic growth, job creation, and youth empowerment. I commend your organization’s work on the essential National Apprenticeship Scheme," Kalu added. He reiterated the commitment of the 10th House of Representatives to participatory governance and creating a regulatory environment supportive of entrepreneurship and the broader economy. Kalu acknowledged calls for legislation to institutionalize the National Apprenticeship Scheme and welcomed collaborative dialogue and stakeholder input to ensure the bill bridges the national skills gap and helps spark industrial growth. On the National Language Bill, Kalu noted that many young Nigerians learn better in their native dialects and emphasized the educational and cultural benefits of expanding the country’s official languages. He pledged support for the initiative and promised to support 3,000 youths across the federation in the first phase of the apprenticeship system to be led by Buildup Integrated Services. Chibuike Aguene, CEO of Buildup Integrated Services, called for legislative support to institutionalize the dual apprenticeship system in Nigeria.

Parlant a Abuja mentre rebia l’equip directiu de Buildup Integrated Services, liderat pel CEO Chibuike Aguene, Kalu va explicar que els projectes de llei volen establir un marc legal per ampliar les habilitats i les oportunitats d’ocupació per a la creixent població nigeriana de joves sense qualificació. Un comunicat signat pel Secretari de Premsa en Cap de Kalu, Levinus Nwabughiogu, citava Kalu dient que el Pla Nacional d’Aprenentatge és un model dual d’aprenentatge impulsat per la tecnologia, dissenyat per Buildup, que combina educació teòrica i formació pràctica. Kalu va destacar la gran quantitat de joves sense formació a Nigèria, i va assenyalar que el sistema d’aprenentatge “Igba-Boi”, comú al sud-est (on les persones aprenen un ofici durant un període acordat abans de ser establerts pel seu ocupador), seria formalitzat legislativament. “Un sistema dual d’aprenentatge institucionalitzat connectarà coneixement acadèmic i experiència pràctica, assegurant que les persones apliquin els seus estudis i tinguin les habilitats requerides pels seus camps escollits”, va afirmar Kalu. Kalu, que representa la Circumscripció Federal de Bende a l’estat d’Abia sota l’APC, va afegir que el pla s’alinea amb l’Agenda d’Esperança Renovada del president Bola Tinubu. Va subratllar que, tot i que els certificats acadèmics són importants, han d’anar acompanyats d’habilitats pràctiques per garantir vides productives. Kalu va citar Alemanya i la Xina com exemples d’economies impulsades per habilitats pràctiques més que per certificats. Va expressar agraïment a Buildup Integrated Services per impulsar la formació en habilitats i el desenvolupament empresarial a Nigèria i a tot el continent africà. “La vostra dedicació al desenvolupament d’habilitats i de l’emprenedoria dona suport a les aspiracions del nostre país per al creixement econòmic, la creació d’ocupació i l’apoderament juvenil. Felicito la vostra tasca en aquest important Pla Nacional d’Aprenentatge”, va afegir Kalu. Va reiterar el compromís de la 10a Cambra amb la governança participativa i amb la creació d’un entorn regulador favorable a l’emprenedoria i al conjunt de l’economia. Kalu va reconèixer les crides per legislar la institucionalització del Pla Nacional d’Aprenentatge i va donar la benvinguda al diàleg i la col·laboració de les parts interessades per assegurar que la llei cobreixi el gran desfasament d’habilitats i ajudi a impulsar el creixement industrial. Sobre el Projecte de Llei de Llengües Nacionals, Kalu va assenyalar que molts joves nigerians aprenen millor en els seus dialectes nadius i va destacar els beneficis educatius i culturals d’ampliar les llengües oficials del país. Va prometre suport a la iniciativa i va anunciar que donarà suport a 3.000 joves a tot el país en la primera fase del sistema d’aprenentatge encapçalat per Buildup Integrated Services. Chibuike Aguene, CEO de Buildup Integrated Services, va demanar suport legislatiu per institucionalitzar el sistema dual d’aprenentatge a Nigèria.

article_content: A rare television appearance featuring Samuel J. Seymour, the last known living witness to the assassination of Abraham Lincoln, has surfaced on YouTube. The video is from a February 1956 episode of the TV game show 'I've Got a Secret,' in which Seymour, then 95, appears as a guest. The show involved a panel trying to guess the guest's secret. In this episode, host Garry Moore escorts Seymour onto the set; Seymour is visibly injured, wearing a bandage on his head after a fall at his hotel. Host Moore explains that Seymour had taken a fall and sustained a black eye, but insisted on appearing after his doctor left the decision up to him. The secret, revealed onscreen for viewers, was: 'I saw John Wilkes Booth shoot Abraham Lincoln (April 14, 1865).' Seymour witnessed the assassination as a five-year-old at Ford's Theatre. Seymour had previously shared his story in the Milwaukee Sentinel. Moore tells the panel that Seymour didn't realize what had happened at the time — only that he saw a man leap from the balcony. That man was, of course, John Wilkes Booth. "I was scared to death," Seymour recalls on the show. Although the panel successfully guesses the secret, Seymour is awarded $80 and a can of Prince Albert pipe tobacco for his participation. Samuel J. Seymour died on April 12, 1956, about two months after his television appearance.

El programa consistia en un panell que intentava endevinar el secret del convidat. En aquest episodi, l’amfitrió Garry Moore acompanya Seymour a l’escenari; Seymour duu una bena al cap després d’una caiguda a l’hotel. Moore explica que Seymour va caure i es va fer un trau, però que va insistir a participar després que el metge deixés la decisió a les seves mans. Seymour va presenciar l’assassinat quan tenia cinc anys al Ford’s Theatre. Seymour ja havia explicat la seva història prèviament al Milwaukee Sentinel. Moore diu al panell que Seymour, en aquell moment, no va entendre què havia passat — només va veure un home saltar des del balcó. Aquest home era, naturalment, John Wilkes Booth. "Em vaig espantar molt", recorda Seymour al programa. Tot i que el panell va endevinar el secret, Seymour va rebre 80 dòlars i una llauna de tabac Prince Albert per participar-hi. Samuel J. Seymour va morir el 12 d’abril de 1956, aproximadament dos mesos després de la seva aparició televisiva.

article_content: Google is rolling out a new Google Assistant Tile feature for Wear OS smartwatches. First reported in August, the Tile lets users add custom commands as shortcuts to their watch's panel. Android expert Mishaal Rahman spotted the rollout after a tip from X user Lance Adams. The feature is available to Galaxy Watch and Pixel Watch users, allowing quick access to Google Assistant commands directly from the watch. Previously, Google Assistant was already present on some Wear OS devices, but required users to speak commands each time. The new Tile streamlines this process, enabling users to create ready-made commands accessed with a tap—no need to voice or type repeatedly. Opening the Tile shows generic actions like 'Send a message,' 'Turn off the lights,' or 'Set a five-minute timer,' with the option to create custom shortcuts via the microphone or keyboard icons. These saved commands can be used whenever needed. The Tile is especially timely as Google recently announced it will discontinue Assistant support on Wear OS 2. The Tile is now rolling out to devices on Wear OS 3 and 4, including the Galaxy Watch 4 and other compatible smartwatches. The Google Pixel Watch 2 is noted as one of the top smartwatches available, featuring excellent design, performance, clean software, and upgraded health tracking with Fitbit integration.

article_content: Kuwait's oil minister has unveiled a comprehensive strategy to increase fossil fuel production, including the development of infrastructure for the Durra gas field, which Kuwait shares with Saudi Arabia and is also claimed by Iran. The state-run Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC) is targeting a boost in overall oil production capacity to 4 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2035. Currently, Kuwait's production capacity stands at 2.9 million bpd and is projected to reach 3.2 million bpd by 2025 or 2026, according to Ahmed Jaber Al-Eidan, CEO of KPC subsidiary Kuwait Oil Company (KOC). OPEC data from August indicates that Kuwait’s crude oil production averaged about 2.55 million bpd. KPC's new strategy aims for its subsidiary KOC to reach an oil production capacity of 3.65 million bpd by 2035, potentially generating an additional $11 billion in revenue for the state over the next five years, as noted by KPC CEO Sheikh Nawaf Saud al-Sabah. KOC, responsible for roughly 90% of Kuwait's oil output, also plans to hit a gas production capacity of 1.5 trillion cubic feet per day by 2040. Kuwait's proven oil reserves are estimated at 100 billion barrels. To support its strategic goals, KPC plans to invest $410 billion through 2040, funded by company cash flow, debt, and partnerships with other companies, explained Bader Al Attar, KPC's managing director for planning and finance. Of this, $110 billion is allocated to support the group’s transition to cleaner energy. Oil Minister Saad Al Barrak reiterated KPC’s commitment to achieving net zero carbon emissions by 2050. Regarding the Durra gas field, Al Barrak described the offshore project as central to the government’s current legislative agenda. A KPC executive recently stated that the Durra field is expected to be fully operational by 2029. While Kuwait and Saudi Arabia signed a bilateral agreement last year to develop the field—estimated to hold about 20 trillion cubic feet of proven gas reserves—Iran has criticized this deal, asserting its own stake in the field and calling the agreement 'illegal.' Al Barrak has maintained that Kuwait and Saudi Arabia have exclusive rights to Durra and urged Iran to resolve border demarcations regarding its claim. On shared resources with Iraq, Sheikh Nawaf said Kuwait and Iraq are discussing the best mode of production for the Ratqa and Abdali oilfields. In 2019, both countries agreed to commission British firm ERC Equipoise to study the development of these joint border oilfields. KPC seeks to expand its overall refining capacity to 1.6 million bpd domestically and 425,000 bpd in overseas facilities by 2025. The Al Zour refinery complex in southern Kuwait is set to reach its full 615,000 bpd capacity imminently, according to Waleed Al Bader, CEO of Kuwait Integrated Petroleum Industries Company (KIPIC). The third refinery at Al Zour is expected to begin operations by the end of October. Meanwhile, Kuwait Petroleum International CEO Shafi Al-Ajmi says the Duqum refinery in Oman is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2023, with trial operations already at 81% completion and nearly all construction finished. Additionally, Kuwait Foreign Petroleum Exploration Company (KUFPEC) is in active negotiations to acquire Asia’s largest gas field, though the field has not yet been publicly identified.

Al Barrak manté que Kuwait i l'Aràbia Saudita tenen drets exclusius sobre Durra i ha instat l'Iran a delimitar les seves fronteres marítimes per resoldre el conflicte. article_content: A group of African penguins at Everland Amusement Park in Yongin, South Korea, thrilled visitors this December by donning festive holiday outfits. Dressed as tiny Santas and Christmas trees, the penguins, accompanied by their costumed caretakers, delighted crowds with daily parades that began at the start of the month. Visitors flocked to capture photos of the charming spectacle.  The event, originally planned to run until Christmas, concluded earlier because falling temperatures created risks for the penguins, which come from warmer habitats. 'Today was the last day,' said Everland spokesperson Kim In-chul. 'Since African penguins aren't used to the cold, we decided to end the parades to protect their health.'  Addressing media questions about whether the parade was cute or potentially harmful, Kim assured that the activity provided exercise for the penguins and was conducted in a safe, trusted setting with their usual keepers.

Els visitants s’afanyaven a fer fotos d’aquest espectacle encantador.  L’esdeveniment, previst inicialment fins a Nadal, es va acabar abans a causa de la baixada de les temperatures, que suposa un risc per als pingüins, ja que provenen de climes més càlids. “Avui ha estat l’últim dia”, va explicar el portaveu d’Everland, Kim In-chul. “Com que els pingüins africans no estan acostumats al fred, vam decidir posar fi a les desfilades per protegir la seva salut”.  En resposta a preguntes dels mitjans sobre si la desfilada era una activitat tendra o perjudicial, Kim va afirmar que aquests passeigs són exercici pels pingüins i es fan sempre en un entorn segur amb els seus cuidadors habituals.

article_content: The recent passing of professional ice hockey player Adam Johnson, who suffered a fatal neck injury during a game, has reignited debates about player safety in the sport. Johnson, part of the Nottingham Panthers, died after being struck in the neck by a skate during a match in Sheffield, UK. His team described the event as a highly unusual accident. Johnson, a 29-year-old from Minnesota, was new to the Panthers following two seasons with the NHL’s Pittsburgh Penguins. Although deaths from on-ice incidents are uncommon, similar tragedies have happened before. For example, high school player Teddy Balkind in Connecticut lost his life in 2022 from a skate-related neck injury, while NHL players Clint Malarchuk and Richard Zednick both survived comparable incidents that threatened their lives. According to Brock University’s Professor Nicole Chimera, skate blades pose a distinctive and serious risk in ice hockey, creating dangers not typically found in other contact sports like football or rugby. Some prior injuries have led to calls for making neck protection compulsory. After a player sustained a throat injury in Woodstock, the Ontario Hockey Association began requiring neck guards for all its players back in 2010. However, major leagues such as the NHL still do not enforce this rule. Following Johnson’s death, the English Ice Hockey Association (EIHA) announced that starting in 2024, neck guards will be required for all on-ice activities. Previously, adult players in the UK could play without them. Yet, the Elite League where Johnson played hasn't implemented such changes, and some members of the hockey community view neck guards as childish or unnecessary. Abbie Culshaw, a Great Britain international player, expressed to BBC Newsbeat that wearing a neck guard is seen as immature among some players, who often mock or disrespect those who wear them. She hopes recent events will change these perceptions. Serious injuries in ice hockey aren’t limited to skate blades—spinal cord and brain injuries are also possible, sometimes with dire consequences. A 2020 US study found that hockey players have a higher rate of cervical spine injuries compared to football, with most of these occurring during competitive play due to the sport’s high speed and aggressive style. The study also notes that as players become bigger and faster, injury risks might increase. Despite these dangers, hockey’s overall injury rate remains lower than in other popular sports like football, basketball, or soccer, according to 2022 statistics from the US National Safety Council. Professor Chimera points out that while sports provide valuable physical and social benefits, it is crucial to acknowledge and address the inherent risks. She advocates for continued consideration of rule changes and innovations to better protect athletes.

Defensa seguir revisant les normes i innovar per protegir millor els atletes.

article_content: Vivienne Westwood’s Red Label Autumn/Winter 2014 show blended fashion with protest. Her stance on fracking was highlighted by the statement ‘Fracking We Need to Talk’ printed on invitations, making her environmental concerns clear to all attendees. Celebrities like Jessie J, Eliza Doolittle, and Paloma Faith sat together in the front row, embracing the show’s bold spirit. Inspired by privileged women, the collection featured triangle print tights, oversized Amish hats, classic tartan, and structured tailoring. Playful details included bustles on mini skirts and cardigans worn alone. Pearls and faux fur accessories completed the elevated and ladylike aesthetic. Despite the privileged theme, Westwood stressed that her muse is socially aware and engaged with global issues. To further raise awareness on fracking, she invited guests to a 'Frack Future Carnival Rally' scheduled for March 19 at London’s Knightsbridge station. Elsewhere at the fashion week, Christopher Kane debuted his AW14 collection, noted for striking neons, shiny patents, and floral lace. Hair stylist Guido Paolo chose soft, undone hair to keep the focus on the clothes, while makeup artist Lucia Pieroni delivered a radiant look with strong brows and luminous skin, using pink hues for a modern and fresh finish.

article_content:
Rebecca Kalam, a former firearms officer with West Midlands Police, has been awarded £30,000 after an employment tribunal determined she suffered from harassment, sex discrimination, and victimization at work. Kalam’s lawsuit detailed inappropriate treatment, including being forced to strip down to her underwear during a training exercise and enduring sexist comments from male colleagues. She also noted that she was denied proper personal protective equipment and was pressured into a photoshoot for the firearms unit while pregnant. Previously, she was awarded an additional £3,000 for injuries resulting from unsuitable PPE.

The tribunal, overseen by Judge Christopher Camp, found that these incidents caused Kalam significant psychological harm, ultimately leading to her medical retirement in July 2023. Kalam spoke publicly about feeling validated by the ruling but expressed disappointment that such treatment is not an isolated incident within the force, citing a lack of substantial cultural improvement for female officers.

West Midlands Police responded by indicating they are reviewing the tribunal's findings, and Deputy Chief Constable Scott Green apologized for not addressing these serious concerns sooner. Green stated the force has worked to improve conditions for women in recent years, implementing better uniforms and equipment for female officers, while promising continued efforts to promote respect and equality.

Colleagues, such as former superintendent Karen Geddes, recognized both Kalam’s professionalism and the ongoing gender imbalance in specialized units. Additional claims by Kalam regarding future loss of earnings and pensions are scheduled to be decided in January.

article_content: Slovakia has accused Russia of interfering in its recent parliamentary election and has summoned a Russian embassy official in response. This action follows remarks by Russia's foreign intelligence chief, Sergei Naryshkin, who claimed the US was meddling in Slovak affairs and described the centrist Progressive Slovakia party as 'US proxies.' In Saturday's vote, the populist Smer-SD party led by former Prime Minister Robert Fico received 23 percent, defeating Progressive Slovakia, which garnered 18 percent. In a statement, Slovakia's foreign ministry condemned what it described as 'deliberately disseminated misinformation' by Russia, calling it unacceptable interference in Slovakia's electoral process. The ministry demanded that Moscow cease disinformation efforts targeting Slovakia and lodged a strong protest against the Russian intelligence chief's remarks, emphasizing that these statements undermined the integrity of Slovakia's free and democratic elections. In response, Moscow denied the accusations. The Russian embassy in Bratislava stated, as quoted by Russian news agencies, 'Unlike some of Slovakia's current allies, we do not interfere in the domestic affairs of other countries and we do not engage in regime change.'
